attrs: doc = " A reaped child means its pid is free for the OS to reassign, so the exit"
doc = " callback has to fire — a host still holding that pid would aim its"
doc = " shutdown kill at whatever inherits the number next."
tests.name: acp::agent_process::tests::exit_callback_fires_once_the_child_is_reaped

attrs: doc = " Regression for the select race in `connect_to`: the protocol side may"
doc = " finish before the child-monitor future receives its first poll. The"
doc = " monitor must already own a `ChildGuard`, otherwise dropping that"
doc = " unpolled future bypasses kill/reap and never fires `on_exit`."
tests.name: acp::agent_process::tests::dropping_an_unpolled_child_monitor_still_reaps_and_reports_exit

attrs: doc = " Dropping the guard kills the tree but does not wait, so the exit is not"
doc = " observed yet — and must not be reported yet. It has to be reported once"
doc = " the child actually dies, which only works because `drop` keeps owning the"
doc = " child instead of letting Tokio's orphan queue reap it out of sight."
doc = " A current-thread runtime makes the ordering exact: the detached reaper"
doc = " cannot run during the synchronous assertion right after `drop`."
tests.name: acp::agent_process::tests::dropping_the_guard_reports_the_exit_only_once_the_child_is_reaped

attrs: doc = " The case that makes the whole design necessary: a child that ignores the"
doc = " kill signal is STILL RUNNING after `drop`. Its pid must stay published so"
doc = " a host's shutdown backstop still sweeps it — reporting an exit here would"
doc = " disarm that backstop and leave a real orphan behind."
tests.name: acp::agent_process::tests::a_child_that_survives_the_kill_keeps_its_pid_published

attrs: doc = " The detour is a rescue for exactly one combination. Widening it would"
doc = " put a cmd.exe in front of agents that do not need one; narrowing it"
doc = " puts the agent back in `C:\\Windows`."
tests.name: acp::agent_process::tests::pushd_is_reserved_for_a_unc_workspace_behind_a_batch_launcher

attrs: doc = " Rust resolves a bare program name against PATH and never against the"
doc = " child's cwd. cmd.exe searches the current directory FIRST — which"
doc = " `pushd` has just pointed at the workspace — so handing it a relative"
doc = " launcher would let a `hermes.cmd` committed to the repo run instead of"
doc = " the trusted one on PATH. Those launches keep the direct spawn."
tests.name: acp::agent_process::tests::a_relative_launcher_never_takes_the_detour

attrs: doc = " `pushd` is a cmd built-in, so cmd parses this argument itself: the two"
doc = " spellings it cannot resolve have to be gone before it ever sees them,"
doc = " or `&&` takes the whole agent launch down with the failed `pushd`."
tests.name: acp::agent_process::tests::pushd_cwd_is_spelled_the_only_way_cmd_can_resolve_it

attrs: doc = " The whole contract, against the real runtime over an in-memory pipe:"
doc = " codeg creates the session UNTYPED (as `send_new_session_capturing_models`"
doc = " does), attaches afterwards, and still receives the update the agent sent"
doc = " BEFORE its `session/new` response — parked by the runtime because it"
doc = " carries a `sessionId`, and replayed into the router the moment it is"
doc = " added. That replay is what a `session/load` history drain and the"
doc = " `available_commands_update` agents send right after `session/new` depend"
doc = " on. A frame for another session must not leak in."
tests.name: acp::agent_session::tests::an_attached_session_receives_updates_the_agent_sent_before_the_response

attrs: doc = " One test, not six: the slot is process-global, and cargo runs tests on"
doc = " parallel threads — separate cases would fight over it."
doc = " The invariant under test is \"one sign-in at a time\", and the reason it"
doc = " needs a state machine rather than an `Option` is that both slow stretches"
doc = " happen outside the lock. A slow older `start` reaching the install point"
doc = " late must reap ITSELF rather than kill the link already on screen, and a"
doc = " `start` arriving mid-completion must be refused rather than put a second"
doc = " agent on the same credential file."
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::the_slot_admits_exactly_one_sign_in

attrs: doc = " The protocol requires the check (\"Clients MUST NOT call `logout` unless"
doc = " this is advertised\"), and without it an Antigravity too old to sign out"
doc = " answers `-32601` instead of saying so."
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::reads_the_logout_capability_out_of_the_handshake

attrs: doc = " The prompt shares a file descriptor with the JSON-RPC stream, so a frame"
doc = " can be spliced onto the same line. Both halves must still be recovered."
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::finds_the_url_when_a_json_frame_shares_the_line

attrs: doc = " The regression that made \"Get sign-in link\" spin for the full 90s and"
doc = " then claim the agent produced no link: 1.1.1 moved the prompt from"
doc = " stdout to stderr, and only stdout was scanned. Both PUMPS are driven"
doc = " here, not just the sink — the sink was never the broken part."
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::either_pump_delivers_the_sign_in_link

attrs: doc = " Two pumps, one channel: whoever matches first wins and the other's offer"
doc = " is inert. Without this a build that printed the prompt to BOTH streams"
doc = " would panic or lose the link on the second send."
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::the_first_stream_to_see_the_link_wins

attrs: doc = " `start_claimed` reads a closed channel as `StartSignal::Gone`, so the"
doc = " sink must not survive its pumps — a clone parked anywhere else would"
doc = " turn a dead child into a silent 90s wait."
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::dropping_both_pumps_closes_the_channel

attrs: doc = " The prompt line is the last thing on stderr when the URL scan misses, so"
doc = " an unfiltered hint would append a truncated consent URL to \"no link was"
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::the_stderr_hint_never_quotes_the_sign_in_link

attrs: doc = " The whole SSRF surface: whatever the user pastes, the request must go to"
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::the_request_target_ignores_the_pasted_host

attrs: doc = " A userinfo trick (`127.0.0.1:80@host`) makes the real host the part after"
doc = " the `@`, so the port must be digits and nothing else."
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::rejects_a_userinfo_disguised_authority

attrs: doc = " A fragment is not part of the query; letting it through would append"
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::drops_a_url_fragment

attrs: doc = " The paste is checked before the attempt is spent, so these are the"
doc = " failures a user can fix by pasting again — no second trip through"
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::rejects_only_what_it_can_decide_without_the_agent

attrs: doc = " The agent's message is rendered in the panel, so it goes through the"
doc = " same redaction every other agent diagnostic does."
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::redacts_a_credential_echoed_back_in_an_error

attrs: doc = " On macOS the default backend is the keychain, so the file path would name"
doc = " something that never gets written."
tests.name: acp::antigravity_login::tests::no_credential_path_when_the_keychain_owns_it

attrs: doc = " FORK layout regression. A fork copies the parent transcript (records keep"
doc = " their ORIGINAL, pre-fork timestamps) and writes fresh `queue-operation`"
doc = " metadata at the FILE HEAD stamped at fork time. That head record is"
doc = " post-epoch by timestamp but sits BEFORE the copied history by byte"
doc = " offset, so a boundary keyed on \"first record at/after epoch\" of ANY type"
doc = " would land at offset 0 and pull the entire copied history into the"
doc = " out-of-turn overlay — duplicating what the detail fetch already renders."
doc = " The boundary must skip non-conversation records and land on the first"
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::baseline_skips_fork_head_metadata_and_lands_on_the_first_new_turn

attrs: doc = " A new session's file can be discovered mid-flush of its FIRST record:"
doc = " no complete post-epoch line exists yet, and an EOF fallback would"
doc = " baseline past the fragment — its completing suffix then reads as"
doc = " unparseable garbage and the record (a launch ack here) is lost."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::adopt_with_trailing_partial_line_keeps_it_ahead_of_the_baseline

attrs: doc = " Production fork timing: the frontend fires its follow-up prompt the"
doc = " moment the fork resolves, so post-fork records land in the forked"
doc = " transcript BEFORE the polling watcher's next tick notices the session"
doc = " change. The re-arm epoch is therefore the instant the session id"
doc = " CHANGED (stamped by SessionStarted in session state), not the tick"
doc = " time — records written in that gap must still process, while the"
doc = " fork-copied history (original, pre-fork timestamps) stays skipped."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::post_fork_records_written_before_the_watcher_notices_still_process

attrs: doc = " `settled_ids` must survive a fork//re-resume re-arm: a post-fork"
doc = " `SendMessage(to: <id>)` resumes a sub-agent that settled BEFORE the"
doc = " fork, and missing the re-arm leaves outstanding at 0 — closing the"
doc = " tab could then kill the resumed background work."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::settled_ids_survive_rearm_so_post_fork_resume_rearms

attrs: doc = " `/clear` keeps the ACP session id but writes a NEW sibling jsonl."
doc = " The watcher must leave the frozen file and tail the successor so"
doc = " post-clear out-of-turn records (and the reopen reader, via the"
doc = " pending transcript id) are not stranded on a file nobody writes to."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::clear_rollover_adopts_the_new_transcript_while_acp_id_stays

attrs: doc = " Every conversation opened on one folder shares a project directory, so"
doc = " a `/clear` successor written by a DIFFERENT session sits right next to"
doc = " ours and looks identical on disk: fresh uuid, `/clear` head, starting"
doc = " when our own file happens to have gone quiet. Adopting it would tail a"
doc = " stranger's transcript and re-point this row's `external_id` at a"
doc = " session another row owns. The only thing that separates the two cases"
doc = " is whether WE asked for the clear."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::clear_rollover_ignores_a_sibling_session_we_did_not_clear

attrs: doc = " One connection outlives a fork, and the watcher learns of the session"
doc = " switch up to a poll late — so at re-arm time an unconsumed `/clear`"
doc = " may belong to either side of it. The session's own change instant is"
doc = " what separates them: a `/clear` typed into the new session before the"
doc = " watcher noticed the switch still has a successor to adopt."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::clear_rollover_expectation_survives_a_rearm_it_postdates

attrs: doc = " The successor's `/clear` record and the predecessor's last record are"
doc = " written by one process milliseconds apart, and the CLI's timestamps are"
doc = " not ordered across the two files (measured on 2.1.270: the successor's"
doc = " caveat record is stamped 6ms BEFORE the command record that follows"
doc = " it). A detector that demands `successor >= predecessor` to the"
doc = " millisecond therefore drops real rollovers — and drops them for good,"
doc = " since every later tick re-compares the same two files."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::clear_rollover_tolerates_a_successor_stamped_just_before_us

attrs: doc = " A `_session/steering` injection reaches the agent outside"
doc = " `session/prompt`, but the CLI still writes it to the transcript as a"
doc = " user record — which starts a new turn as far as `group_into_turns` is"
doc = " concerned. Since claude-agent-acp #958 the owning prompt stays in"
doc = " flight across the steered work, so every update of that turn is"
doc = " already streaming over the wire; surfacing it as overlay activity too"
doc = " double-renders it and shuffles the transcript as the upserts land"
doc = " (observed live before the `Steer` arm fingerprinted its text)."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::steered_message_classifies_foreground_like_a_prompt

attrs: doc = " A slash command sent from codeg writes MORE than its own record: the"
doc = " STRING instruction Claude Code injects for the model — and only then the"
doc = " reply. Those side records are user records carrying text, so"
doc = " `turn_initiator_text` reads them as initiators and the ledger, already"
doc = " emptied by the command itself, has nothing to match them against. That"
doc = " flipped the watcher to Background mid-turn and the wire-rendered reply"
doc = " came back as an overlay copy — the reported `/goal` bug, where the whole"
doc = " answer rendered twice while streaming."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_commands_own_side_records_do_not_reopen_the_turn_as_background

attrs: doc = " The command record is the only one the ledger can match, and its"
doc = " initiator text is REBUILT from command tags — `slash_command_display`"
doc = " joins the name and the trimmed args with a single space, whatever the"
doc = " sender typed. The composer inserts a space after a command badge, so a"
doc = " sender who types their own lands two, and the rebuilt text no longer"
doc = " starts with the fingerprint. That miss leaves the submission window"
doc = " unarmed and every following side record classifies out-of-turn, which"
doc = " is the same duplicated `/goal` turn as above by a different route."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_command_matches_the_ledger_despite_a_rebuilt_separator

attrs: doc = " The window is scoped by SUBMISSION, not by time: an autonomous prompt"
doc = " that lands in the same interval — after the ledger match, before the"
doc = " model's first record — carries a different `promptId` and must still"
doc = " open its episode. Without this the fix would trade a recoverable"
doc = " duplicate for a turn missing from the live view."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_foreign_submission_inside_the_window_still_surfaces

attrs: doc = " The other initiator the window may not swallow: an async sub-agent's"
doc = " `<task-notification>`. It settles on its own schedule and IS stamped with"
doc = " the in-flight submission's `promptId`, so only the explicit exemption"
doc = " keeps it out-of-turn. Its follow-up has no other live rendering path —"
doc = " the wire never carries it — so suppressing it would lose the turn until"
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_task_notification_inside_the_window_still_opens_an_episode

attrs: doc = " The window must never outlive the turn that opened it. Both resets are"
doc = " asserted directly, because the `promptId` scoping makes their effect"
doc = " invisible from the outside in all but contrived transcripts: the model's"
doc = " first record closes it, and — for a turn that ends without ever writing"
doc = " one — any non-prompting tick does. The reset is level-triggered on"
doc = " purpose: an EDGE can be missed entirely (a whole turn can start and"
doc = " finish between two polls, and a tick's own lines re-arm the window AFTER"
doc = " the edge was handled), which would strand it set forever."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::submission_window_is_closed_by_the_reply_and_by_any_idle_tick

attrs: doc = " The Critical arm-gap regression: a brand-new session's file (and its"
doc = " first prompt + launch ack) can exist BEFORE the watcher's first"
doc = " successful discovery — SessionStarted lags file creation by seconds."
doc = " Those records must still be accounted and ledger-consumed; blindly"
doc = " baselining at EOF dropped them (outstanding never armed, and the"
doc = " unconsumed fingerprint could swallow a later same-text cron refire)."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::pre_discovery_records_are_accounted_and_ledger_consumed

attrs: doc = " A background shell re-observed via a repeat `BashOutput`-style poll"
doc = " (the identical `backgroundTaskId` shape appearing again) must not"
doc = " reset its `started_at` — a blind `insert` would restart the max-age"
doc = " clock on every poll, letting an actively-polled-but-actually-finished"
doc = " shell pin the connection alive indefinitely. `entry().or_insert_with()`"
doc = " only sets `started_at` on the FIRST observation."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::repeat_shell_observation_does_not_reset_started_at

attrs: doc = " follow-up for an id THIS turn launched, arriving while the connection"
doc = " is still `Prompting` (claude-agent-acp v0.59.0's #870 holds the turn"
doc = " open for its own spawned sub-agents), is already rendering on the"
doc = " wire — so the OVERLAY turn for it must be suppressed. The `settled`"
doc = " entry, by contrast, MUST still flow: the frontend needs it to flip the"
doc = " launch card (which it does in-memory, so it can't double-render), and it"
doc = " carries the launching `tool_use_id` + `<result>` for exactly that."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::held_turn_followup_for_this_turns_launched_agent_is_suppressed

attrs: doc = " The exact real-world race that broke a naive \"is_prompting right now\""
doc = " check: the turn settles (Prompting→Connected) BEFORE the watcher's own"
doc = " tick gets around to reading the follow-up's tail content — the content"
doc = " was genuinely wire-rendered a beat earlier, while still `Prompting`,"
doc = " but this tick observes `is_prompting == false`. There is no grace"
doc = " window anymore: `current_turn_launched_ids` simply isn't cleared until"
doc = " the NEXT turn starts (or an abnormal ending releases it early), so"
doc = " OVERLAY suppression tolerates an arbitrarily-delayed read — several idle"
doc = " ticks pass with no new content before the follow-up finally lands, and"
doc = " the overlay turn must still be suppressed. The `settled` entry still"
doc = " flows regardless (it flips the launch card)."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::held_turn_followup_still_suppressed_when_settlement_races_ahead_of_the_read

attrs: doc = " A turn that ends ABNORMALLY (cancelled, refused, etc — the same"
doc = " uniformly elsewhere) must release its launched ids immediately: that"
doc = " content never reached the wire (the ACP call was torn down before the"
doc = " real background work settled), so unlike a normal completion there is"
doc = " no live view left for a later notification to duplicate — the overlay"
doc = " is correctly the only place left to render it, and must not wait for"
doc = " the next turn to start."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::abnormal_turn_ending_releases_launched_ids_immediately

attrs: doc = " A background shell launched while `Prompting` must NOT enter"
doc = " `current_turn_launched_ids`: #870 never holds a turn open for a shell,"
doc = " so a shell's owning turn ends via an ordinary `end_turn` while the"
doc = " shell keeps running. If the shell's id were suppression-eligible, its"
doc = " eventual completion would be silently swallowed for the shell's entire"
doc = " realistic runtime — content that was never on the wire to begin with."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::background_shell_launched_while_prompting_is_never_suppression_eligible

attrs: doc = " A `SendMessage`-resumed sub-agent must be suppression-eligible again if"
doc = " the RESUMING turn is itself held open by #870 for it — mirroring the"
doc = " launch-time insert. Without this, a resume-then-hold reproduces the"
doc = " same double-render the original launch-time tracking exists to"
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::resumed_agent_held_by_the_resuming_turn_is_suppressed

attrs: doc = " A cron//loop autonomous turn has no originating task id at all (its"
doc = " initiator is plain injected text, not a `<task-notification>`), so it"
doc = " must never be caught by the held-turn suppression filter — even if,"
doc = " coincidentally, some OTHER turn happens to be `Prompting` when it"
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::cron_followup_is_never_suppressed_even_while_prompting

attrs: doc = " A `<task-notification>` can name a task id that was launched (and"
doc = " settled) by a PAST, already-ended turn — not the turn currently"
doc = " `Prompting`. Only ids launched by the CURRENTLY active turn are"
doc = " rising edge), so this must render normally."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::notification_for_a_past_turns_task_is_not_suppressed_by_a_new_turn

attrs: doc = " The dominant real-world shell path: a background shell is launched, the"
doc = " agent awaits it with `TaskOutput{block:true}`, and the result's"
doc = " `task.status` goes terminal — with NO `<task-notification>` ever"
doc = " written. That collection must clear the outstanding count (the bug:"
doc = " only `<task-notification>` used to settle, so these stranded for the"
doc = " full keep-alive max-age). A non-terminal poll must NOT clear it."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::taskoutput_terminal_status_settles_background_shell

attrs: doc = " An explicit `TaskStop` settles the task immediately — the process is"
doc = " gone and no completion notification will follow."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::taskstop_settles_background_task

attrs: doc = " Sent with nothing typed, a page has no text block to fingerprint. Its"
doc = " own turn then classified as out-of-turn, and the overlay drew the"
doc = " prompt and the reply a second time under the live copy."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_page_sent_with_nothing_typed_stays_a_foreground_turn

attrs: doc = " The whole point of reading titles here: Claude Code's background"
doc = " summarizer writes `ai-title` AFTER the turn that triggered it has"
doc = " ended, and the ACP adapter only reads the name back at turn-end — so on"
doc = " a short session nothing ever publishes it. That tail is pure metadata:"
doc = " no turns, no settlements, no accounting change, so `tick` returns"
doc = " `None`. The title must still come out, which is why `run_watch` takes"
doc = " it independently of the activity event."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_title_only_tail_yields_no_activity_event_but_still_surfaces_the_title

attrs: doc = " Once taken, the same name must not be re-queued on every later tick —"
doc = " each publish walks the state write lock and a DB write."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::an_unchanged_title_is_queued_once

attrs: doc = " `customTitle ?? aiTitle` — Claude Code's own precedence, and the one"
doc = " `parsers::claude` applies over the whole file. A generated title"
doc = " arriving after the user named the session must not take the name back."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_user_set_title_outranks_a_later_generated_one

attrs: doc = " Claude Code writes an empty `aiTitle` for trivial sessions. Publishing"
doc = " it would rename the conversation to nothing."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_blank_title_record_is_never_queued

attrs: doc = " History before the arm baseline renders through the ordinary detail"
doc = " fetch, which resolves the title from the whole file. Re-publishing it"
doc = " from here would rename the conversation on every reconnect."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_title_in_pre_baseline_history_is_not_queued

attrs: doc = " `customTitle ?? aiTitle` is a WHOLE-FILE rule, but the two records are"
doc = " appended independently — `/rename` writes a lone `custom-title`, the"
doc = " summarizer a lone `ai-title`. A session renamed BEFORE this watch armed"
doc = " keeps its `custom-title` in the skipped history, so resolving over the"
doc = " tail alone would let the very next `ai-title` (the CLI re-emits it"
doc = " constantly) publish over the user's own name. The arm seeds the slots"
doc = " from history to close that."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_pre_baseline_user_title_outranks_a_generated_one_read_later

attrs: doc = " The CLI re-emits the SAME `ai-title` record throughout a session (228"
doc = " identical copies in one observed transcript). On a resumed session the"
doc = " first one past the baseline is a repeat of what history — and therefore"
doc = " the detail fetch, and therefore the row — already holds, so seeding must"
doc = " swallow it rather than spend a lifecycle write on a no-op."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::a_generated_title_already_in_history_is_not_republished

attrs: doc = " A brand-new session baselines at offset 0 (its file is created after the"
doc = " spawn epoch), so there is no history to seed and the seed must be a"
doc = " no-op — the path this PR actually targets stays untouched."
tests.name: acp::background_watch::tests::seeding_is_a_noop_for_a_fresh_session_whose_whole_file_is_ours

attrs: doc = " The common case: nothing at the destination, so the whole tree moves in"
doc = " one rename and the old root is gone afterwards."
tests.name: acp::binary_cache::tests::migrate_root_renames_when_the_destination_is_empty

attrs: doc = " A destination that already has content cannot be renamed onto, so the"
doc = " merge path runs. Everything must still end up under the new root, and"
doc = " the legacy root must still disappear — leaving it would make it a second"
doc = " live root, which is how an uninstall gets undone by a read-through."
tests.name: acp::binary_cache::tests::migrate_root_merges_into_an_existing_destination

attrs: doc = " A symlink used to be \"copied\" by skipping it and returning `Ok`, after"
doc = " which the caller deleted the source. A `uv` tool venv is exactly that"
doc = " shape — `bin/` is links — so the agent it migrated arrived missing the"
doc = " file it launches through, and the original was already gone."
tests.name: acp::binary_cache::tests::copy_tree_recreates_a_symlink_instead_of_dropping_it

attrs: doc = " A successful merge must leave no staging directory behind, or every"
tests.name: acp::binary_cache::tests::migrate_root_leaves_no_staging_directory_behind

attrs: doc = " Staging must NOT live under `.trash/`, because `sweep_trash` deletes"
doc = " every child of that directory unconditionally — including, from a peer"
doc = " codeg, a copy this one is still assembling."
tests.name: acp::binary_cache::tests::staging_is_out_of_the_trash_sweep

attrs: doc = " A staging directory abandoned by a process that is gone is reclaimed;"
doc = " one whose owner is still alive is left alone, because a peer codeg may"
doc = " be copying into it right now."
tests.name: acp::binary_cache::tests::dead_owners_staging_is_reclaimed_and_a_live_owner_is_not

attrs: doc = " The uninstall fix in one line: removal is parameterized by ROOT, so the"
doc = " legacy root gets the same treatment — including the rename-aside — as"
doc = " the current one. Clearing only the current root would let"
doc = " `installed_binary_path`'s legacy fallback resurrect the agent the user"
doc = " just removed, while the call still reported success."
tests.name: acp::binary_cache::tests::clear_agent_dir_in_clears_whichever_root_it_is_given

attrs: doc = " When both roots hold the same agent the destination wins and the stale"
doc = " copy is dropped, rather than the migration silently preferring the old"
tests.name: acp::binary_cache::tests::migrate_root_keeps_the_destination_copy_on_a_collision

attrs: doc = " A refusal has to name the tab and carry a slug the agent can branch on"
doc = " — the prose is for the user, the slug is for the model."
tests.name: acp::browser_tools::tests::a_refusal_names_the_tab_and_the_button_that_lifts_it

attrs: doc = " `snapshot` and `error` are exclusive, and the absent one is absent from"
doc = " the wire rather than present-and-null: the companion branches on which"
tests.name: acp::browser_tools::tests::the_wire_carries_exactly_one_of_the_page_and_the_refusal

attrs: doc = " An empty listing is not an error, and the two kinds of empty are told"
tests.name: acp::browser_tools::tests::a_runtime_without_tabs_says_so_rather_than_looking_idle

attrs: doc = " The refusals an action tool can give each name the tab and the thing"
doc = " the agent (or the user) does next; `action` and `error` are exclusive."
tests.name: acp::browser_tools::tests::an_action_refusal_says_what_to_do_next

attrs: doc = " The console and screenshot refusals borrow the read's words — the"
doc = " console and the pixels are the page — and each carries exactly one of"
doc = " its payload and its error."
tests.name: acp::browser_tools::tests::console_and_capture_refusals_read_like_a_refused_read

attrs: doc = " The three tab tools share one answer shape: an open and a navigation"
doc = " describe the tab the way the listing does, a close has no tab left to"
doc = " describe, and a refusal carries the slug and no tab at all."
tests.name: acp::browser_tools::tests::a_tab_op_answers_with_the_tab_or_with_why_not

attrs: doc = " The refusals `browser_eval` can give are distinguishable, and the one"
doc = " the person caused says not to try again."
tests.name: acp::browser_tools::tests::an_eval_refusal_says_whether_asking_again_is_worth_anything

attrs: doc = " codex retires a model by flipping it to `hide` (keeping its `upgrade`"
doc = " migration stub), which turns an old removal into a ghost. Honouring the"
doc = " ghost would delete the stub from the table codex reads."
tests.name: acp::codex_model_catalog::tests::expand_keeps_hidden_officials_even_when_excluded

attrs: doc = " Nullability is per-key: codex answers `invalid type: null, expected"
doc = " string or map` for the non-optional enums and rejects the whole catalog,"
doc = " so a stray `null` (from a legacy override or an imported hand-written"
doc = " file) must be dropped rather than written."
tests.name: acp::codex_model_catalog::tests::expand_rejects_null_in_non_nullable_enums_but_allows_optional_ones

attrs: doc = " The compatibility template the editor writes must survive sanitization"
doc = " intact — it is the whole point of the \"third-party gateway\" preset."
tests.name: acp::codex_model_catalog::tests::expand_keeps_the_openai_compatible_override_bundle

attrs: doc = " A non-boolean in a boolean slot answers `invalid type: string …, expected"
doc = " a boolean` and takes the whole catalog down with it."
tests.name: acp::codex_model_catalog::tests::expand_drops_non_boolean_values_in_boolean_fields

attrs: doc = " A burst of withdrawals: `b` is already taken back when `a` leaves the"
doc = " screen, but its own watcher has not run yet. Promoting it would flash a"
doc = " dead card on every client and push it to chat channels, so the queue"
doc = " answers it `Cancelled` on the spot and shows `c` — whichever way `a`"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::permission_queue_never_promotes_a_card_already_withdrawn

attrs: doc = " A card's watcher never retires anything once the card has left the"
doc = " queue, even when the withdrawal is ready at the same moment — a plain"
doc = " `tokio::select!` would pick either arm at random, hence the repeats."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::a_settled_permission_is_never_treated_as_withdrawn

attrs: doc = " The withdrawal path end to end, over the real runtime: the agent raises"
doc = " `session/request_permission` and takes it back with `$/cancel_request`,"
doc = " exactly as claude-agent-acp does when the tool call's signal aborts. It"
doc = " must get its answer (`Cancelled`) without anyone touching the card, and"
doc = " the card the client showed must be retracted."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::an_agent_withdrawing_a_permission_request_retires_its_card

attrs: doc = " codex abandons a `request_user_input` it stops waiting for — its"
doc = " `autoResolutionMs` expired, or the turn was interrupted — with"
doc = " `$/cancel_request`. The question card must go at once (it used to wait"
doc = " on a timer guessed from `autoResolutionMs`), and codex still gets a"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::codex_withdrawing_a_question_elicitation_retires_the_card

attrs: doc = " Typed side channel only: display-string recovery must not mint RouteSpecific."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::bootstrap_outcome_typed_only_no_substring_fallback

attrs: doc = " with the classified timeout map (design 2026-07-30)."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::session_request_meta_grok_codeg_mcp_timeouts_on_new_load_resume

attrs: doc = " Complete base argv (as production builds before `AcpAgent::from_args`)"
doc = " must receive structured route insertion via `apply_process_route` only:"
doc = " Grok `--no-subagents` before `agent stdio`, CodeBuddy deny union before"
doc = " `--acp`. Second application is a no-op (idempotent)."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::apply_process_route_on_complete_argv_is_ordered_and_idempotent

attrs: doc = " Native CodeBuddy must be a strict no-op on the complete argv, including"
doc = " pre-seeded `--disallowedTools` in any supported position."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::native_codebuddy_preserves_preseeded_disallowed_tools

attrs: doc = " Fork must re-assert the same Claude Codeg Agent/Task deny list as"
doc = " new/load/resume (via `session_request_meta` / deep merge). Native is"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::claude_fork_meta_reasserts_codeg_agent_task_deny

attrs: doc = " Mirrors the connection-loop prompt path: ledger/UI use original user"
doc = " blocks; only the wire `ContentBlock` list receives `append_once`."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::wire_prompt_gets_context_user_message_does_not

attrs: doc = " A changed title emits; the SAME title arriving again does not. CodeBuddy"
doc = " (`sendPendingTitleUpdate`) resends its 80-code-unit fallback after every"
doc = " completed prompt with no last-sent guard of its own, and that string"
doc = " differs from the 100-char title our own parser derives from the same"
doc = " first message — so without this skip the sidebar name would flip on"
doc = " every turn (live write, then session-file parse, repeat)."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::session_info_title_emits_once_and_skips_an_identical_repeat

attrs: doc = " A title published before the first prompt binds the row has nowhere to"
doc = " land, so it is dropped — and deliberately NOT remembered, so the resend"
doc = " that follows `ConversationLinked` is still accepted. Guards the"
doc = " `conversation_id.is_some()` half of the skip: a stale cache here would"
doc = " leave the row \"Untitled\" for the rest of the connection."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::session_info_title_dropped_while_unbound_is_accepted_after_link

attrs: doc = " Goal-only / metadata-only `session_info_update`s (the common case for"
doc = " codex `/goal` transitions) carry no title and must not queue the"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::session_info_without_a_title_emits_no_native_title

attrs: doc = " claude-agent-acp 0.74.0's mid-session sign-out record, verbatim off the"
doc = " category, severity, title, details, actions — `kind`/`recoveryPolicy`"
doc = " stay agent-internal). Two things in it changed with that release and"
doc = " * the CLI's own \"… Please run /login\" prose moved OUT of `title` into"
doc = "   `details`, leaving the policy's client-neutral fallback as the title —"
doc = "   so the strip reads as a heading with the TUI advice behind its"
doc = "   expander, not the other way round;"
doc = " * the record may carry a `reason` refinement. codeg never produces one"
doc = "   (it is `--hide-claude-auth`-only; see the registry entry), and the"
doc = "   parser reads fields individually, so an unknown key must simply ride"
doc = "   through instead of failing the record."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::parse_session_failure_record_reads_claude_074_sign_out

attrs: doc = " codex gets `terminal_output_delta` (its completion frames stop repeating"
doc = " the output the bridge already streamed); claude must NOT — there the"
doc = " same key moves shell output onto a `_meta` channel codeg does not"
doc = " bridge. Neither may get the other spelling: it would move codex's shell"
doc = " output onto `terminal_output`, a key its bridge does not read."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::client_capabilities_advertise_terminal_output_delta_to_codex_only

attrs: doc = " After a codex fork, the sibling row codeg creates to keep the pre-fork"
doc = " history points at the PARENT thread — whose writer the forking process"
doc = " still holds, because `session/fork` only unsubscribes the child. Opening"
doc = " it must stop with a banner, never fall through to `session/new`: that"
doc = " rebinds the row to a fresh empty session and destroys the only pointer to"
doc = " the history the row exists for. The lock clears when the fork is closed."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::classify_load_failure_names_a_session_another_client_holds

attrs: doc = " A var the method READS but the panel did not store must still be cleared."
doc = " This is the whole Agent Platform choice: the method takes either a"
doc = " `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or a project + location, and the server suppresses the"
doc = " pair whenever the key is set — so the panel deletes `GOOGLE_API_KEY`"
doc = " from the row when the field is left empty. A policy that only asked"
doc = " \"does this method read the var\" left the slot open, and an inherited key"
doc = " walked into it and outranked the project the user typed."
doc = " Note the shape this needs: the earlier cases all put the var IN `merged`"
doc = " first, which is the one arrangement that cannot catch this — the bug was"
doc = " about the var being absent."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::antigravity_env_policy_clears_a_kept_var_the_panel_left_empty

attrs: doc = " The sign-out asks this instead of reading the stored row, because the"
doc = " row is not what the server infers from. Getting it wrong means aiming"
doc = " `logout` at a flavor that has nothing to clear — which it answers `{}`"
doc = " to, so the mistake would be reported to the user as a sign-out."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::antigravity_effective_auth_type_reads_the_file_the_server_reads

attrs: doc = " Clearing the project and location in the panel has to REACH the file."
doc = " The old signature could not say it: \"the panel does not manage this"
doc = " field\" and \"the panel manages it and the user emptied it\" both arrived"
doc = " as `None`, and the merge left the block alone for both. So the values"
doc = " written by an earlier save stayed in force forever — and for"
doc = " `oauth-business` that file is the ONLY place the project comes from, so"
doc = " the agent kept authenticating against a project the UI showed nowhere."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::antigravity_settings_gcp_fields_can_be_cleared_by_the_panel

attrs: doc = " Which fields count as the panel's is decided by the METHOD, so a"
doc = " hand-written block under a method that never renders those inputs is"
doc = " still none of codeg's business."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::antigravity_gcp_ownership_follows_the_recorded_method

attrs: doc = " A `GEMINI_HOME` that only codeg's OWN environment carries still names"
doc = " the directory the agent uses."
doc = " `merge_agent_env` lists the variables a launch SETS; anything absent is"
doc = " inherited, and relocating the tree from a container's environment"
doc = " (`GEMINI_HOME=/data/gemini` in the image, nothing in the per-agent row)"
doc = " is exactly that shape. Treating \"absent\" as \"unset\" sent codeg to"
doc = " `~/.gemini` — so on a Docker deployment it wrote `auth.type` into"
doc = " `/root/.gemini` while the agent read the relocated file, and the panel"
doc = " named a token path that was never written. The same three-state"
doc = " distinction `child_home_dir` makes for `HOME`, for the same reason."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::antigravity_settings_path_follows_a_gemini_home_codeg_only_inherits

attrs: doc = " `GEMINI_HOME=~/x` names `$HOME/x` to the server, so it has to name the"
doc = " Antigravity runs `os.path.expanduser` on the value"
doc = " (`acp_server/paths.py`). codeg built the path with a bare"
doc = " `PathBuf::from`, so it created a directory literally named `~` under its"
doc = " own working directory and wrote `auth.type` into THAT — leaving"
doc = " `session/new` failing with `Authentication required` no matter how many"
doc = " times the panel was saved."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::antigravity_settings_path_expands_a_tilde_home_the_way_the_server_does

attrs: doc = " Task 3 Step 1: watchdog cancel shares `stop_reason=cancelled` with user"
doc = " Stop but must never set `termination_source` / `provider_turn_id`, and"
doc = " must clear any stored fence id. Exercises"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::watchdog_cancel_does_not_set_user_stop_and_clears_provider_id

attrs: doc = " The five `_x.ai/session/setup` frames grok 1.0.40 emits BEFORE the"
doc = " session id exists, captured verbatim off `grok agent stdio` during"
doc = " `session/new`. Each carries `\"sessionId\": null`, which is what killed the"
doc = " connection in #794 — the runtime treats the present-but-null field as"
doc = " session-bound, and `sacp` 11 then failed to parse it into a `SessionId`."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::null_session_id_is_recognized_on_grok_setup_frames

attrs: doc = " The two shapes that must keep flowing: the LATER `_x.ai/session/setup`"
doc = " phases, which carry a real session id and belong to the session channel,"
doc = " and connection-level pushes that have no `sessionId` field at all"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::null_session_id_leaves_real_and_absent_session_ids_alone

attrs: doc = " A REQUEST with a null `sessionId` is parked by the runtime like any"
doc = " session-bound message, and nothing would ever answer it: the agent would"
doc = " block for the life of the connection. Over the real runtime, the guard"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::a_request_with_a_null_session_id_is_answered_not_parked

attrs: doc = " The exact `_x.ai/session_notification` envelope captured from grok 0.2.111"
doc = " the token delta and an `_meta.eventId`."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::map_grok_ext_notification_maps_auto_compact_completed

attrs: doc = " The same variant may arrive on the sibling `_x.ai/session/update` method."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::map_grok_ext_notification_handles_session_update_method

attrs: doc = " Without `notes` there is no sentence to show, so the fallback has to"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::map_grok_ext_notification_image_dropped_without_notes_still_names_the_subject

attrs: doc = " grok's validator rejects `image/svg+xml` outright (\"unsupported or"
doc = " unrecognised image format\") and the model then sees nothing at all. As a"
doc = " resource blob the same file lands in the session's assets, where the"
doc = " model can read the source — so an undecodable mime must NOT ride the"
doc = " native carriage, whichever producer built the block."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::normalize_grok_image_blocks_demotes_mimes_grok_cannot_decode

attrs: doc = " The allow-list is the boundary between the two carriages, so pin it:"
doc = " grok's own raster set in, everything else out."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::grok_decodes_image_mime_covers_groks_raster_set_only

attrs: doc = " A failed auto-compaction renders the shared compaction card in its"
doc = " failed state — where every other compaction outcome shows — not a"
doc = " session error under the composer."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::map_grok_ext_notification_auto_compact_failed_renders_failed_compaction_card

attrs: doc = " A DELAYED prior-turn `subagent_spawned` (its launch turn ended, its"
doc = " pending entry was cleared) must NOT steal the pairing slot a NEW turn's"
doc = " spawn queued: the `(description, subagent_type)` captured from the"
doc = " launch input has to match the notification's own fields."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::delayed_subagent_spawned_does_not_steal_a_new_turns_slot

attrs: doc = " Full background-subagent lifecycle over the stateful mapper: spawned"
doc = " pairs FIFO, progress lands as a meta-only ToolCallUpdate on the paired"
doc = " call, and finished settles over the BackgroundActivity channel with the"
doc = " launch call's id (so the frontend flips its marker card in-memory)."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::map_grok_subagent_notification_background_lifecycle

attrs: doc = " A BLOCKING spawn (call not yet settled when the child finishes) must NOT"
doc = " emit a settle — its own completion frame carries the output; a duplicate"
doc = " marker would double-render it. Non-grok agents never route at all."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::map_grok_subagent_notification_skips_blocking_and_other_agents

attrs: doc = " A traversal-shaped `child_session_id` must not reach the card: the"
doc = " frontend hands that value to `get_conversation`, which resolves a session"
doc = " directory by it, so the live path applies the same `is_safe_subagent_id`"
doc = " gate the history parser (`grok::subagent_stats`) does. The stamp still"
doc = " carries the subagent id — the run is identified, there is just no session"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::map_grok_subagent_notification_rejects_unsafe_child_session_id

attrs: doc = " The turn-loop consults this to keep a compaction-only `/compact` turn"
doc = " from being reclassified as `\"empty\"` (which re-surfaces a spurious error)."
doc = " It must count exactly the compaction outcomes that emit a card/error."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::grok_ext_notification_is_turn_output_marks_compaction_outcomes

attrs: doc = " Every severity the RFD defines has to survive the raw read, and an"
doc = " unknown one has to survive it TOO — grading happens in the consumer,"
doc = " which degrades an unrecognized level to `info` rather than dropping it."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::a_notice_is_read_at_every_severity

attrs: doc = " Frames captured byte-for-byte off the live adapters over stdio, with the"
doc = " * claude-agent-acp 0.81.0: a project `UserPromptSubmit` hook exiting 2"
doc = "   blocks the prompt before any model call (the turn reported 0 tokens),"
doc = "   and the SDK's `informational` frame arrives as this notice."
doc = "   `model` is not in the catalog, logged in with a dummy API key — the"
doc = "   fallback-metadata warning fires at turn start, then the 401 produces"
doc = "   the transport-fallback warning (a multi-line title, kept verbatim)."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::notices_captured_live_from_both_adapters_are_read_verbatim

attrs: doc = " `title` is required and non-empty per the RFD. Without it there is"
doc = " nothing to show, and a toast with an empty body is worse than silence."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::a_notice_without_a_usable_title_is_dropped

attrs: doc = " Claiming a dispatch before the typed pipeline is destructive, so both"
doc = " readers have to be exact about what they claim."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::the_session_readers_claim_only_their_own_frames

attrs: doc = " The whole point of the translation: claude's reserved `_meta` block is"
doc = " what the card's full label (counts, duration, trigger) is built from, so"
doc = " it has to arrive on the synthetic call untouched."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::a_claude_compaction_update_keeps_its_reserved_meta

attrs: doc = " codex sends no `_meta` at all (its legacy call carried none either), so"
doc = " the card must still be recognizable — recognition is by the"
doc = " `contextCompaction` key, not by anything inside it."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::a_codex_compaction_update_is_still_recognizable_without_meta

attrs: doc = " A failed compaction's reason is a SIBLING of `status` on the wire but a"
doc = " member of the card's payload, so it has to be folded in where the card"
doc = " looks — otherwise the divider says \"failed\" with no reason."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::a_failed_compaction_carries_its_error_into_the_card_payload

attrs: doc = " The retained summary is the one thing the legacy presentation could"
doc = " never carry. It rides `raw_output` — the streamed chunks APPEND — and"
doc = " every translated update claims that channel with the codeg marker the"
doc = " card expands on, because a bare `raw_output` is exactly what a legacy"
doc = " call fills with its metadata object."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::a_compaction_summary_is_carried_on_raw_output_and_claimed_by_the_marker

attrs: doc = " `session` reaches the two agents that built these, and NOBODY else."
doc = " Both members must serialize as OBJECTS: claude tests `typeof notices ==="
doc = " \"object\" && !== null && !Array.isArray`, and codex's compaction gate is"
doc = " `!= null` — so an empty struct serializing to `null`, or being skipped,"
doc = " would silently withhold the capability."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::the_session_capability_block_reaches_only_its_two_agents

attrs: doc = " The spawn frame is the only one carrying the task's identity, so every"
doc = " field of it has to survive the raw read — the merge downstream can only"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::async_task_spawn_frame_is_read_whole

attrs: doc = " Progress and state frames revise an announced task. They must NOT read as"
doc = " creates — `spawned` is what lets `apply_event` refuse to invent a row for"
doc = " an announcement codeg failed to read."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::async_task_progress_and_state_frames_are_not_creates

attrs: doc = " codex-acp 1.10.0's frames, verbatim off a live stdio session (`sleep 400`"
doc = " left running in a persistent shell, then stopped). codex fills in far"
doc = " less than claude — no `description`, `usage` or `outputFilePath`, and the"
doc = " task id EQUALS the tool call id — so the reader has to survive on the"
doc = " spawn frame's four fields alone, and `to_record`'s defaults must not"
doc = " invent anything the strip would then render."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::async_task_reader_handles_the_codex_spawn_and_stop_frames

attrs: doc = " The `_auth/status_update` payload codex-acp 1.9+ pushes, unchanged. The"
doc = " only contract that matters is that it DESERIALIZES — a strict struct here"
doc = " would make the typed handler fail on the first field OpenAI adds, and the"
doc = " runtime answers a failing handler by logging `Handler errored` and dropping"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::auth_status_update_deserializes_every_observed_kind

attrs: doc = " The interceptor sits in front of EVERY dispatch, so a false positive"
doc = " would silently swallow ordinary session updates."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::async_task_reader_claims_only_its_own_three_variants

attrs: doc = " The adapter drops a `usage` object missing any of its three counters"
doc = " rather than publishing a partial one; a half-read usage would render as"
doc = " a task that used 0 tokens."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::async_task_usage_is_all_or_nothing

attrs: doc = " The `session/load` replay drains a PAST session. Every grok ext outcome"
doc = " is skipped there: an alert would report a historical failure as if it"
doc = " were happening now, and a compaction card would linger in the live state"
doc = " as in-flight content (grok's transcript gets its cards from the history"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::grok_ext_notification_skipped_on_replay_covers_every_mapped_outcome

attrs: doc = " A failed compaction card travels with a coded `Error`, so the readers of"
doc = " the error stream (chat-channel bridges, `last_error`, the pet) still hear"
doc = " about it; a completed card, or any other event, gets none."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::compaction_failure_error_accompanies_only_a_failed_compaction_card

attrs: doc = " Grok's cumulative token count rides the OUTER `params._meta` of ordinary"
doc = " updates — the only live context signal it offers, and one the typed"
doc = " pipeline drops. The peek must read it there, hold its fire while the"
doc = " number repeats, and stay silent without a window to divide by."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::grok_live_usage_step_reads_the_outer_meta_and_dedupes

attrs: doc = " A model switch between turns moves the denominator, and the frontend's"
doc = " reducer drops a `used == 0` update while it holds a positive one — so the"
doc = " previous model's window has to be re-keyed at turn start, not cleared."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::grok_window_change_usage_rekeys_a_live_pair_to_the_new_window

attrs: doc = " The offline half of the live resolver: Grok's own on-disk catalog, then"
doc = " the id heuristic. A BYO endpoint is keyed by whatever id the user typed,"
doc = " so this genuinely can come back empty — `grok_window_change_usage` is"
doc = " what keeps that from stranding a stale window."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::grok_offline_context_window_falls_through_catalog_then_heuristic

attrs: doc = " The read loop drops at most one update per notification, so an agent"
doc = " speaking a protocol codeg can't decode used to put a WARN on the"
doc = " per-streaming-chunk path — under the DEFAULT level, which is how a field"
doc = " report ended up writing 34GB in 8.8h (issue #427). The throttle collapses"
doc = " the burst; this pins the part that must survive it, the tally."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::dropped_update_log_line_reports_what_the_throttle_swallowed

attrs: doc = " The classifier's whole purpose is to separate \"we went blind\" from"
doc = " \"nothing came\" — a `Plan`-only turn must not read as agent output."
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::diagnose_empty_turn_covers_three_causes_and_priority

attrs: doc = " Drop reasons reach the UI, so they must be redacted at capture time —"
doc = " a parser error inlines the value it choked on, and that value came off"
tests.name: acp::connection::tests::note_dropped_redacts_the_captured_error

tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::permissive_policy_writes_agent_plan_file_outside_workspace

attrs: doc = " End-to-end on the REAL default policy, which is what catches root"

doc = " A raw `starts_with` against the un-canonicalized root would fail here."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::permissive_policy_writes_into_temp_dir

attrs: doc = " A per-agent home relocation must move the allowed root with it, or the"
doc = " agent's own state directory falls outside the policy again."
doc = " Only the keys whose value IS the data root verbatim belong here; the ones"
doc = " their resolver appends a sub-path to (Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor's XDG"
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::agent_data_roots_honor_runtime_env_relocation

attrs: doc = " Each agent's relocation key must land on the SAME directory its own"
doc = " resolver would compute for that value — not one level above it. Getting"
doc = " Gemini's `.gemini` suffix wrong would make the bare relocation target"
doc = " writable, which for `GEMINI_CLI_HOME=$HOME` is the whole home directory."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::relocation_suffixes_match_the_agents_own_resolvers

attrs: doc = " For the agents whose own resolver takes the value verbatim, `~` must NOT"
doc = " be expanded: they treat it literally, so expanding here would hand out"
doc = " `$HOME` as a writable root the user never selected. Hermes' contract is"
doc = " the explicit one — `get_hermes_home` is `Path(val.strip())`, no"
doc = " a BLANK value falls back to `~/.hermes` rather than re-inheriting the"
doc = " The agents that DO expand are covered by"
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::relocation_never_expands_tilde_into_home

attrs: doc = " A `~` follows the CHILD's home, not codeg's."
doc = " `merge_agent_env` copies `HOME` into the child like any other variable,"
doc = " and overriding it is the standard way to isolate a CLI's config — so"
doc = " server's own `expanduser` and nothing else. Expanding against"
doc = " `dirs::home_dir()` authorized a directory the agent never opens while"
doc = " leaving the one it does use unwritable. The `default_rel` branch already"
doc = " went through `child_home_dir`; this makes the override branch agree."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::tilde_expands_against_the_childs_home_not_codegs

attrs: doc = " The over-broad guard has to judge the CANONICAL root, because that is"
doc = " what the policy stores and compares against."
doc = " A syntactic check is trivially bypassable: `~/work/..` is not `$HOME` as"
doc = " written but canonicalizes to exactly it, and `FsAccessPolicy::permissive`"
doc = " canonicalizes every root before storing it — so the agent would have been"
doc = " handed write access to the whole home, and with it every other agent's"
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::an_over_broad_root_is_refused_after_canonicalization

attrs: doc = " The other half of the rule: Antigravity and DeepSeek DO expand, so their"
doc = " relocated tree has to be authorized under the expanded path."
doc = " Both upstreams run the equivalent of `expanduser` on their home variable"
doc = " `GEMINI_HOME=~/relocated` the agent's files really are at"
doc = " `$HOME/relocated`. Treating the value verbatim judged it RELATIVE and"
doc = " refused the slot, which left the agent unable to write its own directory"
doc = " — while codeg, separately, created a literal `~` folder next to wherever"
doc = " it happened to be running."
doc = " A BARE `~` is still refused. It is a legal setting that puts the tree"
doc = " directly in the home directory, but authorizing `$HOME` wholesale would"
doc = " make the containment gate meaningless and hand this agent every other"
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::relocation_expands_tilde_only_for_the_agents_that_do

attrs: doc = " A blank relocation value must fall back to Hermes' default home, not"
doc = " re-inherit codeg's process env — mirroring the launch contract."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::hermes_blank_relocation_falls_back_to_default_home

attrs: doc = " When `runtime_env` relocates a profile, `merge_agent_env` gives it the"
doc = " highest precedence so the child NEVER reads the process-env default. That"
doc = " inactive tree holds config and credentials, so it must not stay writable."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::relocation_excludes_the_inactive_default_root

attrs: doc = " A BLANK value in `env_json` is not \"unset, use ours\" — the spawn layer"
doc = " (`acp::agent_process`) `env_remove`s it, so the child falls back to its"
doc = " OWN default. Reading through to codeg's process env would aim the root"
doc = " at a profile the child never opens, re-breaking the writes this change"
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::blank_runtime_value_falls_back_to_the_agents_default_not_our_env

attrs: doc = " A masked higher-precedence key must fall through to the NEXT candidate,"
doc = " not to the masked key's inherited value."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::blank_runtime_value_falls_through_to_the_next_candidate

attrs: doc = " `child_env_value` must distinguish the ways a var reaches (or fails to"
doc = " reach) the child, and must NOT normalize the value for resolvers that"
doc = " don't. Uses a private key so it cannot race another test."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::child_env_value_models_the_spawn_layers_env_remove

attrs: doc = " A RELATIVE agent home must never become a root. It would be resolved"
doc = " against codeg's cwd while the child runs in the workspace cwd, and that"
doc = " mismatch widens: `\".\"` with codeg launched from `/` yields `/`, which every"
doc = " absolute path passes `starts_with` against; `\"..\"` grants an unrelated tree."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::relative_agent_root_is_refused_not_absolutized

attrs: doc = " `merge_agent_env` copies every `runtime_env` entry into the child, `HOME`"
doc = " included — the classic way to isolate a CLI's config. The home-relative"
doc = " defaults must therefore follow the CHILD's home: anchoring them on codeg's"
doc = " would grant the inactive profile and refuse the active one."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::home_relative_defaults_follow_the_childs_home

attrs: doc = " A relative child `HOME` would be absolutized against codeg's cwd — the same"
doc = " widening as a relative agent home — so the slot is refused instead."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::relative_child_home_refuses_the_slot

attrs: doc = " A BLANK `HOME` is `env_remove`d, so the child resolves its home from the OS"
doc = " account database — which codeg cannot read without duplicating a passwd"
doc = " lookup, and `dirs::home_dir()` does NOT answer because it consults codeg's"
doc = " own `$HOME` first. So the slot is refused rather than guessed at."
doc = " Asserting \"no roots\" is stronger than asserting \"not codeg's root\", and it"
doc = " needs no `temp_env`, so it cannot race other tests that read `$HOME`."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::removed_child_home_refuses_the_slot

attrs: doc = " Refusing a slot must never widen the gate: `permissive` still seeds the"
doc = " workspace root, so an empty agent-root list cannot collapse into the"
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::refused_agent_slot_does_not_produce_an_unrestricted_policy

attrs: doc = " Same hazard through the user-facing knob."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::relative_extra_roots_are_dropped

attrs: doc = " The extra-roots list must be read VERBATIM. `split_paths` does not trim"
doc = " entries, so trimming the value first would rewrite the relative entry"
doc = " `\" / \"` into `/` and hand out the entire filesystem."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::whitespace_padded_extra_root_is_not_trimmed_into_filesystem_root

attrs: doc = " Trimming a relocation value can WIDEN the policy, not just fail to match:"
doc = " `\" / \"` reaches the child as a relative path, but trimmed it becomes the"
doc = " filesystem root and would make everything writable."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::whitespace_padded_root_never_becomes_the_filesystem_root

attrs: doc = " Pins the declarative slot table against the `crate::parsers` resolvers it"
doc = " mirrors, so a change to either side cannot drift silently. Skips any agent"
doc = " whose relocation vars are set in THIS process, where the resolver would"
doc = " legitimately return a relocated path instead of the default."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::root_slots_match_parser_resolvers

attrs: doc = " first match must win rather than both being admitted."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::cursor_relocation_respects_resolver_precedence

attrs: doc = " pi relocates its session store independently of its agent home, so a"
doc = " `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` supplied through `env_json` must widen the"
doc = " roots on its own — the process-env-only resolver cannot see it."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::pi_session_dir_relocation_is_honored

attrs: doc = " No agent may resolve a root so broad that the gate becomes meaningless —"
doc = " checked both with a clean env AND with every relocation key set to `~`,"
doc = " since a tilde-expanding bug would only show up in the latter."
tests.name: acp::file_system_runtime::tests::no_agent_data_root_is_the_home_dir_or_filesystem_root

attrs: doc = " The shape both adapters parse — version 1, and the id under"
doc = " `jetbrains.air.fork` — merged into the same `_meta` as the terminal"
doc = " snapshot. The typed request does not drop one for the other."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::fork_request_carries_the_air_fork_block_as_its_meta

tests.name: acp::fork::tests::meta_omits_absent_fingerprint_and_occurrence

doc = " so both go out: the id resolves on the active chain, the fingerprint is"
doc = " what still resolves once the point has drifted onto an abandoned branch."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::claude_sends_the_derived_id_and_the_fingerprint_together

doc = " to the fingerprint when the id misses, and `turn-<n>` is a position that"
doc = " can never collide with a record uuid."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::claude_falls_back_to_the_fingerprint_with_no_agent_id

doc = " no text and no id. `fingerprint(\"\")` would match every text-free"
doc = " grouping on Claude's side, so guessing between them by occurrence is"
doc = " strictly worse than not naming a point at all."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::claude_declines_a_synthesized_turn_with_neither_id_nor_text

attrs: doc = " A textless turn Claude DID name is still a fork point by id alone."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::claude_forks_a_textless_named_turn_by_its_id_alone

attrs: doc = " An answer repeated verbatim must still fork at the one the user clicked,"

attrs: doc = " Codex hashes agent messages only, so a user turn with identical text"

tests.name: acp::fork::tests::codex_occurrence_ignores_user_turns

attrs: doc = " The fingerprint is the only thing that can resolve on codex, so a turn"
doc = " with no text to hash is not a fork point."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::codex_declines_a_turn_with_no_text

attrs: doc = " DeepSeek reads BOTH halves, so both are sent — unlike codex, whose id"
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::deepseek_sends_the_log_id_and_the_fingerprint_together

attrs: doc = " A log that named nothing still forks by content, the codex shape: the id"
doc = " is codeg's own turn id, which DeepSeek cannot match, so it falls through"
doc = " to the fingerprint instead of failing."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::deepseek_falls_back_to_the_fingerprint_with_no_log_id

attrs: doc = " An id with no text is still a fork point on DeepSeek — a bubble whose"
doc = " whole turn was tool calls names a message the adapter can look up, which"
doc = " is exactly what codex cannot do."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::deepseek_forks_a_textless_turn_by_its_id_alone

attrs: doc = " Neither half available (a bubble opened by a tool result alone) is not a"
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::deepseek_declines_a_turn_with_neither_id_nor_text

attrs: doc = " The fingerprint half counts the same way codex's does, so a repeated"
doc = " answer in a log that named nothing still forks at the one clicked."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::deepseek_counts_repeated_answers

attrs: doc = " Forking \"up to\" a user turn is what a plain fork-send already does, and"
doc = " no adapter resolves an id against a user message."
tests.name: acp::fork::tests::user_turns_are_not_fork_points

attrs: doc = " Every other agent has no explicit fork point — advertising one they do"

attrs: doc = " Pinned against a digest computed outside this crate, so a change of hash"

tests.name: acp::fork::tests::fingerprint_is_sha256_hex

attrs: doc = " will_wake=true`. The live observer must claim that wake so the"

tests.name: acp::grok_autonomous::tests::monitor_event_before_task_completed_emits_autonomous_wake

doc = " verified `<system-reminder>` always follows its `task_completed`, so one"
doc = " arriving with no settled/adjacent evidence is a replay and must not open"
doc = " an episode (which would pin the prompt gate on a wake that never comes)."
tests.name: acp::grok_autonomous::tests::system_reminder_without_completion_evidence_stays_unclaimed

attrs: doc = " Single test sequences all env-var assertions to avoid the"

tests.name: acp::idle_sweep::tests::idle_timeout_env_parsing

attrs: doc = " Transcript rollover is correctness-critical: the filter admits it, and"
doc = " the existing per-destination ingress delivers it to the worker even"
doc = " when that destination is saturated."
tests.name: acp::internal_bus::tests::transcript_rollover_is_critical_and_reaches_worker_under_backpressure

attrs: doc = " A terminal `ToolCallUpdate` (completed) for a registered delegation"
doc = " tombstones its keyed entry, so a `delegate_to_agent` that went terminal"
doc = " without its round-trip ever arriving leaves nothing for a later same-key"
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::terminal_update_tombstones_registered_delegation

attrs: doc = " A NON-terminal update must NOT tombstone: this is the serialized"
doc = " round-trip case (Claude Code runs parallel `delegate_to_agent` calls"
doc = " one-at-a-time, so the 2nd entry waits `in_progress` for up to ~77s before"
doc = " its round-trip fires). Evicting it here would reintroduce the dead-card"
doc = " bug the keyed-retention rule was added to fix."
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::non_terminal_update_does_not_tombstone

attrs: doc = " A terminal update for an unrelated (non-delegation) tool call no-ops and"
doc = " leaves a registered delegation intact — the tombstone runs for every"
doc = " terminal update but only removes a matching pending delegation id."
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::terminal_update_for_unrelated_tool_is_harmless

attrs: doc = " A terminal status shipped via the non-update `ToolCall` variant (some"
doc = " hosts use it for status flips — see `register_pending_tool_call`'s dedupe"
doc = " doc) tombstones too, symmetric with the `ToolCallUpdate` path. Without"
doc = " this, a terminal `ToolCall` still carrying the delegation shape would"
doc = " RE-REGISTER the stale entry instead of removing it. Uses `failed` to also"
doc = " drive that terminal value through the dispatcher."
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::terminal_tool_call_variant_tombstones_registered_delegation

attrs: doc = " A terminal `ToolCall` for an id with no pending entry must NOT register a"
doc = " fresh one — it short-circuits at the terminal branch before the register"
doc = " path, so it can't itself create the stale entry it exists to prevent."
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::terminal_tool_call_does_not_register_fresh_entry

attrs: doc = " The headline regression: a delegation whose `agent_type`/`task` arrive"
doc = " on a `ToolCallUpdate` (the initial `ToolCall` had a model-generated"
doc = " title and no `raw_input`) is still registered, keyed, and claimable by"
doc = " its MCP round-trip. The old `ToolCall`-only path never saw the args, so"
doc = " this call fell back to a synthetic id → dead \"view session\"."
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::registers_delegation_from_tool_call_update

attrs: doc = " An initial `ToolCall` whose title names the tool but carries no args"
doc = " registers UNKEYED; a later `ToolCallUpdate` with the args must backfill"
doc = " the key. The in-loop claim binds ONLY by exact key match (unkeyed entries"
doc = " are never claimed there), so `tc-2` becomes claimable purely because the"
doc = " backfill landed its key — shown here alongside a parallel keyed sibling"
doc = " it must not be mixed up with."
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::update_backfills_key_onto_unkeyed_tool_call

attrs: doc = " The high-frequency non-delegation tool stream (bash/read/write and"
doc = " their `raw_output` update floods) must never register anything — that's"
doc = " what keeps the dispatcher-side check cheap and the pending queue clean."

attrs: doc = " Cursor announces every MCP call as the literal \"MCP: tool\" (identity"

attrs: doc = " The candidate branch is scoped to the EXACT fallback title — other"

doc = " AND to the empty raw_input Cursor actually ships; a same-titled call"
doc = " carrying real args is not the identity-less shape."
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::near_miss_generic_titles_do_not_register

attrs: doc = " Cursor's full-form MCP `raw_input` nests the delegation arguments under"

doc = " announcement with the broker BEFORE calling `enricher.maybe_schedule`"
doc = " — otherwise the store-backed backfill has nothing to attach to and"
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::run_broker_tool_side_effects_registers_then_enriches

attrs: doc = " A terminal `ToolCallUpdate` that lands WHILE the store lookup is"
doc = " still in flight must tombstone the entry, and the eventual (late)"
doc = " store resolution must NOT resurrect it — the tombstone is the"
doc = " permanent winner, never the late backfill."
tests.name: acp::lifecycle::delegation_registration_tests::terminal_event_during_lookup_prevents_late_backfill

attrs: doc = " Exercises the actual injection seam `lifecycle_subscriber_task` uses"
doc = " `enricher_for_lifecycle` — rather than bypassing it (the two tests"

doc = " anywhere in the crate — permanent dead code, and the seam itself"

doc = " (the default every other lifecycle test relies on), the same"
doc = " `broker.as_ref().and_then(...)` composition must yield `None` for a"
doc = " `Some(broker)` input — proving the default-safe path (no"
doc = " `~/.cursor` access) is what every existing `lifecycle_subscriber_task`"

attrs: doc = " Root terminal disconnect must remain the durable CAS winner when a"
doc = " delayed `TurnComplete(end_turn)` arrives later on the same connection."
