tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_keeps_codex_111_orientation

attrs: doc = " A codex form whose questions all have `isOther: false` carries NO"
doc = " companion, in either generation — so the form itself cannot be dated and"
doc = " the running adapter's version is the only real signal. Both readings are"
doc = " reachable, and `None` falls back to the pinned adapter's shape."
doc = " This is the ordinary case, not an edge one: most `request_user_input`"
tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_undated_codex_form_follows_the_running_adapter

attrs: doc = " The running adapter's version OUTRANKS a companion marker: it describes"
doc = " the process that built the frame. They agree in practice, so this pins"
doc = " the precedence rather than a behavior anyone should see."
tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_running_version_outranks_the_companion_marker

attrs: doc = " The 1.12.0 fixups are codex-only. DeepSeek is routed through this same"
doc = " and for DeepSeek a value that is not in the option set is decoded as a"
doc = " CUSTOM answer — so silently eating a real \"None of the above\" would not"
doc = " just hide a radio, it would change what the agent is told."
tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_non_codex_form_keeps_none_of_the_above

attrs: doc = " The gate is the PEER, not the payload. `_meta` is an open namespace, so"
doc = " a non-codex speaker — DeepSeek, or any MCP server whose form either"
doc = " adapter relays — can carry a `codex` block of its own meaning. If that"
doc = " were enough to unlock the codex fixups, a third party could make codeg"
doc = " hide one of its fields (the companion skip), read its questions upside"
doc = " down (the orientation flip) and delete one of its options (the synthetic"
doc = " filter). None of those may fire on `ElicitationPeer::Other`."
doc = " The same payload under a codex peer is asserted right below, so the test"
doc = " shows the identity gate doing the deciding rather than the payload"
tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_foreign_codex_meta_is_ignored_off_codex

attrs: doc = " The synthetic-option filter matches THIS choice's own `oneOf` entry, by"
doc = " `const`, rather than asking whether the array contains a synthetic entry"
doc = " anywhere. Scanning would drop a legitimate option that merely shares the"
doc = " label with one — and since the labels collide, the dedup pass then eats"
doc = " the synthetic one too, leaving the real choice unselectable and its"
doc = " `const` unmappable on the way back."
doc = " A conforming codex cannot send this pair (it writes `const: label` for"
doc = " every option and skips its injection when the label is already taken),"
doc = " so this pins the narrowing rather than a shape seen in the wild."
tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_keeps_a_same_label_option_with_its_own_const

attrs: doc = " …and within codex, a NON-`isOther` question is never injected into"
doc = " either, so its options are left alone too."
tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_codex_non_other_question_keeps_none_of_the_above

attrs: doc = " A generic MCP server's form has no `codex` namespace at all, so it keeps"
doc = " the JSON Schema reading codeg has always used — `description` is the"
doc = " prose, `title` the short label. The swap is codex-only."
tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_generic_mcp_form_keeps_description_as_the_question

attrs: doc = " 1.12.0 omits `description` entirely when the model supplied no header —"
doc = " the question still comes from `title`, and the tab label is synthesized."
tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_codex_112_without_a_header_still_reads_the_title

attrs: doc = " Defense against over-skipping the renamed companion: a REAL question"
doc = " whose id merely ends in `_note` carries no `_meta.codex` marker, so it"
doc = " must render. (This is why the `_note` rename is matched by marker only,"
doc = " never by name — unlike the legacy `__other`.)"
tests.name: acp::question::tests::classify_elicitation_keeps_an_unmarked_field_named_note

attrs: doc = " Regression: desktop setup calls `build_delegation_stack` (and thus"
doc = " `start_maintenance`) on the main thread outside a Tokio context."
doc = " Plain `tokio::spawn` panics there; the tauri-runtime path must not."
tests.name: acp::recovery_authorization::recovery_authorization::start_maintenance_outside_tokio_context_does_not_panic

attrs: doc = " The URL is what decides whether a custom version can be installed, not"
doc = " An agent can have both a registry version and download URLs that never"
doc = " mention it, and then substituting a requested version into the URL is a"
doc = " no-op: the same archive comes down and gets cached under whatever number"
doc = " was typed, leaving `installed_version` describing a build that was never"
doc = " fetched. The settings page used to offer the control to every binary"
doc = " agent with a version, which is exactly that inference."
tests.name: acp::registry::tests::custom_version_install_follows_the_url_not_the_version_field

attrs: doc = " #754. The regression that mattered was not arithmetic, it was a child"
doc = " that could no longer `bind`, so this asserts against the kernel rather"
doc = " Before the length budget existed this bound"
doc = " failed with `path must be shorter than SUN_LEN`."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::a_child_can_bind_a_unix_socket_inside_the_scratch_dir

attrs: doc = " The fallback only fires when it has to: a temp directory short enough to"
doc = " nest under keeps the churn where the user's `TMPDIR` points, which is"
doc = " the case on a typical Linux box where `temp_dir()` is already `/tmp`."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::a_short_temp_dir_is_still_nested_under_normally

attrs: doc = " ...and an over-long one moves to the short root rather than being nested"
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::an_over_long_temp_dir_falls_back_to_the_short_root

attrs: doc = " `short_root` lives in a `1777` `/tmp`, so the root can be waiting for us"
doc = " when we get there. A symlink is the dangerous shape: `create_dir_all` is"
doc = " satisfied by one pointing at a directory, which would put the whole"
doc = " scratch tree — and the sweeps that delete it — wherever it aims."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::a_symlinked_root_is_refused

attrs: doc = " The other half: a root we DO own, merely left group/world-reachable by a"
doc = " codeg that predates the `0700`. Refusing that would turn every upgrade"
doc = " into a silent loss of isolation, so it is tightened instead."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::a_loose_root_we_own_is_tightened_rather_than_refused

attrs: doc = " A launch directory is what the child is actually handed, so it carries"
doc = " the same `0700` as the root above it."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::a_launch_directory_is_private_and_reports_collisions

attrs: doc = " The budget is only worth anything if it is measured against the number"
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::sun_path_cap_matches_the_kernel

attrs: doc = " Whatever root is chosen must stay reachable by the sweeps, or the fix"
doc = " for #754 would reopen the leak #735 closed by stranding directories"
doc = " under a root nothing enumerates any more."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::the_sweeps_still_cover_the_root_that_is_not_in_use

attrs: doc = " Anything that is not ours is skipped rather than deleted — the sweeps"
doc = " only ever touch names they can prove they minted."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::pid_parser_rejects_foreign_names

attrs: doc = " Our own live pid is always `Alive`, and the probe never answers `Dead`"
doc = " for it — the case that would let a sweep delete a running launch."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::probe_reports_our_own_process_alive

attrs: doc = " The failure this guards is silent and permanent: a handle destroyed"
doc = " without `release` (a cancelled HTTP request, an `on_exit` callback"
doc = " dropped because the connection never reported a reap) used to leave its"
doc = " name in `REGISTRY` forever, and `sweep_own_orphans` skips every"
doc = " registered name — so the directory became invisible to the one thing"
doc = " that would have reclaimed it."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::dropping_without_release_still_hands_the_name_back

attrs: doc = " `release` is the same cleanup, just without the \"somebody forgot\" log."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::release_removes_the_directory_and_the_registration

attrs: doc = " Windows env names are case-insensitive while this map is not, so a"
doc = " per-agent `tmp` would ride along beside the injected `TMP` and the child"
doc = " could read either. Unix is the opposite case: there the two really are"
doc = " different variables and dropping one would destroy a setting."
tests.name: acp::scratch_dir::tests::a_case_variant_temp_key_cannot_shadow_the_scratch_dir

attrs: doc = " `ConversationLinked` must forget the live-title skip-cache."
doc = " Today this clear can only ever be a no-op: `emit_conversation_update`"
doc = " refuses to cache a title while `conversation_id` is `None`, and both"
doc = " producers of `ConversationLinked` fire only from that same unbound"
doc = " state, so the cache is already empty every time this runs. It is kept —"
doc = " and pinned here — because the day something rebinds a LIVE connection to"
doc = " another row, a cache carried over from the old one would classify the"
doc = " new row's first title as a repeat and leave it Untitled for the rest of"
doc = " the connection, with no error anywhere to point at."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::conversation_linked_clears_the_native_title_skip_cache

attrs: doc = " Only the spawn frame carries a task's identity, so it is the only one"
doc = " allowed to create a row: a progress delta for an id we never saw"
doc = " announced means codeg failed to read the announcement, and a row with a"
doc = " placeholder name and no type is worse than no row at all."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::async_task_rows_are_created_only_by_a_spawn_delta

attrs: doc = " Progress/state deltas are PARTIAL: an absent field must leave the stored"
doc = " value alone, or the first progress tick would blank out the task's name."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::async_task_deltas_revise_only_the_fields_they_carry

attrs: doc = " Reaping an idle connection kills the agent CLI, and with it any"
doc = " background work. A live async task must hold the connection open on its"
doc = " own — the transcript watcher is a separate, overlapping observer, so the"
doc = " two combine by OR (never a sum, which would double-count one shell)."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::a_live_async_task_alone_defers_the_idle_sweep

attrs: doc = " The exemption is what stops the idle sweep, so a row that never reaches a"
doc = " terminal state would otherwise hold the agent CLI open forever. Bounded"
doc = " by the same window as the watcher's half, and refreshed by any delta —"
doc = " a task that keeps reporting keeps its exemption for as long as it runs."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::a_silent_async_task_stops_deferring_the_sweep_after_the_keepalive_window

attrs: doc = " A fork attaches to a NEW session id on the same process. The old"
doc = " session's task rows can never settle here again — their terminal frames"
doc = " are published on the id the `AgentSession` router has stopped routing to"
doc = " this connection — so they must go, or the strip shows work that never"
doc = " finishes and the keep-alive pins the CLI open."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::a_session_id_change_drops_the_previous_session_tasks

attrs: doc = " Issue #496: a long turn that reconnects N times stacked N permanent"
doc = " strips, because the only settle points were a clean `end_turn` and the"
doc = " next prompt. Turn PROGRESS settles the incident instead — codex's own"
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::session_failure_retry_incidents_settle_on_turn_progress

attrs: doc = " Grace → progress (Cleared) must leave attach snapshot without the lease."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::tool_watchdog_snapshot_grace_then_progress_clear_is_empty

attrs: doc = " Grace → normal complete (Cleared, no error_code) must leave snapshot empty."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::tool_watchdog_snapshot_grace_then_complete_clear_is_empty

attrs: doc = " TimedOut is a terminal event: publish then remove — never a durable ledger."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::tool_watchdog_snapshot_timed_out_does_not_accumulate

attrs: doc = " I1: TimedOut first (emit race), then stale lower-version Cancelling must"
doc = " not resurrect an actionable banner after the terminal tombstone."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::tool_watchdog_rejects_stale_cancelling_after_timed_out

attrs: doc = " I1 R3: multi-lease cold attach must expose complete terminal floors so"
doc = " a late lower-version Cancelling for A is rejected after B replaced"
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::tool_watchdog_snapshot_carries_multi_lease_max_version_floors

attrs: doc = " Concurrent leases: high per-lease version must not hide a newer"
doc = " transition from a different lease (versions restart at 1 per lease)."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::last_diagnostic_prefers_transition_at_over_lease_version

attrs: doc = " Two concurrent leases transitioning inside the same wall second: the"
doc = " later sub-second transition wins even when the older lease has a later"
doc = " grace_deadline (lease-local field, not a global sequence)."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::last_diagnostic_same_second_prefers_later_millis_not_grace

attrs: doc = " After timed_out leaves the actionable map, reattach still sees the"
doc = " secret-safe diagnostic via snapshot history."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::last_diagnostic_survives_timed_out_reattach_snapshot

attrs: doc = " Parent → subagent → parent interleave must produce three blocks: the"
doc = " merge predicate requires the SAME `parent_tool_use_id`, so subagent"
doc = " prose can never concatenate onto the main thread (and vice versa)."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::parented_delta_interleave_never_merges_across_attribution

attrs: doc = " The frontend reducer drops an empty `CONTENT_DELTA` outright, so a"
doc = " streaming client never sees an empty `Text` block. If this side kept"
doc = " one, a snapshot-hydrated client would get an extra block the streaming"
doc = " one lacks — and prose either side of it would render as two runs"
doc = " instead of one (#494 on the snapshot path only)."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::empty_text_delta_adds_no_block_and_never_splits_a_run

attrs: doc = " …and it must not open a live message either — same as the reducer,"
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::empty_text_delta_does_not_open_a_live_message

attrs: doc = " Out-of-turn parented chunks (async subagent still streaming after the"
doc = " parent turn settled) must not resurrect a live_message via"
doc = " `ensure_live_message` — the snapshot would hand that ghost to every"
doc = " attaching client. Main-thread chunks keep the unconditional append."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::parented_delta_outside_prompting_does_not_touch_live_message

attrs: doc = " Snapshot round-trip: `parent_tool_use_id` survives serialization, and a"
doc = " snapshot written by an older backend (no field) still deserializes."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::live_block_parent_survives_snapshot_and_old_snapshots_parse

attrs: doc = " `last_assistant_text` is the delegation child's result — a subagent's"
doc = " trailing prose is the CHILD's voice and must not read as the answer."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::last_assistant_text_ignores_parented_blocks

attrs: doc = " The ordinary turn stays byte-identical: nothing is trimmed while the"
doc = " table fits the budget, so the wire shape is exactly what it always was."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::snapshot_carries_every_tool_call_whole_while_it_fits_the_budget

attrs: doc = " A long turn keeps the running call and the most recent finished calls"
doc = " inside the tool cap. Older finished cards are omitted and counted."
doc = " Pending permission, questions, plans, delegations, and the watchdog"
doc = " stay on their own projections, so a missing tool card is not \"no task\"."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::snapshot_bounds_finished_tool_call_payload_on_a_long_turn

attrs: doc = " In-progress output is projected before finished output, so a running"
doc = " call that still fits the payload budget keeps its result whole."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::snapshot_keeps_a_running_tool_call_ahead_of_finished_output

attrs: doc = " An image on a finished call past the tool cap is an omission, not a"
doc = " card shipped with empty bytes that the client would render as failure."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::snapshot_counts_an_image_on_a_tool_call_past_the_cap

attrs: doc = " Three hundred in-progress calls still overflow the 128 slot cap. The"
doc = " newest 128 ship; the rest are an explicit omission, not a full table."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::snapshot_omits_active_tools_past_the_cap_with_an_explicit_count

attrs: doc = " Field case: a mid-turn parent with more tool calls than the numeric cap,"
doc = " including delegation cards whose ids sort after the lexicographic prefix."
doc = " Those cards must still be in the projection, and the in-memory session"
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::snapshot_keeps_live_referenced_delegation_tools_past_the_count_cap

attrs: doc = " A turn that never opened a live message has no text of its own either."
doc = " An agent whose only output was an empty text chunk reaches exactly that"
doc = " state (`append_text_delta` drops it), and the turn still ends on"
doc = " `end_turn` — so without clearing, `get_delegation_status` would hand the"
doc = " PREVIOUS turn's answer back as this turn's result."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::turn_complete_clears_stale_text_when_the_turn_produced_nothing

attrs: doc = " `TurnComplete` is emitted from three places, and the cancel path does"
doc = " not wait for the agent — so a second one can land on an already-settled"
doc = " turn. It must not wipe the text the first one captured."
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::a_repeat_turn_complete_keeps_the_captured_text

attrs: doc = " 对账测试：从初始状态全程 apply 到 N 个事件 == 从 snapshot"
doc = " (apply 完前 K 个) + apply 剩下 N-K 个事件，最终状态等价。"
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::snapshot_filtered_events_yield_same_state_as_live_subscriber

attrs: doc = " 验证 envelope 序列化 + 反序列化 round-trip"
tests.name: acp::session_state::tests::event_envelope_round_trips_through_json

attrs: doc = " The skip-cache is what keeps the two producers cheap: Claude Code"
doc = " re-emits its `ai-title` record throughout a session (228 identical"
doc = " copies in one observed transcript) and CodeBuddy re-pushes its fallback"
doc = " after every prompt. Only a CHANGED name may reach the lifecycle worker."
tests.name: acp::session_title::tests::only_a_changed_title_is_emitted

attrs: doc = " A title published before the first prompt binds the row has nowhere to"
doc = " land, so it is dropped — and deliberately NOT remembered, or the retry"
doc = " that follows `ConversationLinked` would be swallowed and the row would"
doc = " keep its fallback name for the rest of the connection."
tests.name: acp::session_title::tests::a_title_dropped_while_unbound_does_not_poison_the_cache

attrs: doc = " The two Claude producers must NORMALIZE identically, or they stop being"
doc = " claude-agent-acp 0.73.0 publishes its generated title over the wire"
doc = " (here) AND persists it to the session file, where the transcript watcher"
doc = " and the detail-fetch backfill read it back through"
doc = " `publish_native_title`, whose skip-cache only collapses IDENTICAL"
doc = " strings — and whose doc notes that two producers admitting DIFFERENT"
doc = " strings can broadcast out of order. So a divergence in trimming or in"
doc = " the length cap would not merely differ cosmetically: it would turn every"
doc = " long title into a permanent two-writer ping-pong on the sidebar row."
doc = " Asserting against the transcript helper rather than a literal is the"
doc = " point — a future change to either cap has to change both."
tests.name: acp::session_title::tests::agrees_with_the_transcript_producer_on_normalization

attrs: doc = " Matching a safe phrase says nothing about what follows it: serde_json"
doc = " appends input-derived context to some of these, and a custom error can"
doc = " open with the phrase and continue with anything at all."
tests.name: acp::stderr_tail::tests::syntax_prefix_match_drops_the_suffix

attrs: doc = " Truncating before redacting would slice a token below the length its"
doc = " pattern requires, letting the fragment through unrecognized."
tests.name: acp::stderr_tail::tests::redacts_before_truncating_so_a_split_secret_cannot_survive

attrs: doc = " A password long enough to push its terminating `@` past the scan bound"
doc = " defeats the `@`-anchored rule; the head of the password would otherwise"
doc = " survive into the retained prefix."
tests.name: acp::stderr_tail::tests::redacts_a_uri_credential_whose_terminator_is_past_the_scan_bound

attrs: doc = " The load-bearing invariant: whatever path a parser error takes, the"
doc = " original secret must not survive into the output."
tests.name: acp::stderr_tail::tests::never_echoes_the_original_secret

attrs: doc = " `route.rs` is fork-only and never conflicts, so a registry bump (Task 5"
doc = " takes upstream's 2.149.0) leaves it stale unless someone edits it by hand."
doc = " No version literal here on purpose: the invariant is agreement, not a number."
tests.name: acp::sync_invariants::codebuddy_registry_pin_matches_route_constant

attrs: doc = " Unpack DIRECTORIES are Windows-only, because that is the only platform"
doc = " where `is_idle` can actually prove a directory is not in use."
tests.name: acp::temp_reclaim::tests::directory_reclaim_is_windows_only

attrs: doc = " A path outside the system temp root is refused even when its NAME"
doc = " matches — the traversal guard, which matters because the path list"
tests.name: acp::temp_reclaim::tests::reclaim_refuses_paths_outside_the_temp_root

attrs: doc = " A freshly created artifact is inside the age guard, so even a"
doc = " correctly-shaped name in the right place is left alone."
doc = " The in-root assertion matters: without it this test would still pass if"
doc = " the path check rejected the file, and would prove nothing about the age"
doc = " guard it is named after."
tests.name: acp::temp_reclaim::tests::reclaim_respects_the_age_guard

attrs: doc = " The accept path: right shape, right place, old enough. Backdating the"
doc = " mtime is what makes this testable without a 15-minute wait."
tests.name: acp::temp_reclaim::tests::reclaim_deletes_an_aged_resource_file

attrs: doc = " Being old enough is not sufficient — the NAME still has to match a known"
doc = " leak shape, or an unrelated stale temp file would be fair game."
tests.name: acp::temp_reclaim::tests::reclaim_ignores_an_aged_file_with_an_unrelated_name

attrs: doc = " Regression: when an ACP agent calls `terminal/create` (e.g. to run"
doc = " `git push`), the runtime's base env — populated by the connection"
doc = " layer with the codeg credential helper's `GIT_CONFIG_*` keys —"
doc = " must reach the spawned process. Per-request `env` from the agent"
doc = " still wins on key collision so the agent can scrub or override"
doc = " specific keys for individual commands."
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::base_env_propagates_and_request_env_overrides

attrs: doc = " A server an AGENT starts is a server the person is about to want to"
doc = " look at, and its address only ever appears in this output — there is"
doc = " no xterm anywhere in this path."
doc = " End to end over a real child process: a real banner, a real socket,"
doc = " and the event the workspace listens for, carrying the window the"
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::a_server_an_agent_starts_is_announced_to_its_window

attrs: doc = " A runtime built without a watch is the one every test and the"
doc = " delegation probe get: it must behave exactly as it did before."
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::without_a_watch_nothing_is_announced

attrs: doc = " A `terminal/create` that omits `cwd` defaults to the runtime's"
doc = " configured working directory rather than codeg's own process cwd."
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::falls_back_to_default_cwd_when_request_omits_cwd

attrs: doc = " An explicit absolute `cwd` in the request takes precedence over the"
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::request_cwd_overrides_default_cwd

attrs: doc = " A whitespace-bearing command with empty args runs through the shell. A"
doc = " direct exec would ENOENT trying to run a program literally named with"
doc = " spaces — this is the shape CodeBuddy sends."
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::whitespace_command_runs_through_shell

attrs: doc = " A whole shell line longer than the OS path limit still runs through the"
doc = " shell. grok crams `<shell> -lc \"<script>\"` into `command` with empty"
doc = " args; a multi-KB heredoc makes the direct exec fail with ENAMETOOLONG →"
doc = " must also catch. The marker exceeds Linux's PATH_MAX (4096) so the direct"
doc = " exec fails with ENAMETOOLONG on both macOS (1024) and Linux — a sub-limit"
doc = " line would return `NotFound` and silently exercise the other branch."
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::overlong_command_line_falls_back_to_shell

attrs: doc = " The shell-wrapped path still honors the working directory, so a"
doc = " CodeBuddy-style `pnpm build` runs in the session folder."
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::shell_wrapped_command_respects_cwd

attrs: doc = " When the agent supplies explicit `args`, the command is exec'd directly"
doc = " (no shell), so an argument containing spaces stays a single argument."
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::explicit_args_bypass_shell_wrap

attrs: doc = " An explicit but non-existent absolute `cwd` is honored as-is and"
doc = " surfaces as a spawn failure — never silently downgraded to the default"
doc = " fallback or the inherited process cwd."
tests.name: acp::terminal_runtime::tests::explicit_missing_cwd_surfaces_as_spawn_failure

attrs: doc = " A real executable whose path contains spaces is exec'd directly: the"
doc = " direct spawn succeeds, so the shell fallback never fires (shell-wrapping"
doc = " would split the path at the space)."
doc = " Note: writing an executable and exec'ing it from a multi-threaded test"

tests.name: browser::agent::tests::a_listed_tab_gives_up_its_title_only_once_it_is_readable

attrs: doc = " A tab that has not committed a document yet is still a tab. Dropping it"
doc = " would make the listing flicker while a page loads; a document guest is"
doc = " dropped because it can never be shared at all."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::a_blank_tab_is_listed_and_a_document_guest_is_not

attrs: doc = " The refusal has to happen here, not at the UI: a tab showing nothing"
doc = " with an origin has no way to ever lose a grant again."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::a_tab_with_no_web_origin_cannot_be_shared_at_all

attrs: doc = " The case the whole design turns on. A dev server under `nodemon` or"
doc = " `cargo watch` is a new process on every save, and an agent-driven edit"
doc = " loop is made of saves — so the pin is the *program*, and a restart of"
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::a_restarted_dev_server_keeps_the_grant

attrs: doc = " The accident this is really for: the same runtime, an hour later,"
doc = " serving a different project. `node` and `node` say nothing; the"
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::the_same_runtime_serving_a_different_project_ends_the_grant

attrs: doc = " A grant that was never pinned — a real site, or a loopback address"
doc = " this machine could not look into — is not judged by a probe. The check"
doc = " narrows what an agent may read or does nothing; it never widens."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::an_unpinned_grant_is_never_taken_away_by_the_check

attrs: doc = " The probe runs outside the registry lock. By the time it answers, the"
doc = " tab can have navigated and been shared again for somewhere else — and"
doc = " that grant is not the one this answer is about."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::a_probe_of_one_address_does_not_judge_a_grant_on_another

attrs: doc = " Pressing \"share\" on a tab that is already shared is not a transition —"
doc = " no toast, and the audit surface keeps showing when access began. It is"
doc = " still a fresh statement about what the person means, so the pin moves."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::re_sharing_refreshes_the_pin_without_resetting_the_clock

attrs: doc = " A page that ends up with no origin at all — an `about:blank` the"
doc = " engine substituted for a load it refused, a `data:` document — is not"
doc = " the page that was shared."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::losing_the_origin_loses_the_grant

attrs: doc = " The strip branches on these three words. Renaming a variant without"
doc = " renaming its message would leave the user reading a blank line about"
doc = " something an agent just did to their page."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::an_activity_line_says_which_of_the_three_things_happened

attrs: doc = " No cap is no cap: the option is absent rather than zero, which the"
doc = " bundle would also treat as \"no cap\" but which would claim the caller"
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::an_absent_cap_stays_absent

attrs: doc = " The bundle is a program and the shim evaluates an expression, so the"
doc = " installing form has to be a function body that ends in the call. If"
doc = " this ever stops holding, world eval fails with a syntax error on a"
doc = " hundred kilobytes of generated source, which is a bad thing to debug"
doc = " on a platform one does not have."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::the_installing_form_is_one_expression_ending_in_the_call

attrs: doc = " The engine really is what the host is about to call into: if the"
doc = " bundle stopped publishing this name, every snapshot would come back"
doc = " `absent` forever and the retry would install it again each time."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::the_bundle_publishes_the_global_the_host_calls

attrs: doc = " The host's half of the ref check reads its own epoch back from the"
doc = " token the world made (`<world>.<generation>.<nav_epoch>`), and is not"
doc = " fooled by a suffix match."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::a_ref_is_current_only_under_the_epoch_it_was_issued_in

attrs: doc = " The request goes to the world as the shape `act.ts` expects — the"
doc = " action tagged by `kind`, the ref as a JSON string or null — behind the"
doc = " same \"is the engine here\" guard the read uses, and never installs it."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::the_act_call_carries_the_request_as_json_and_never_installs_the_engine

attrs: doc = " The wire shapes both sides agree on: kebab-case kinds and errors, the"
doc = " optional fields absent rather than null, and the world's answer read"
doc = " back with whichever fields it had."
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::action_wire_shapes_are_the_ones_the_world_and_the_frontend_read

attrs: doc = " The `control` level is above `read`, and asking for `read` of a"
doc = " `control` grant is allowed — the ranks are what the two checks in the"
tests.name: browser::agent::tests::control_allows_reading_and_reading_does_not_allow_control

attrs: doc = " A clip is given in CSS pixels and lands on the pixels the engine drew"
doc = " for them: the right half of a 100-CSS-pixel viewport is the blue half"
tests.name: browser::capture::tests::a_clip_in_css_pixels_lands_on_the_right_pixels

attrs: doc = " A capture that would not fit the budget is scaled down until it does"
doc = " — `maxWidth` is a ceiling — and one that fits is left at the size it"
tests.name: browser::capture::tests::a_capture_over_the_budget_is_narrowed_until_it_fits

attrs: doc = " A clip has to be a box in a viewport whose width is known; a zero-area"
doc = " region at a fractional offset must not round up to a pixel of nothing."
tests.name: browser::capture::tests::a_clip_must_be_a_real_box_in_a_known_viewport

attrs: doc = " \"Did anything break on this page\" is not \"which error lines can still"
doc = " be read\": a page that logs a thousand lines after its one error pushes"
doc = " that error out of the ring and past the budget, and the answer must"
doc = " still be yes until the document is replaced."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::an_error_pushed_out_of_the_ring_is_still_an_error_the_page_printed

attrs: doc = " The budget refuses a line before the ring ever sees it — and the very"
doc = " first error of a page in a logging loop is exactly the line that gets"
doc = " refused. Counting it is the difference between a red mark and a page"
tests.name: browser::console::tests::an_error_the_budget_refuses_is_counted_all_the_same

attrs: doc = " Reads answer with the seq to continue from, and `since` excludes what"
doc = " was already seen — the two together are what makes polling the console"
doc = " cheap for an agent working through a page."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::a_read_can_be_continued_from_where_it_stopped

attrs: doc = " A line from an origin the grant does not cover is never handed out,"
doc = " whichever way it got into the ring."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::a_read_gives_only_the_lines_of_the_granted_origin

attrs: doc = " The ring is bounded, what it evicts is counted, and the sender's own"
doc = " count rides along. A clear resets the count with the lines: it is a"
tests.name: browser::console::tests::the_ring_is_bounded_and_counts_what_it_lost

attrs: doc = " The host admits a bounded number of lines per second per tab however"
doc = " many frames send them, counts the rest, and starts afresh a second"
doc = " later. A default ring is a new ring."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::the_host_budget_bounds_a_tab_however_many_frames_it_has

attrs: doc = " A line that is not admissible still spends the tab's budget — a"
doc = " frame on another origin is one of the tab's frames — but is neither"
doc = " stored nor counted as dropped, and a long URL is cut like the text."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::an_inadmissible_line_spends_the_budget_without_being_kept_or_counted

attrs: doc = " Only a line from the tab's own origin is worth storing."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::a_line_is_admissible_only_from_the_tabs_own_origin

attrs: doc = " The engine can hand over a megabyte in one argument or a thousand"
doc = " arguments; neither is copied whole."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::cdp_pieces_are_capped_before_they_are_joined

attrs: doc = " The helper's payload is page-controlled: only a known level makes a"
doc = " line, the source falls back to `console`, numbers are bounded, and the"
doc = " engine's word on the frame wins over anything in the payload."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::a_reported_payload_is_checked_field_by_field

attrs: doc = " Each kind of CDP value reads as the developer tools would show it,"
doc = " and `%` substitutions are applied as the page meant them."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::cdp_arguments_read_like_a_console_line

attrs: doc = " Thirty-two capped pieces would still add up to more than the channel"
doc = " envelope; the assembled line is capped before it leaves the shim."
tests.name: browser::console::tests::a_cdp_line_of_many_large_pieces_is_capped_as_a_whole

attrs: doc = " A snippet ending in a line comment must not swallow the wrapper that"
doc = " follows it — the newline after the code is what keeps the expression"
tests.name: browser::eval::tests::a_trailing_line_comment_cannot_eat_the_wrapper

attrs: doc = " The answer type has no address in it, and cannot grow one by accident:"
doc = " the field the host holds against the grant is filled in by the host."
tests.name: browser::eval::tests::the_pages_answer_carries_no_address

attrs: doc = " What the page chose to send is clamped on arrival as well as at the"
doc = " source: the render is the page's code, and a page that skips it is"
doc = " exactly the case the host cap is for."
tests.name: browser::eval::tests::an_oversized_answer_is_clamped_by_the_host_too

attrs: doc = " A snippet that threw comes back as an outcome with the stack in it —"
doc = " not as a failed call, which would throw the answer away."
tests.name: browser::eval::tests::an_exception_is_an_answer

attrs: doc = " A value clipped at the cap must not be cut inside a character."
tests.name: browser::eval::tests::clipping_lands_on_a_character_boundary

attrs: doc = " The renderer opens every call, so a snippet that never returns anything"
doc = " still has something to report with — and nothing it declares outlives"
doc = " the call on the page's globals."
tests.name: browser::eval::tests::every_call_carries_its_renderer_and_leaves_nothing_behind

attrs: doc = " The banners this feature exists for, verbatim from the tools that"
doc = " print them. A change that stops recognising one of these lines is the"
doc = " whole feature silently not working for that framework."
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::real_dev_server_banners_are_recognised

attrs: doc = " The token IS the credential; an address without it opens a login page"
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::a_query_string_survives_but_a_fragment_does_not

attrs: doc = " A terminal hyperlink puts the address in an OSC 8 sequence AND in the"
doc = " visible text; stripping the sequence leaves the one we can trust."
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::an_osc8_hyperlink_is_read_from_its_visible_text

attrs: doc = " 8 KiB reads cut wherever they cut. Half an address must not be probed"
doc = " as a whole one — `http://localhost:51` is a valid address for a port"
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::an_address_split_across_chunks_is_found_once_and_whole

attrs: doc = " The line the server prints right after the local one. It names another"
doc = " machine's view of this host, and nothing here can vouch for it."
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::the_network_line_and_public_addresses_are_refused

attrs: doc = " The scheme's default port is the socket the probe has to reach."
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::an_address_without_a_port_still_names_one

attrs: doc = " A watcher that reprints its banner on every rebuild must not turn into"
doc = " a stream of offers — but ten seconds later the same address is worth"
doc = " another look, because the previous offer may have found nothing"
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::the_same_origin_is_rate_limited_not_silenced_forever

attrs: doc = " Two different ports in one banner are two services."
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::a_banner_with_two_addresses_offers_both

attrs: doc = " A process that never prints a newline must not grow the buffer without"
doc = " bound; past the cap the text is scanned as it stands."
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::an_unterminated_flood_is_bounded_and_still_scanned

attrs: doc = " The rate-limit table is bounded, and evicting an entry only costs a"
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::the_recent_table_is_capped

attrs: doc = " Output with no address at all is the common case and must not allocate"
doc = " a carry buffer it will never use."
tests.name: browser::service_url::tests::ordinary_output_is_ignored_without_buffering

attrs: doc = " The banner of a watcher that rebuilds twenty times an hour is the same"
tests.name: browser::services::tests::the_same_terminal_announces_an_origin_once

attrs: doc = " Someone starting a server in a second terminal did something new, and"
doc = " hears about it — but the list still has one entry for the address."
tests.name: browser::services::tests::another_terminal_on_the_same_address_is_announced_again

attrs: doc = " The whole liveness story: an entry whose server has gone is dropped by"
doc = " the read that finds it gone, and a live one survives."
tests.name: browser::services::tests::reading_the_list_drops_what_no_longer_answers

attrs: doc = " Output full of addresses must not turn into output full of threads,"
doc = " each parked on a socket for two seconds."
tests.name: browser::services::tests::probes_are_capped_and_the_cap_is_given_back

attrs: doc = " A probe that never succeeds leaves nothing behind, so the next banner"
doc = " from the same terminal is still a candidate."
tests.name: browser::services::tests::a_dead_address_is_not_recorded_by_announcing_it

attrs: doc = " An answer to a question that is no longer waiting changes nothing — and"
doc = " in particular does not release the question that IS waiting."
tests.name: browser::confirm::tests::an_answer_to_the_wrong_question_is_ignored

attrs: doc = " Saying no quiets that tab, and only that tab."
tests.name: browser::confirm::tests::a_refusal_buys_quiet_on_that_tab

attrs: doc = " Allowing does not start a cooldown: a person who says yes is working"
doc = " with the agent, and the next snippet is part of the same work."
tests.name: browser::confirm::tests::saying_yes_does_not_quiet_the_tab

attrs: doc = " Nobody answered: the slot frees and the tab goes quiet, exactly as for"
doc = " a refusal. An empty room does not become a fuller one by being asked"
tests.name: browser::confirm::tests::silence_frees_the_slot_and_quiets_the_tab

attrs: doc = " A late abandon must not take down the question that replaced it."
tests.name: browser::confirm::tests::abandoning_a_stale_id_leaves_the_live_question_alone

attrs: doc = " Pins are keyed by the path that was asked for: a link served once"
doc = " and then pointed at another file is a change under that path, even"
doc = " when the new target is older than the approval."
tests.name: browser::doc_guest::tests::a_retargeted_link_is_a_change

attrs: doc = " A directory link retargeted after the approval changes what every"
doc = " path through it names: a file not yet pinned, older than the"
doc = " approval, must still be refused."
tests.name: browser::doc_guest::tests::a_retargeted_directory_link_is_a_change

attrs: doc = " A link reached through another link's target is part of the path as"
doc = " much as a lexical component: retargeting it is a change too."
tests.name: browser::doc_guest::tests::a_retargeted_link_behind_a_link_is_a_change

attrs: doc = " The link walk resolves like the filesystem (relative targets, `..`,"
doc = " absolute targets) and refuses what it cannot read."
tests.name: browser::doc_guest::tests::the_link_walk_resolves_like_realpath_and_fails_closed

attrs: doc = " The component-wise open refuses a path that goes through a symlink,"
doc = " which is what a directory swapped for a link after the confinement"
tests.name: browser::doc_guest::tests::open_beneath_refuses_symlinked_components

attrs: doc = " A request that finds scripts switched off meanwhile answers as safe"
doc = " mode: the policy in the response follows the decision, not the mode"
tests.name: browser::doc_guest::tests::a_request_after_a_switch_to_safe_is_served_safe

attrs: doc = " The half of per-document origins that actually holds."
doc = " A guest can ask for any host under the scheme — its own handler is"
doc = " the one that answers, and the webview check passes because it really"
doc = " is that guest asking. Serving it would hand out this root's files,"
doc = " which is no leak, under the OTHER document's origin, which is that"
doc = " document's storage. Distinct hosts without this are decoration."
tests.name: browser::doc_guest::tests::a_request_for_another_documents_origin_is_refused

attrs: doc = " A dangling symlink is \"nothing here\" to `exists()`, and the engine"
doc = " would write through it to wherever it points."
tests.name: browser::downloads::tests::a_symlink_in_the_way_counts_as_taken

attrs: doc = " The cap must never drop a transfer that is still running: its"
doc = " completion would find nothing and the UI would say \"downloading\" for"
tests.name: browser::downloads::tests::the_history_cap_never_evicts_a_running_download

attrs: doc = " The badge the element goes in is named by this label, and the block"
doc = " says it on one line — which a page could break with its own `id`."
tests.name: browser::handoff::tests::a_label_the_page_split_over_lines_is_one_line

attrs: doc = " Every block opens with the header the shared code recognizes a"
tests.name: browser::handoff::tests::every_block_opens_with_the_shared_header

attrs: doc = " A page can describe an element with more than the channel will carry."
doc = " The picker sheds parts to get the report through, and the block has to"
doc = " say so — otherwise \"no attributes\" reads as a fact about the element."
tests.name: browser::handoff::tests::a_report_the_page_made_too_large_says_it_was_cut

attrs: doc = " Three shapes that each looked safe and were not: a URL with no"
doc = " authority still has a query, a percent-encoded key is still that key,"
doc = " and the address a console line names is fetched like any other."
tests.name: browser::handoff::tests::the_ways_a_credential_used_to_get_out

attrs: doc = " Clicking a link that downloads leaves the navigation for ever"
doc = " uncommitted. Without this the load watcher's \"the requested address"
doc = " never arrived\" rule paints an error page over a perfectly good page."
tests.name: browser::hooks::tests::a_download_leaves_the_tab_on_the_page_it_is_showing

attrs: doc = " A tab opened straight on a download URL has no document at all; it"
doc = " stays empty rather than claiming a failure."
tests.name: browser::hooks::tests::a_download_into_a_fresh_tab_settles_empty

attrs: doc = " The load in flight ended and nothing was reported for it. A tab with a"
doc = " page on screen keeps it: the navigation was abandoned (superseded,"
doc = " cancelled by the page, answered with nothing to show), which is not a"
doc = " failure — and an error page here would take the surface off the screen"
doc = " and stop the script that was about to navigate again."
tests.name: browser::hooks::tests::a_page_on_screen_survives_a_navigation_that_ended_without_one

attrs: doc = " Nothing ever arrived: the error page names the address that was asked"
doc = " for, and falls back to the tab's own when there is none."
tests.name: browser::hooks::tests::an_empty_tab_reports_the_address_that_never_arrived

attrs: doc = " Only an adopted popup — a window a page opened — may close itself."
tests.name: browser::hooks::tests::a_page_may_only_close_the_window_it_opened

attrs: doc = " An empty document committed in place of the page that was started is"
doc = " a refused load; a page that heads for `about:blank` itself is not."
tests.name: browser::hooks::tests::a_blank_commit_counts_as_failure_only_when_something_else_was_started

attrs: doc = " Apple's codes, by kind — and the two that are NOT page failures."
tests.name: browser::hooks::tests::load_errors_classify_by_domain_and_code

attrs: doc = " Two tabs can be asked for at once — unlike a consent dialog, opening a"
doc = " tab puts no question in front of anyone, so there is nothing to"
tests.name: browser::open_request::tests::two_requests_are_in_flight_at_once_and_do_not_cross

attrs: doc = " A second document answering the same request changes nothing: the"
doc = " first answer is the tab the agent was told about, and replacing it"
doc = " would name a tab the agent never heard of."
tests.name: browser::open_request::tests::the_first_answer_wins

attrs: doc = " An abandoned request is forgotten rather than left in the map, and a"
doc = " late answer to it is refused like any other stale one."
tests.name: browser::open_request::tests::abandoning_frees_the_entry

attrs: doc = " A workspace that could not open the tab says so, rather than going"
doc = " quiet and leaving the agent to wait out the timeout."
tests.name: browser::open_request::tests::a_workspace_can_answer_that_it_opened_nothing

attrs: doc = " A page's own frames may hold the opaque-origin content pages compose"
doc = " (srcdoc previews, data: sandboxes); the filesystem and app schemes"
doc = " stay out of frames too."
tests.name: browser::policy::tests::subframes_may_hold_opaque_content_but_not_local_schemes

attrs: doc = " The same server under a different spelling of its name must not slip"
doc = " past a rule: a trailing dot, a long-form IPv6 literal, upper case."
tests.name: browser::policy::tests::host_spellings_that_name_the_same_server_match

attrs: doc = " Mirror of the frontend's `matchHostRule` table."
tests.name: browser::policy::tests::wildcard_semantics

attrs: doc = " The derivation must keep finding the store the default profile has"
doc = " used since it shipped, and must tell profiles apart."
tests.name: browser::profile::tests::identifiers_derive_from_the_profile_id

attrs: doc = " The tokens a sniffing site looks for, and the reason this exists: a"
doc = " string that stops at `(KHTML, like Gecko)` is read as \"not a browser\"."
tests.name: browser::profile::tests::the_default_identity_names_the_browser_the_engine_belongs_to

attrs: doc = " The environment list extends the built-in one with the same rule"
doc = " (exact host or a subdomain), whatever the spelling."
tests.name: browser::profile::tests::extra_sign_in_hosts_come_from_the_environment_list

attrs: doc = " One open at a time per id: the second reservation fails while the"
doc = " first is held, and a dropped reservation frees the id again."
tests.name: browser::registry::tests::open_reservations_are_exclusive_and_released_on_drop

attrs: doc = " There is no tab to arm a pick on until a surface exists, and a surface"
doc = " needs a webview — so the slot's behaviour with a tab is covered on a"
doc = " real machine. What is checkable here is that asking about a tab that is"
doc = " not there answers \"no\" rather than creating anything."
doc = " The rule a superseded pick is held to. Only reachable as a unit here —"
doc = " arming one needs a tab, and a tab needs a webview — but it is the whole"
doc = " of the decision, and getting it wrong made two picks in a row both end"
tests.name: browser::registry::tests::only_the_pick_that_owns_the_slot_may_end_it

attrs: doc = " The engine's errors, by kind — and the one that is NOT a page failure."
doc = " A load the user stopped must not paint an error over the page they"
tests.name: browser::shim::linux::tests::load_errors_classify_by_engine_error

attrs: doc = " The per-record clear must spare every host the app's own webviews are"
doc = " served from and nothing else."
tests.name: browser::shim::macos::tests::app_origins_are_recognised_by_record_name

doc = " therefore retires the entry its older one left behind, and a context"
doc = " nobody knows is nobody's main frame."
tests.name: browser::shim::windows::tests::a_frames_newer_world_retires_the_one_it_replaced

attrs: doc = " A context id names a context only together with the CDP session that"
doc = " reported it: ids are handed out per renderer and start over in each, so"
doc = " a frame running in one of its own can hold the very number the page's"
doc = " world has. It still speaks for itself alone — and destroying its context"
tests.name: browser::shim::windows::tests::a_context_is_named_by_its_session_as_well_as_its_id

attrs: doc = " The engine's statuses, by kind — and the one that is NOT a page failure."
tests.name: browser::shim::windows::tests::load_errors_classify_by_engine_status

attrs: doc = " The freeze frame needs the captured size, and `CapturePreview` reports"
doc = " none: it comes out of the JPEG's own frame header."
tests.name: browser::shim::windows::tests::jpeg_dimensions_come_from_the_frame_header

attrs: doc = " A browser tab must have NO Tauri IPC: its label (and the popup and"

doc = " `tauri::WebviewWindow`, so it carries a WEBVIEW label of the same name"
doc = " alongside its window label, and a capability scoped with `webviews`"
doc = " reaches it exactly as one scoped with `windows` does."
tests.name: browser::tests::browser_labels_are_absent_from_every_capability

doc = " the Lark card. Guards against a regression back to the markdown element."
tests.name: chat_channel::backends::lark::tests::body_renders_as_plain_text_not_markdown

attrs: doc = " Field VALUES carry untrusted content (a permission tool command, an agent"
doc = " error string), so they must render as `plain_text` — never `lark_md`,"
doc = " which would interpret embedded `<at>` / links / markdown. Guards against a"
doc = " regression back to the lark_md field rendering."

doc = " `find(|s| s.agent == agent)`, so a duplicated name silently routes the"
doc = " SECOND source's entries into the FIRST source's root on restore. That is"
doc = " invisible in a backup and only shows up as misplaced files on someone"
doc = " else's machine, so pin the invariant here rather than trusting review."
doc = " An agent that owns two independently-relocatable trees (DeepSeek: its"
doc = " session logs and its attachment store) needs two distinct names."

doc = " degrades every image to the parser's `[image …]` placeholder with the"
doc = " bytes gone for good — so both trees must be registered, must restore to"
doc = " their own roots, and the store's non-conversation siblings must stay out."

doc = " \"new db + stale wal\", so they must not be representable."

doc = " would be silent and permanent (the archive would hold the broken copy)."

doc = " directory SQLite may not write to, so the read-only open cannot"
doc = " succeed. The frames must still be recovered — on OUR copy — and the"
doc = " degradation must be reported rather than logged and forgotten."
tests.name: commands::backup::external::tests::readonly_open_failure_recovers_on_a_private_copy_and_is_reported

attrs: doc = " The coherence proof behind the degraded path: a main file and a WAL read"
doc = " at two instants are only usable together if the source did not move"
tests.name: commands::backup::external::tests::fingerprint_notices_the_store_moving

attrs: doc = " When the store cannot be copied at all, archive nothing for it and say"
doc = " so — rather than a torn copy `integrity_check` would call healthy."

doc = " it replaces; otherwise the next open replays a foreign WAL into it."

attrs: doc = " We did not replace that store, so its sidecars are not ours to remove."

attrs: doc = " An IO failure part-way through the sidecar sweep must leave the live"
doc = " database byte-identical — never half-published. (A directory named"
tests.name: commands::backup::external::tests::sidecar_removal_failure_leaves_the_db_untouched

attrs: doc = " Once a sidecar is gone the live store is incomplete, and the staged"
doc = " replacement is the only whole copy. Deleting it too would leave the"

tests.name: commands::backup::external::tests::replacement_is_preserved_when_publication_fails_after_destroying_something

attrs: doc = " A WAL that exists but cannot be read means committed frames are"

tests.name: commands::backup::external::tests::unreadable_wal_downgrades_below_recovered_on_copy

doc = " generation, and SQLite would apply a mismatched pair without"
doc = " complaining, so refuse the entry outright and leave the live store as"
tests.name: commands::backup::external::tests::legacy_pair_is_refused_and_live_store_untouched

attrs: doc = " The refusal is per entry, not per source: a store in the same legacy"
doc = " archive that has no `-wal` beside it is provably self-contained and"
tests.name: commands::backup::external::tests::legacy_single_file_store_still_restores

doc = " name, is what keeps that from deleting the newest snapshot."

attrs: doc = " The migration is two writes, and the second one can fail: the keyring"
doc = " takes the secret, then the row rewrite loses to a busy database. That"
doc = " leaves the state this test seeds — keyring populated, plaintext STILL in"
doc = " the row — and the next load has to finish the job."
doc = " Keying the retry off \"the keyring is empty\" would skip it forever here,"
doc = " and the plaintext would stay in `app_metadata` (and in every backup"
doc = " archive taken from it) for the life of the install."
tests.name: commands::config_sync::webdav_sync::tests::an_interrupted_migration_is_finished_by_the_next_load

attrs: doc = " The migration rewrites the row, and the row is shared: a save that lands"
doc = " between this load's read and its write must survive, and so must fields"
doc = " a NEWER build wrote that this one cannot parse. Both are the same"
doc = " property — the migration removes one key rather than serializing its own"
doc = " idea of the settings over the top — and the unknown field is the half"
doc = " that can be pinned down without racing anything."
doc = " Serializing the parsed struct back would drop `futureField` here, and in"
doc = " the racing case would pair the OLD server URL with the NEW password the"
doc = " keyring just took: the exact combination `merge_settings` refuses to"
doc = " create, arrived at behind its back."

doc = " used to write whatever it had just read — so `\"\"` went out as DELETE and"

doc = " copy already on the remote. Nothing brings that back."
doc = " The fix is that saying nothing about a secret touches nothing, which"
doc = " also means the save still SUCCEEDS: settings that need no credential"
doc = " must not fail because a credential could not be reached. A Linux desktop"
doc = " with no Secret Service running would otherwise be unable to turn config"
doc = " sync off, or change its interval, for as long as it stayed that way."
tests.name: commands::config_sync::webdav_sync::tests::a_save_that_carries_no_secret_leaves_an_unreadable_store_alone

attrs: doc = " The other half: a save that DOES carry a secret still writes it, and an"
doc = " account change still erases the password that no longer belongs to the"
doc = " account — unconditionally, because a store that could not be read may"
doc = " still be holding the old host's copy."
tests.name: commands::config_sync::webdav_sync::tests::a_save_writes_the_secrets_it_was_given_and_erases_an_orphaned_one

attrs: doc = " And when the two copies disagree — the user re-saved a new password"
doc = " after a partial migration — the keyring is the one every save writes to,"
doc = " so it wins and the stale row copy is erased rather than resurrected."

attrs: doc = " Switching encryption on leaves the PLAINTEXT snapshot byte-identical, so"
doc = " the hash alone would say \"already uploaded\" and the remote would keep"
doc = " its unencrypted copy — the user would have turned on a protection that"
doc = " never reached the server. Same shape as the retarget bug, same fix: the"
doc = " baseline records what it was uploaded under."

attrs: doc = " The passphrase is not scoped to the account the way the password is, and"

attrs: doc = " The manifest is the authority on whether the payload is wrapped, and it"

doc = " otherwise a two-file swap (attacker's snapshot + `encryption: \"none\"` +"

doc = " provider endpoints and API keys into the local database."

attrs: doc = " A row written before the target was recorded must not read as \"already"

doc = " card would be stuck on the `running` its ack reported, because the"
doc = " child's real outcome only ever landed on the DB row."
tests.name: commands::conversations::tests::inject_delegation_meta_binds_a_resume_call_by_its_task_id_argument

attrs: doc = " Hosts don't all persist the bare argument object, and a preview is"
doc = " allowed to be cut off. Every shape here reaches `inject_delegation_meta`"
doc = " in practice, and each one that fails to yield an id leaves the reloaded"
doc = " resume card frozen on its own ack with no task text."
tests.name: commands::conversations::tests::parse_resume_task_id_peels_host_wrappers_and_survives_truncation

attrs: doc = " The channel half of a title notification must not be on the caller's"
doc = " critical path: `edit_thread_title` reaches Telegram with a 60s per-call"
doc = " timeout, and `list_all_conversations` is the sidebar's primary read."
tests.name: commands::conversations::tests::notify_conversation_title_updates_detaches_channel_sync_from_the_caller

attrs: doc = " A detached edit can land after a rename that happened while it was in"
doc = " flight. The last value the provider (and the binding's `display_title`)"
doc = " ends up with must be the conversation's CURRENT title, not the one the"
doc = " stalled sync started with — nothing retries afterwards."
tests.name: commands::conversations::tests::detached_title_sync_converges_on_a_rename_that_lands_mid_flight

attrs: doc = " The convergence loop must not be defeated by a RUN of renames that each"
doc = " land mid-flight. Any fixed retry cap exits stale on a long enough run —"
doc = " this drives more consecutive mid-flight renames than any such cap."
tests.name: commands::conversations::tests::detached_title_sync_converges_after_a_run_of_mid_flight_renames

attrs: doc = " After parent teardown, SessionState may still show turn_in_flight while"
doc = " status is terminal. That must not keep a terminal child locked when the"
doc = " durable parent row is already idle."
tests.name: commands::delegate_access::tests::disconnected_parent_with_stale_turn_in_flight_does_not_lock

attrs: doc = " Broker pre-creates a delegate row then spawns child ACP. Early SessionState"
doc = " may have neither conversation_id nor external_id. That must NOT be treated"
doc = " as a brand-new root (which would allow prompt to create a regular row)."
tests.name: commands::delegate_access::tests::effective_guard_fails_closed_for_unbound_delegation_bootstrap

attrs: doc = " Startup applies persisted settings via `set` before any consumer has"
doc = " called `subscribe`. With zero receivers, `Sender::send` drops the value"
doc = " and later subscribers would still see the channel default."
tests.name: commands::delegation::tests::runtime_settings_retain_value_with_zero_subscribers

attrs: doc = " Status-bar / mcp-service toggles only `enabled`. That write must still"
doc = " land on the same live surfaces a settings-page save uses: runtime watch,"
doc = " catalog revision, broker config, and preserved sibling fields/profiles."
tests.name: commands::delegation::tests::enabled_only_toggle_applies_the_same_live_state_as_settings_save

attrs: doc = " Toggle and profile save must serialize on the same lock order so the"
doc = " enabled-only path cannot snapshot stale profiles and write them back"
doc = " over a concurrent catalog save."
tests.name: commands::delegation::tests::concurrent_enabled_toggle_does_not_overwrite_newer_profiles

attrs: doc = " Startup barrier contract: the reconcile helper must run to completion"
doc = " before any open-folder list surface; after it finishes,"
doc = " `list_open_folder_details` must contain no regular opens without"
tests.name: commands::folders::tests::reconcile_empty_open_folders_core_then_list_has_no_empty_regular

attrs: doc = " Surface contract: Tauri command name + JSON `{ closed }` shape (core path"
doc = " shared with the registered `close_folder_if_empty` command)."
tests.name: commands::folders::tests::close_folder_if_empty_result_serializes_closed_field

attrs: doc = " AutoEmpty is visibility-only: never deletes opened tabs, never stops"
doc = " office watches under the folder root, never soft-deletes the folder row,"
doc = " and never removes files from disk."
tests.name: commands::folders::tests::close_folder_if_empty_core_does_not_cascade_tabs_watches_soft_delete_or_disk

attrs: doc = " UserRemove on a non-empty folder still cascades tabs, stops office"
doc = " watches under the root, emits `Close{{UserRemove}}`, leaves"
doc = " `deleted_at` alone (not a history soft-delete), and does not wipe disk."
tests.name: commands::folders::tests::remove_folder_from_workspace_core_cascades_tabs_watches_and_emits_user_remove_for_nonempty

attrs: doc = " A delegated child's `working_dir` is whatever the agent picked — a PR"
doc = " checkout under /tmp, a throwaway worktree. It needs a folder row (the"
doc = " conversation's `folder_id`, and the cwd a resume reads back), but it must"
doc = " not become a project in the user's sidebar. Both cwd lookups ignore"
doc = " `is_open`, so a closed row serves the delegation fully."
tests.name: commands::folders::tests::registration_only_creates_a_closed_row

attrs: doc = " The overwhelmingly common case: the child runs in the same folder as its"
doc = " parent. That folder is already open and must stay exactly as it was —"
doc = " including `last_opened_at`, which orders the folder history and has no"
doc = " business being bumped by a background delegation."
tests.name: commands::folders::tests::registration_only_leaves_an_open_folder_untouched

attrs: doc = " The regression this replaced `add_folder` for: that helper flips"
doc = " `is_open = true` on an existing row, so delegating into a folder the user"
doc = " had closed put it back in their sidebar behind their back."
tests.name: commands::folders::tests::registration_only_does_not_reopen_a_closed_folder

attrs: doc = " `deleted_at` is the one field that must be cleared: both cwd lookups"
doc = " filter on it, so leaving a soft-deleted row deleted would break the very"
doc = " resume the row is created for. Reviving it must still not open it."
tests.name: commands::folders::tests::registration_only_revives_a_soft_deleted_row_but_leaves_it_closed

attrs: doc = " Absent scenario = the kind's historical default, so pre-scenario"
doc = " clients (and the plain \"Start\" path) keep minting the same tasks."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::scenario_defaults_per_kind_and_rejects_the_other_kinds

attrs: doc = " Wire names are snake_case — what the dialog sends — and every one of"
doc = " them survives the round trip through `as_str`."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::scenario_parses_from_wire_names

attrs: doc = " A retired name is REFUSED with something the user can act on, and"
doc = " never remapped: \"investigate only\" asked for a turn that touches no"
doc = " code, and both surviving issue flows may commit. A stale tab must not"
doc = " have its read-only request quietly upgraded into a change-producing"
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::a_retired_scenario_is_refused_by_name_not_remapped

attrs: doc = " Milestone/completion reporting belongs to the engine's \"Work task"
doc = " context\" block, which every launch gets appended — a second, blunter"
doc = " copy here would just contradict its \"if available\" phrasing on agents"
doc = " that never get those tools."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::no_template_mentions_the_reporting_tools

attrs: doc = " Every issue template makes verification a STEP with an outcome, not a"
doc = " preamble: it says the check is required, and it gives the failure"
doc = " branch its own paragraph BEFORE the work, ending in \"stop\". Without"
doc = " that branch an agent reads \"confirm it, then fix it\" as one instruction"
doc = " and produces a fix for a problem it never found — which is exactly what"
doc = " removing the separate \"investigate only\" choice has to keep out."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::the_issue_templates_require_confirmation_before_acting

attrs: doc = " Each scenario states its own goal, and the report ones close their"
doc = " loop: the reply carries the deliverable, and the user can return the"
doc = " task for the follow-up work."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::templates_carry_their_scenario_contract

attrs: doc = " Both review scenarios weigh the DESIGN, not only the diff — a change"
doc = " can be correct line by line and still be unnecessary, built the wrong"
doc = " way, or not ready to run in production, and those are the findings a"
doc = " reviewer is actually wanted for."
doc = " The two differ in what they may then do about it: \"review & fix\" is"
doc = " explicitly fenced off from rewriting the change into its own preferred"
doc = " design (its commits are pushed back to the author's branch), and"
doc = " \"review only\" touches nothing at all."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::the_review_templates_judge_the_approach_and_production_readiness

attrs: doc = " A work task's prompt renders verbatim in the transcript, with the"
doc = " sender's own line breaks and no Markdown — so a bare newline between"
doc = " two paragraphs shows up as one unbroken wall of prose."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::templates_separate_their_paragraphs_with_a_blank_line

attrs: doc = " The dialog's note is the user's own words, so it gets its own section"
doc = " rather than being glued onto the template's last sentence — and onto"
doc = " the envelope block that follows it."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::the_users_note_becomes_a_section_of_its_own

attrs: doc = " The workbench's standing text and this trigger's note are two sections,"
doc = " in that order: policy, then the ask made while looking at this item. A"
doc = " merged section would leave the agent unable to tell which is which."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::standing_instructions_precede_the_note_as_their_own_section

attrs: doc = " The envelope is a separate prompt block appended right after the"
doc = " instruction, and blocks arrive back to back — so the seam between the"
doc = " two must survive without any separator being added between them."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::the_envelope_block_starts_a_line_of_its_own_after_the_note

attrs: doc = " The settings blob keys its standing instructions by SCENARIO WIRE NAME"
doc = " and the trigger looks them up with `ForgeScenario::as_str` — two files"
doc = " agreeing on a string. A rename on either side would not fail to"
doc = " compile; it would quietly stop every configured instruction from"
doc = " applying, which is the kind of silence a user reads as \"it ignored me\"."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::every_scenario_can_be_addressed_from_the_panel_settings

attrs: doc = " The whole chain for the one thing a task does where other people are"
doc = " watching: what the client sent → what gets stored → what the engine's"
doc = " The asymmetry is the point. A checked box sends `true` and comments; an"
doc = " unchecked one sends `false`; a client that never showed the question"
doc = " sends nothing and gets silence — NOT the dialog's default, because a"
doc = " default the user never saw is not consent."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::the_write_back_answer_survives_the_wire_and_defaults_to_silence

attrs: doc = " A row minted before the choice lived on the task carries no field at"
doc = " all, and that absence has to keep meaning \"silent\" — it is what every"
doc = " pre-existing forge task in a user's database looks like."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::source_metadata_without_the_field_reads_as_silent

attrs: doc = " The deliverable flag is what makes the engine swap the commit licence —"
doc = " exactly the reply-deliverable scenarios, never the change ones."
tests.name: commands::forge::tests::report_scenarios_and_only_those_mark_the_report_deliverable

attrs: doc = " No service handle is installed in unit tests, so every report here is"
doc = " the \"socket down\" branch — which is exactly the case that must never"
doc = " offer a start button it cannot honor."
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::reports_stopped_and_unstartable_without_an_installed_handle

attrs: doc = " The socket verdict outranks the tool switches: turning every group on"
doc = " cannot make a dead socket read as running."
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::enabled_groups_do_not_override_a_dead_socket

attrs: doc = " `browser_eval` is reported as a switch of its own so both surfaces that"
doc = " render this list can show it — and reported as belonging to `browser`,"
doc = " so neither has to hardcode that relation. It never reads as on while"
doc = " the group is off, whatever the database says."
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::browser_eval_is_reported_under_the_group_it_belongs_to

attrs: doc = " `browser` and `browser_eval` are two keys of one record, one popover"
doc = " row apart. Each must move on its own: a writer that read the pair and"
doc = " wrote it back would silently revert whichever flip landed first."
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::the_two_browser_switches_do_not_clobber_each_other

attrs: doc = " The popover's per-group switches must go through the same writers the"
doc = " settings window uses, which means a toggle carries the sibling fields"
doc = " forward untouched. `delegation` is the sharp case: its record also holds"
doc = " `depth_limit` and the per-agent defaults, so a writer that sent a fresh"
doc = " struct would reset a user's configured depth on every switch flip."
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::toggling_delegation_preserves_the_rest_of_its_record

attrs: doc = " `automations` and `taskboard` share one settings record, so each must"
doc = " carry the other across — the two switches sit adjacent in the popover"
doc = " and are the likeliest pair to be flipped in sequence."
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::the_two_authoring_switches_do_not_clobber_each_other

attrs: doc = " The sharp version of the case above: the popover leaves every switch"
doc = " but the in-flight one live, so the two authoring toggles can genuinely"
doc = " be in flight together. A writer that read the pair, edited one field and"
doc = " wrote the pair back would drop whichever flip lost the race — both must"
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::concurrent_authoring_flips_both_survive

attrs: doc = " The popover owns one bool per group. Flipping delegation must not"
doc = " republish the rest of that record, which the settings form owns."
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::toggling_delegation_does_not_republish_its_siblings

attrs: doc = " Every slug the status report emits must be writable. A group added to"
doc = " the read side without a matching write arm would render a switch that"
doc = " errors on click, so pin the two lists together."
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::every_reported_group_is_toggleable

attrs: doc = " Two companions on one connection is one session, not two — the popover"
doc = " counts agent sessions, and re-injection can leave an old token behind."
tests.name: commands::mcp_service::tests::counts_companions_and_distinct_sessions

attrs: doc = " Regression: an `api_key` containing a multibyte character (e.g. a"
doc = " full-width char typed under a CJK IME) must not panic the masking in"
doc = " `ModelProviderInfo::from`. Before the fix, `create` persisted the row"
doc = " and then panicked, after which every `list_model_providers` call"
doc = " panicked on that row — breaking the settings list and the agent"
doc = " management provider dropdown until the row was removed."
tests.name: commands::model_provider::tests::create_and_list_tolerate_multibyte_api_key

attrs: doc = " Regression for the model-provider staleness path: editing a provider must"
doc = " flag the running sessions of agents bound to it. The mechanism is \"the"
doc = " bound agent's config fingerprint shifts\" — `refresh_connection_staleness`"
doc = " (tested in manager.rs) then flags any session whose spawn fingerprint no"
doc = " longer matches. This proves the shift actually happens for a credential"
doc = " change, and that a non-runtime edit (display name) does NOT shift it (so"
doc = " DB-only: we mutate the provider row directly via the service rather than"
doc = " `update_model_provider_core`, so the on-disk config cascade never runs and"
doc = " the test can't touch a developer's real agent config files. The fingerprint"
doc = " also reads native config files, but only ever reads them and only between"
doc = " DB mutations, so that component stays constant across the comparisons."
tests.name: commands::model_provider::tests::provider_credential_change_shifts_bound_agent_fingerprint

attrs: doc = " The `?id=` suffix is the difference between landing on the app's own"
doc = " notification page and dumping the user on the list of every app"
doc = " installed, which is what shipped before."
tests.name: commands::notification::tests::macos_deep_links_to_the_delivering_app

attrs: doc = " The fallback is the crate's, not ours — if this constant ever drifts"
doc = " from the literal in `mac-notification-sys`'s swizzled getter, the"
doc = " settings panel starts naming an app that isn't the one receiving the"
tests.name: commands::notification::tests::macos_fallback_matches_the_crate_default

attrs: doc = " On timeout the *whole tree* must die, not just the direct shell — the"
doc = " vendor script downloads the binary in a descendant. Models that with"
doc = " `sh` spawning a long-lived `sleep` grandchild and asserts the grandchild"
tests.name: commands::office_tools::tests::install_timeout_kills_whole_process_tree

attrs: doc = " A `.cmd` shim stays the program. Wrapping it in `cmd /C` by hand would"
doc = " hand the target path to cmd under `CommandLineToArgvW` quoting, which"
doc = " leaves `&` live — see [`spawn_vscode`]. `Command` does the wrapping"
tests.name: commands::open_in::tests::from_binary_keeps_windows_shim_as_the_program

attrs: doc = " `&` is a legal file-name character on every platform codeg ships to, and"
doc = " a cmd command separator on one of them. The teeth are on Windows, where"
doc = " the stub is a `.cmd`: hand-wrapping it in `cmd /C` truncates the argument"
doc = " at the `&` and runs the remainder as a command. Elsewhere the stub is"
doc = " `/bin/sh` reading a quoted `\"$1\"`, so this only pins the arg down."
doc = " The name is deliberately free of whitespace. `append_arg` — the quoting"
doc = " the hand-rolled wrapper would have gotten — quotes on space/tab alone, so"
doc = " a name like `a & b` would come out quoted and survive cmd either way,"
doc = " leaving nothing to discriminate. (Which does assume the temp root itself"
doc = " has no space in it; it doesn't on CI.)"
tests.name: commands::open_in::tests::spawn_passes_shell_metacharacters_through_intact

attrs: doc = " #718: the matrix renders a column per `skills_capable` agent, but the"
doc = " backend snapshot came from a hand-maintained subset. Antigravity had a"
doc = " column and no row, so the authoritative refresh that follows a toggle"
doc = " read the freshly linked cell back as unlinked and flipped it off — and"
doc = " the re-enable then collided with the link the first one had created."
doc = " Both status endpoints must therefore cover every built-in that declares"
doc = " Built-ins only: `all_acp_agents()` also reads the process-global custom"
doc = " rewrites from another test thread."
tests.name: commands::science::tests::supported_agents_cover_every_skills_capable_builtin

attrs: doc = " Regression for the review finding: a timed-out parse must keep occupying its"
doc = " slot until the underlying (uncancelable) work actually finishes — NOT be"
doc = " released the moment the caller gives up waiting."
tests.name: commands::session_info::tests::bounded_parse_holds_permit_past_caller_timeout

attrs: doc = " Turning it on always rewrites the entry. That is what repairs a"
doc = " registration still pointing at an executable the user has since moved,"
doc = " so \"already on\" must not short-circuit into doing nothing."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::autostart_tests::enabling_rewrites_the_entry_even_when_already_enabled
