attrs: doc = " The Windows guard: `disable` there deletes the Run value and errors when"
doc = " it is absent, so turning off an already-off entry must not call it. This"
doc = " is the assertion no macOS or Linux CI box can make against the real"
doc = " backend, which is the whole reason the trait exists."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::autostart_tests::disabling_an_already_disabled_entry_never_calls_unregister

attrs: doc = " The reply is the OS's answer, not an echo of the request: a vetoed"
doc = " registration has to come back as `false` so the switch shows what will"
tests.name: commands::system_settings::autostart_tests::reports_the_state_the_os_settled_on_not_the_request

attrs: doc = " A scheme-less address is what a user actually types, and what used to"
doc = " reach `HTTP_PROXY` verbatim — killing every npm-based agent install with"
doc = " `ERR_INVALID_URL` while codeg's own reqwest calls kept working."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::scheme_less_proxy_addresses_gain_an_http_scheme

attrs: doc = " The repaired value is the user's own string with a prefix, never the"
doc = " `url` crate's re-serialization — which would append a trailing slash and"
doc = " churn what the settings field shows back."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::normalizing_does_not_reserialize_the_address

attrs: doc = " Re-running normalization over its own output must be a no-op: the value"
doc = " is normalized once on save and again on env export."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::normalizing_is_idempotent

attrs: doc = " An address that already names a scheme must survive untouched — most of"
doc = " all a socks proxy, which would stop working if rewritten to `http://`."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::proxy_addresses_with_a_scheme_are_left_alone

attrs: doc = " The repair must not launder a malformed address into a parseable one:"
doc = " `http://` has a scheme separator but no host, so prefixing it would"
doc = " produce `http://http://` and quietly accept it."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::malformed_addresses_are_still_rejected

attrs: doc = " Disabling keeps the stored address as typed: it is only a remembered"
doc = " value at that point, not something exported to a child process."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::disabled_proxy_keeps_its_address_unchanged

attrs: doc = " What actually reaches `HTTP_PROXY` and every spawned agent."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::exported_env_value_carries_the_scheme

attrs: doc = " Commas, semicolons and line breaks all separate entries, so a list"
doc = " pasted from anywhere lands as one canonical list — comma-separated with"
doc = " no spaces, the format the settings page asks for; a repeat keeps its"
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::bypass_list_is_canonicalized_when_the_proxy_is_on

attrs: doc = " The commas a Chinese, Japanese or Arabic keyboard types separate too:"
doc = " no host contains one, and kept inside an entry they would leave a list"
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::bypass_list_takes_the_commas_other_keyboards_type

attrs: doc = " Only the separators change; entries are stored and exported as written."
doc = " `*.corp.example.com` stays distinct from `.corp.example.com`: most tools"
doc = " read the dot form as `corp.example.com` itself too, the one host the"
doc = " star form leaves on the proxy."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::a_star_dot_entry_is_kept_as_written

attrs: doc = " The page shows back whatever the save returns, so a list typed before"
doc = " the proxy is switched on reads in the same canonical form. (That the"
doc = " disabled path still never validates is pinned by the control-character"
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::bypass_list_is_canonicalized_while_the_proxy_is_off_too

attrs: doc = " A control character cannot name a host, and a NUL in the exported value"
doc = " would make the env write panic. Disabling still never validates, so a"
doc = " bad list can always be switched off, like a bad address."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::bypass_list_with_a_control_character_is_rejected_only_while_exported

attrs: doc = " What reaches `NO_PROXY` next to the proxy: the loopback hosts first —"
doc = " always, so an agent's own local services stay reachable through a proxy"
doc = " on another machine — then the settings' list."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::exported_bypass_list_leads_with_the_loopback_hosts

attrs: doc = " Enabling writes the bypass list next to the proxy, in both spellings —"
doc = " the child processes that read it disagree on which one comes first."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::enabling_the_proxy_exports_the_bypass_list

attrs: doc = " Disabling removes the bypass list along with the proxy it was written"
doc = " for, so a stale list cannot outlive its settings."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::disabling_the_proxy_removes_the_bypass_list_too

attrs: doc = " `*` bypasses everything, but Python and curl only honour it as the"
doc = " whole value, so it is never exported inside a list."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::a_wildcard_bypass_is_exported_alone

attrs: doc = " Rows written by a build that stored the address verbatim must heal on"
doc = " read, so startup exports a usable value without a migration."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::stored_scheme_less_proxy_heals_on_load

attrs: doc = " The command-color opt-in survives a save AND a restart, and reaches the"
doc = " launch env both times — a value that only persisted would leave every"
doc = " connection made before the next restart on the wrong setting."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::colorize_command_output_persists_and_reaches_the_launch_env

attrs: doc = " The line under the picker reads `effective_shell_for_display`, so it"
doc = " has to answer for the SELECTION, not only for the host. Reporting the"
doc = " system shell unconditionally is what made every row in the dropdown"
doc = " — pwsh, powershell, a custom path — read back as the same"
doc = " `COMSPEC`/`SHELL` value, which is precisely the state where a user"
doc = " concludes the setting does nothing."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::the_reported_shell_follows_the_selection

attrs: doc = " `CreateProcessW` appends `.exe` to an extension-less path, so"
doc = " has to find that `.exe`. The display resolver does not invent a file it"
doc = " cannot stat; it echoes the stored path."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::an_extension_less_windows_path_resolves_the_way_it_launches

attrs: doc = " The picker and the line under it are built from one probe, so a shell"
doc = " the host cannot find must never be badged \"installed\" while its path is"
doc = " reported as resolved (or the reverse)."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::the_option_badges_agree_with_the_reported_shell

attrs: doc = " A row stored before the field existed must load as \"off\" rather than"
doc = " failing to parse (which would strand the user's shell choice too)."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::tests::terminal_settings_row_without_the_color_field_loads_as_off

attrs: doc = " The close button is the user's last exit. A row this build cannot parse"
doc = " — hand-edited, written by a newer build, or truncated — must degrade to"
doc = " \"ask\", never to an error that leaves the window unclosable."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::close_behavior_tests::corrupt_close_behavior_falls_back_to_ask

attrs: doc = " The close handler is a synchronous callback and reads the atomic, not"
doc = " the database — so a save that updates only the row would be invisible"
tests.name: commands::system_settings::close_behavior_tests::cache_reflects_update

attrs: doc = " Seeding is what makes the preference survive a restart: the atomic"
doc = " starts at its default every launch, so a missing seed would silently"
doc = " serve \"ask\" to a user who picked \"exit\" months ago."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::close_behavior_tests::startup_seeding_loads_persisted_behavior

attrs: doc = " The de-dup flag: one prompt at a time, and the claim is reusable only"
doc = " after it is given back. Without this the close button — which stays"
doc = " clickable while the dialog is up — stacks one dialog per press."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::close_behavior_tests::close_prompt_claim_is_exclusive_until_released

attrs: doc = " The backstop for every way a prompt can fail to reach a dialog that the"
doc = " readiness flag cannot see — including the one it provably cannot rule"
doc = " out, where wry runs the close handler's emit inline on the main thread"
doc = " ahead of a listener registration still queued on the event-loop proxy."
doc = " Whatever the cause, the press after the grace has to act."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::close_behavior_tests::an_unanswered_close_prompt_expires_and_hands_the_press_back

attrs: doc = " A claim younger than the grace is a dialog the user is still reading."
doc = " Expiring it would exit (or hide) out from under them."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::close_behavior_tests::a_fresh_close_prompt_is_never_expired

attrs: doc = " `main` is visible before its webview has a listener, and an emit into"
doc = " that gap looks successful. The close handler asks this first, so the"
doc = " press falls through to the preference instead of disappearing."
tests.name: commands::system_settings::close_behavior_tests::listener_readiness_starts_false_and_is_raised_by_the_dialog

attrs: doc = " Failed persistence must leave the live registry on its prior settings."
tests.name: commands::tool_watchdog::tests::failed_persist_leaves_live_settings_unchanged

attrs: doc = " Concurrent saves serialize write+apply; final live matches durable."
tests.name: commands::tool_watchdog::tests::concurrent_settings_saves_keep_live_and_durable_aligned

attrs: doc = " Shared Rust/TS test vector — the TypeScript implementation must"
tests.name: commands::turn_window::tests::fingerprint_shared_test_vector

attrs: doc = " Every section the frontend's `SettingsSection` union can send must map"
doc = " to a real route. `general` is the one that looks redundant and is not:"
doc = " the fallback below it is Appearance, so a caller wanting the General"
doc = " page must be able to name it and land there. `collaboration` is where"
doc = " the codeg-mcp tool switches live in full, and it is what the status-bar"
tests.name: commands::windows::settings_route_tests::every_named_settings_section_resolves_to_its_own_route

attrs: doc = " Linux (and Windows) fullscreen is not a separate Space. Close must"
doc = " not wait on it, or a maximized window would take the settle delay on"
tests.name: commands::windows::macos_fullscreen_close_tests::non_macos_never_drains_fullscreen

attrs: doc = " The flag is up for the whole of a user-driven exit animation (tao"
doc = " only clears it in `windowDidExitFullScreen`), so it is also what"
doc = " covers a close pressed mid-animation. Windowed must not drain: that"
doc = " would put the settle delay on every ordinary close."
tests.name: commands::windows::macos_fullscreen_close_tests::macos_drains_exactly_while_the_fullscreen_flag_is_up

attrs: doc = " The drain is claimed once and answered once: a second press while one"
doc = " is in flight is dropped rather than queueing a second hide. And while"
doc = " it is in flight it stays observable, because tao's fullscreen flag is"
doc = " already down by then and would otherwise read as \"nothing to wait for\"."
tests.name: commands::windows::macos_fullscreen_close_tests::a_drain_claim_is_exclusive_and_observable_until_released

attrs: doc = " The list must name each task's agent the way the ENGINE would pick it"
doc = " (`effective_agent_config`), or the views draw a mark for an agent that"
doc = " never runs. Walks the layering from the outside in."
tests.name: commands::work_task::tests::agent_type_is_stamped_with_the_engines_own_layering

attrs: doc = " A folder with no default and no settings anywhere leaves the field"
doc = " empty rather than guessing — the same state the engine refuses to"
doc = " launch, which both views draw as a placeholder."
tests.name: commands::work_task::tests::agent_type_is_none_when_nothing_is_configured

attrs: doc = " Renaming a card renames the session it produced: the two must not drift"
doc = " apart, or the sidebar goes back to showing a name nothing on the board"
tests.name: commands::work_task::tests::renaming_a_task_renames_the_session_it_produced

attrs: doc = " …but a session the user named themselves keeps that name. Both titles"
doc = " are `title_locked`, so only the card's PREVIOUS name can tell \"still in"
doc = " sync\" from \"the user picked this\"."
tests.name: commands::work_task::tests::renaming_a_task_leaves_a_hand_named_session_alone

attrs: doc = " A task's session CAN own a chat-channel thread: Telegram's `/resume <id>`"
doc = " takes any conversation id and binds it to the forum topic it was typed"
doc = " in (`chat_channel/session_commands.rs::handle_resume`). So the rename has"
doc = " to walk the same channel-sync path a manual rename does — a locked title"
doc = " never passes through the auto-title backfill that would otherwise"
doc = " re-sync the topic, so skipping it here would strand the topic name"
doc = " The remote edit itself is not observable here (a bare manager has no"
doc = " backend registered, so the sync stops at `NotFound` without touching the"
doc = " network); what this pins is that the path is wired, reached with a real"
doc = " binding in place, and leaves the binding row intact."
tests.name: commands::work_task::tests::renaming_a_task_syncs_a_bound_session_through_the_channel_path

attrs: doc = " A card that never ran has no session to follow it — the edit must still"
doc = " succeed, untouched by the propagation path."
tests.name: commands::work_task::tests::renaming_a_task_without_a_session_is_harmless

attrs: doc = " Drive this migration's `up` against a minimal stand-in of the"
doc = " `conversation` table and assert the legacy backfill locks exactly the"
doc = " rows that already have a title."
tests.name: db::migration::m20260608_000001_conversation_title_locked::tests::up_locks_preexisting_titled_rows_only

attrs: doc = " `up` adds a nullable `pinned_at` column; pre-existing rows default to NULL"
tests.name: db::migration::m20260610_000001_conversation_pinned_at::tests::up_adds_nullable_pinned_at_defaulting_null

attrs: doc = " Apply every migration except this one, seed legacy-shaped rows via raw"
doc = " SQL (the entities already reflect the post-migration schema), then run"
doc = " the remainder and assert the backfill: chat folder → kind='chat';"
doc = " delegation child → 'delegate' (even inside a chat folder); top-level"
tests.name: db::migration::m20260612_000001_conversation_folder_kind::tests::backfills_folder_and_conversation_kind

attrs: doc = " Agents registered before this column existed were all forwarded MCP, so"
doc = " the migration must leave them that way — a default of `false` would"
doc = " silently drop the codeg-mcp companion (delegation, live feedback, task"
doc = " tools) out of every existing custom agent's session."
tests.name: db::migration::m20260808_000001_custom_agent_supports_mcp::tests::up_defaults_existing_rows_to_forwarding_mcp

attrs: doc = " Drive `up` against minimal stand-ins of the two tables and assert the"
doc = " backfill touches exactly the sessions a card produced and never renamed"
tests.name: db::migration::m20260817_000001_work_task_conversation_title::tests::up_renames_only_unlocked_task_sessions

attrs: doc = " The cap must count CHARACTERS, not bytes — SQLite's `substr` does, which"
doc = " is what makes it agree with the engine's `conversation_title_for_task`."
tests.name: db::migration::m20260817_000001_work_task_conversation_title::tests::up_caps_a_long_title_at_eighty_characters

attrs: doc = " Regression for the day-of-week off-by-one: a weekly cron must fire on the"
doc = " weekday the UI label promises (UI 0=Sun..6=Sat), not a day early."
tests.name: db::service::automation_service::tests::compute_next_run_weekly_lands_on_intended_weekday

attrs: doc = " The \"weekdays\" preset (`1-5`) must fire Mon–Fri only, never Sat/Sun."
tests.name: db::service::automation_service::tests::compute_next_run_weekdays_preset_excludes_weekend

attrs: doc = " Neither auto-title primitive may write a soft-deleted row. Both are now"
doc = " driven from the live ACP path (a title can land while the user is"
doc = " deleting the conversation), and a late write to a deleted row is a"
doc = " resurrection the sidebar can never show — `emit_conversation_upsert`"
doc = " filters it out, so the row would silently diverge from every client."
tests.name: db::service::conversation_service::tests::auto_title_writes_skip_soft_deleted_rows

attrs: doc = " The work-task / automation launch path: the seed IS the name, so locking"
doc = " must keep the title byte-identical, keep the row where it is in a"
doc = " recency-sorted sidebar, and make the next auto-title a no-op."
tests.name: db::service::conversation_service::tests::lock_title_freezes_the_seed_without_rewriting_or_bumping

attrs: doc = " A missing row must not be an error — the caller locks on a best-effort"
doc = " path where a failure would be worse than the drift it prevents."
tests.name: db::service::conversation_service::tests::lock_title_on_a_missing_row_is_a_no_op

attrs: doc = " The guard that makes the sync safe: once the user names the conversation"
doc = " themselves, the owner's rename must not reach it. `title_locked` is true"
doc = " in BOTH cases, so only the expected-value comparison can tell them apart."
tests.name: db::service::conversation_service::tests::retitle_if_unchanged_refuses_after_a_manual_rename

attrs: doc = " Parent-end durable settle may project a pure provisional shell to"
doc = " canceled before abandon reclaims the run. Step 1 must rewrite that"
doc = " shell to `provisional_admission_rejected` so Step 2 can hide it."
tests.name: db::service::conversation_service::tests::terminalize_provisional_child_rewrites_parent_end_canceled_shell

attrs: doc = " Sequencing proof for the startup readiness barrier: after bulk reconcile"
doc = " completes, `list_open_folder_details` (the client open-list surface) must"
doc = " not include any regular folder with zero sidebar-visible root conversations."
tests.name: db::service::folder_service::tests::reconcile_then_list_open_folder_details_has_no_empty_regular

attrs: doc = " Deterministic UNIQUE recovery: pre-insert the winner, then force"
doc = " `add_folder` to skip find and re-insert so the recovery branch runs."
tests.name: db::service::folder_service::tests::add_folder_recovers_from_unique_constraint_after_forced_skip_find

attrs: doc = " Path-keyed inject: unguarded ensure_folder on another path must not"
doc = " consume the armed path's skip budget (parallel-cargo safety)."
tests.name: db::service::folder_service::tests::skip_existing_inject_is_path_scoped_not_stolen_by_other_paths

attrs: doc = " Service-level composition only. Production call sites are covered by"
tests.name: db::service::folder_service::tests::registration_only_does_not_open_when_hidden_child_would_use_path

attrs: doc = " The upgrade path, which is every existing install: rows written before"
doc = " the `headers` column existed. `ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` has to"
doc = " backfill them — a NULL there fails to deserialize into `Model.headers:"
doc = " String` and takes the whole connection list down, not just the headers."
doc = " The insert omits `headers` exactly the way the old schema did."
tests.name: db::service::remote_workspace_connection_service::tests::list_reads_a_row_written_without_the_headers_column

attrs: doc = " The card's live note line: whose news it is, and what it says while a"
doc = " round is parked on its pre-prompt compaction."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::the_live_note_belongs_to_the_current_generation

attrs: doc = " `preparing` is a live status for the note line: a resumed round spends"
doc = " it on the compaction turn, which is the whole reason the line exists."
doc = " A generation that never compacted must not inherit the last one's"
doc = " dangling `started` (a launch killed mid-compaction leaves one)."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::a_preparing_round_reports_its_own_compaction_only

attrs: doc = " What a `preparing` row's `connection_id` is allowed to mean: the LIVE"
doc = " connection of the setup in progress, or nothing at all. Never the"
doc = " previous generation's, which is dead by the time a new one is claimed —"
doc = " a viewer that streams this status (the pre-prompt compaction is a real"
doc = " agent turn) would otherwise open onto a connection that is gone."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::a_preparing_row_names_the_live_connection_or_none

attrs: doc = " #649: start, cancel, requeue, start again used to land the task in"
doc = " `canceled`. The requeue kept the conversation of the run the user had"
doc = " just stopped, and `launch_mode_for` reads exactly that column to pick"
doc = " `Retry` over `Fresh`, so the second start resumed the killed session"
doc = " instead of running the task, on a conversation row still recorded as"
doc = " `cancelled`, which the reconcile sweep then read as this generation's"
doc = " verdict. A requeue puts the task back on the board, so it keeps the"
doc = " worktree and drops the session."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::a_requeue_drops_the_canceled_run_s_conversation

attrs: doc = " A plan must not outlive the task's stay in `todo`: cancel drops it, so"
doc = " a requeue weeks later cannot launch an agent at a time nobody remembers"
doc = " setting. And a claim — from any arm — invalidates the previous run's"
doc = " self-reported verdict, which the settle path reads as this generation's."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::a_claim_or_a_cancel_consumes_the_plan_and_the_stale_verdict

attrs: doc = " The reason the user gave when stopping a task rides the `canceled`"
doc = " status event, which is what the drawer's timeline renders under the"
doc = " phase header. Blank input must leave the payload alone — an empty"
doc = " `reason` key would render as a stray empty line."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::a_cancel_reason_rides_the_status_event

attrs: doc = " `done` no longer means one thing, so every writer of it has to say"
doc = " which ending this was — a NULL `completion_kind` on a fresh row would"
doc = " make the board guess again."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::each_ending_records_how_the_task_finished

attrs: doc = " A delivery's whole lifecycle at the service layer: the CAS that starts"
doc = " it, what it keeps and clears, and the settle that records the pull"
doc = " request on the row the issue list reads back."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::a_delivery_starts_settles_and_binds_to_its_own_generation

attrs: doc = " The auto-merge bookkeeping: a refused dispatch leaves its banner on the"
doc = " review row (generation-guarded, and the stop that keeps auto-merge from"
doc = " retrying a hopeless dispatch forever), and a dispatched auto merge"
doc = " records \"auto\" as the actor who pulled the trigger."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::auto_merge_marks_actor_and_banners_refused_dispatches

attrs: doc = " The lock-wait race of the no-auto-retry invariant: two unattended"
doc = " sweeps pick the same review generation, the first dispatch fails after"
doc = " bumping it, and the second — queued on the folder lock with the"
doc = " pre-failure snapshot — must not redispatch. Its stale generation"
doc = " misses the CAS, and even a fresh re-listing is stopped by the banner;"
doc = " only a user dispatch reopens the row."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::auto_merge_never_retries_a_failed_generation

attrs: doc = " The parked column is the ONLY carrier of the user's extra merge"
doc = " instructions between the dialog and the pump's later dispatch — a drop"
doc = " anywhere along park → column → parse → wire loses what they asked for"
doc = " with no trace on the card or the timeline."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::a_queued_merge_carries_the_users_extra_instructions

attrs: doc = " The merge queue's row-level contract: an intent only lands on the exact"
doc = " review generation the caller validated, it survives on the row until"
doc = " something spends it, and a dispatch (from the pump or from a click that"
doc = " found the slot free) consumes it."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::a_queued_merge_is_generation_bound_and_spent_by_the_dispatch

attrs: doc = " The pump scans the queue, then spends real time on it — a worktree"
doc = " stat, the folder git lock, three git subprocesses — before the CAS that"
doc = " spends the intent. A user can withdraw or edit the merge anywhere in"
doc = " that window WITHOUT moving `run_seq`, so the intent itself is the token:"
doc = " every write the pump makes demands the column still equal what it"
doc = " scanned. Without this, a withdrawn merge still landed on the base"
doc = " branch, and a refusal could delete an edit made a moment earlier."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::a_queued_dispatch_loses_to_a_withdrawal_or_an_edit_under_it

attrs: doc = " Withdrawing a queued merge: only from review, only when something is"
doc = " actually queued (so a withdrawal that lost the race to the pump reports"
doc = " the miss), and the engine's silent variant leaves no timeline entry."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::unqueue_merge_is_guarded_and_the_silent_clear_is_not

attrs: doc = " A task that leaves review by any door drops its place in the merge"
doc = " queue with it — a follow-up, a stop, or an outright completion must not"
doc = " leave an intent the pump would later dispatch."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::leaving_review_drops_the_queued_merge

attrs: doc = " A task that changed nothing finishes without a merge commit — from"
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::complete_without_merge_lands_done_from_review_only

attrs: doc = " The forge path is the only writer of the source columns; the public"
doc = " create leaves them NULL, and the dedup guard turns a second trigger"
doc = " into a `Duplicate` answer unless the user forces a second live task."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::forge_create_writes_source_and_dedups_active

attrs: doc = " A finished task is history, not a blocker: dedup only counts the"
doc = " ACTIVE set, so re-triggering a done issue creates a fresh card."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::forge_dedup_ignores_terminal_tasks

attrs: doc = " Editing a forge task keeps its provenance intact and refuses a folder"
doc = " move — the folder was validated against the source repo at trigger"
doc = " time, and a move would silently void that check."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::forge_task_update_keeps_source_and_pins_folder

attrs: doc = " `deliverable` is trigger-owned and no editor shows it, so an edit whose"
doc = " config OMITS the key must keep the stored value — dropping it would"
doc = " silently hand a report task the write licence back. An explicit null is"
doc = " a statement, not ignorance, and still clears it."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::update_preserves_the_stored_deliverable_unless_explicitly_cleared

attrs: doc = " The write-first transaction shape under real concurrency: a file-backed"
doc = " WAL database (multi-connection pool, like production) and two"
doc = " simultaneous `force=false` triggers must yield exactly one `Created`"
doc = " and one `Duplicate` — never `database is locked`. This is the exact"
doc = " failure a dedup-SELECT-before-first-write shape produced (deferred"
doc = " read→write upgrade loses under WAL instead of waiting)."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::concurrent_forge_creates_yield_one_created_one_duplicate

attrs: doc = " Resurrection guards on BOTH roads back into the active set: a failed"
doc = " retry claim and a canceled requeue must refuse while another active"
doc = " task holds the same source key — and the explicit override waives it."
tests.name: db::service::work_task_service::tests::resurrection_guards_block_and_override_waives

attrs: doc = " The `url` crate lower-cases a URL's host before `event.urls()` hands it"
doc = " over, but an argv-delivered link keeps the caller's casing, so the"
doc = " `session` segment must match either way. The ref after it must not — an"
tests.name: deep_link::tests::session_segment_is_case_insensitive_but_the_ref_is_not

attrs: doc = " Nothing stops an agent from issuing all-digit session ids, so an"
doc = " all-digit ref that matches no live primary key must still be tried as"
doc = " an `external_id` rather than reported as a dead link."
tests.name: deep_link::tests::numeric_ref_falls_back_to_external_id

attrs: doc = " The parked-target handoff that carries a macOS cold start, where the"
doc = " `workspace://focus-conversation` emit lands before the webview listens."
doc = " Single test on purpose: `PENDING_FOCUS` is process-global."
tests.name: deep_link::tests::pending_focus_is_taken_exactly_once

attrs: doc = " GitLab mounts its API under the instance itself — public and"
doc = " self-hosted alike, there is no `api.gitlab.com`."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::gitlab_api_base_is_always_under_the_instance

attrs: doc = " Gitea mounts at `/api/v1`, and — unlike GitHub — there is no public"
doc = " service with a dedicated API host to exempt. gitea.com and codeberg.org"
doc = " answer under their own origins like every self-hosted instance does."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::gitea_api_base_is_v1_under_the_instance

attrs: doc = " The user's own accounts decide what a host is; the hostname only gets a"
doc = " vote when nothing is declared, and GitHub stays the last resort so"
doc = " every existing install keeps behaving exactly as it did."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_hosts_forge_comes_from_its_accounts_first

attrs: doc = " The GitHub fallback is a GUESS, and a host it was guessed for is not a"
doc = " host codeg can read. Saying which is which is the whole point of"
doc = " `recognized`: a Bitbucket or Gitee remote resolves to the same"
doc = " well-formed `(github, host, owner/repo)` triple a GitHub Enterprise"
doc = " does, and only this flag separates \"your account is missing\" from \"that"
doc = " is not a forge we speak\"."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_guessed_host_is_marked_unrecognized

attrs: doc = " The advice a failed auth resolution gives has to be advice that can"
doc = " work. \"Add a GitHub account for gitee.com\" is not — no such account"
doc = " would make the read succeed — so a host nothing vouches for is refused"
doc = " as unsupported instead, and only a host that IS one of the two gets the"
doc = " actionable \"you have no account here\"."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::an_unvouched_for_host_is_refused_as_unsupported_not_as_a_missing_account

attrs: doc = " Whole labels only, in both directions — the same rule the provider"
doc = " guess has always used. `mygitlabhost.com` is somebody's domain."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_hostname_claims_a_forge_only_by_whole_label

attrs: doc = " What the instance itself said vouches for it, exactly as an account or a"
doc = " forge-claiming name does. Without this the two halves of the forge work"
doc = " contradict each other on the SAME host: `host_profile` marks a detected"
doc = " GitLab `recognized` — which is what lets the panel spend a request on it"
doc = " — and this function then answers that request with \"not a forge codeg"
doc = " speaks\", about an instance the probe positively identified. What the"
doc = " user is actually missing is an account, and that is the actionable"
doc = " Neither half had this alone: without the probe such a host was never"
doc = " `recognized`, so no request was spent and nothing contradicted anything."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_detected_forge_is_vouched_for_even_when_nothing_else_speaks_for_the_host

attrs: doc = " A GitLab mounted under a relative URL root (`https://host/gitlab`) puts"
doc = " that prefix in front of every repository path a git remote carries,"
doc = " while no API path has it. Without stripping, the project addressed over"
doc = " REST would be `gitlab%2Fgroup%2Fproj` — a project that does not exist —"
doc = " and the push URL would repeat the prefix twice."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::an_instance_mount_path_is_learned_from_its_account_and_stripped

attrs: doc = " A GitLab token handed to the GitHub client buys a 401 that reads like"
doc = " an expired credential. Declared accounts serve only their own forge;"
doc = " undeclared ones serve whatever the host is."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::accounts_only_serve_the_forge_they_declare

attrs: doc = " Error paths never touch the token store, so they are safe to assert in"
doc = " BOTH modes (the happy path needs a token and is covered below in the"
doc = " server-mode-only test — the desktop build would write the real OS"
doc = " keyring, which a unit test must never do)."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::resolution_rejects_wrong_host_and_missing_accounts

attrs: doc = " Server mode only: the file-backed token store can be pointed at a temp"
doc = " dir. Desktop would hit the real OS keyring — never in a unit test."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::resolution_prefers_pinned_id_then_default_and_redacts_debug

attrs: doc = " The whole point: a GitLab that is NOT called `gitlab.*`. The hostname"
doc = " says GitHub, the instance says otherwise, and the instance wins — which"
doc = " is what stops `/api/v3` (and its 410) from ever being requested."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::an_instance_that_serves_v4_is_detected_as_gitlab

attrs: doc = " No `/api/v4` means \"not a GitLab\", which is NOT the same as \"a GitHub\":"
doc = " the caller keeps its existing guess."
doc = " The host ANSWERED though, so that is recorded — `folder_forge_remote_core`"
doc = " runs on every forge call, and without a cached negative every GitHub"
doc = " Enterprise request would carry a fresh probe."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_host_without_v4_leaves_the_guess_alone

attrs: doc = " An SSO portal in front of a GitHub Enterprise can answer 401 to"
doc = " anything — but it answers with a login page. Requiring JSON is what"
doc = " keeps that from being read as \"this is a GitLab\"."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::an_html_401_is_not_a_gitlab

attrs: doc = " The regression this guards: a gateway that answers JSON 401 to EVERY"
doc = " path. It is indistinguishable from GitLab on `/api/v4/version` alone, so"
doc = " believing that one answer would move a working GitHub Enterprise onto"
doc = " the GitLab client and break it. A real API 404s a path it does not"
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_gateway_that_401s_everything_is_not_taken_for_a_gitlab

attrs: doc = " A GitLab that is mid-deploy answers 502 through its own reverse proxy."
doc = " That is \"ask again later\", NOT \"not a GitLab\" — recording it would pin"
doc = " the host to the hostname guess until codeg restarts, which is the exact"
doc = " failure this detection exists to remove."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_transient_server_error_is_not_a_verdict

attrs: doc = " The cache has THREE states, and the middle one is the one worth having:"
doc = " \"asked, and it is not a GitLab\" is what stops a GitHub Enterprise from"
doc = " re-probing on every call, while \"never got an answer\" has to stay"
doc = " distinct from it so an unreachable host is re-asked instead of pinned to"
doc = " the hostname guess for the life of the process."
doc = " Exercised through the recorder rather than through a dead port: this"
doc = " machine may sit behind a proxy, which answers for unreachable origins"
doc = " and would make a connection-level test assert the proxy's behaviour."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::the_cache_tells_a_negative_verdict_apart_from_no_verdict

attrs: doc = " What `github::finish` does when GitLab announces itself in a 410: the"
doc = " answer is remembered, so the probe is not even consulted next time and"
doc = " an unreachable origin cannot undo the correction."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_remembered_forge_short_circuits_the_probe

attrs: doc = " The public hosts are decided by name and never probed — a round trip"
doc = " per panel load to learn something already known."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::the_public_hosts_are_never_probed

attrs: doc = " The Gitea equivalent of the GitLab probe, and the reason it goes FIRST:"
doc = " `/api/v1/version` needs no credential, so a self-hosted instance whose"
doc = " name says nothing identifies itself before a single token is spent."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::an_instance_that_announces_a_version_on_v1_is_detected_as_gitea

attrs: doc = " The BODY is what concludes it, not the status. A proxy that answers 200"
doc = " JSON to every path — the mirror image of the 401 gateway the GitLab"
doc = " control request exists to catch — carries no `version`, so it is not"
doc = " taken for a Gitea, and the probe falls through to the GitLab question"
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_json_200_without_a_version_is_not_a_gitea

attrs: doc = " A Gitea mid-restart answers 502 through whatever sits in front of it."
doc = " That has to stay \"ask again later\" on the FIRST probe too — recording it"
doc = " would pin the host to the hostname guess for the life of the process,"
doc = " and never even ask the GitLab question."
tests.name: forge::auth::tests::a_transient_answer_to_the_gitea_probe_is_not_a_verdict

attrs: doc = " The delivery error string is the only thing a human sees when a push"
doc = " fails, and `classify_remote_git_error` files everything specific under"
doc = " `detail`. `Display` prints `message` alone, so flattening has to reach"
doc = " for the detail explicitly or the reader is left with \"git push failed\"."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::a_flattened_git_failure_keeps_what_git_said

attrs: doc = " Git echoes the remote URL in its errors, and `web_origin` hands back a"
doc = " self-hosted `server_url` verbatim — so credentials a user typed into"
doc = " their own forge address would otherwise come back out in a string that"
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::a_flattened_failure_blanks_credentials_git_echoed_back

attrs: doc = " This string is persisted and rendered, and the detail is another"
doc = " program's output — a hook that answers a push with a banner must not"
doc = " land in the database whole. Multi-byte input is the case that would"
doc = " panic if the cut were taken on bytes."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::a_flattened_failure_bounds_a_runaway_detail

attrs: doc = " The whole point of the four-way match: one commit, two pull requests"
doc = " aimed at different bases. Settling on the OID alone would link the task"
doc = " to whichever came back first."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::same_head_against_another_base_is_not_adopted

attrs: doc = " GitHub answers with canonical casing, our keys are lowercase — an exact"
doc = " repo compare here would reject the task's own pull request as a fork's."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::canonical_casing_still_matches_the_same_repo

attrs: doc = " None of these may be ADOPTED — but they split two ways for what happens"
doc = " next. A pull request already open on this exact branch AND base blocks"
doc = " creation (GitHub allows one per head/base pair), so it has to be told"
doc = " apart from a candidate that leaves the pair free."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::near_misses_are_never_adopted_and_a_blocked_pair_is_named

attrs: doc = " A merged match outranks anything else — if the pull request already"
doc = " landed, the delivery succeeded and must not open a duplicate."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::merged_outranks_open_and_closed

attrs: doc = " `merged` is derived from `merged_at`, because the LIST endpoint does not"
doc = " send a `merged` boolean at all. Getting this wrong would make recovery"
doc = " bounce deliveries whose pull request had already landed."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::listed_pulls_report_merged_from_merged_at

attrs: doc = " \"No commits between…\" is the 422 an empty delivery earns. It has to"
doc = " surface as a readable API error, not a panic or a generic network error."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::empty_delivery_surfaces_the_422

attrs: doc = " The trigger gate answers one question: when the agent finishes, is"
doc = " there anywhere for its commits to go? A task that cannot be delivered"
doc = " cannot be merged locally either, so it would strand in review."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::only_pull_requests_with_somewhere_to_deliver_can_be_worked_on

attrs: doc = " A pull request by number is what turns \"PR #7\" into something"
doc = " checkoutable — the list rows the workbench shows carry no refs at all."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::a_pull_request_is_looked_up_by_number

attrs: doc = " The write-back goes to `/issues/{n}/comments` — the endpoint that"
doc = " comments on issues AND pull requests. `/pulls/{n}/comments` would be a"
doc = " review comment on a diff line and would 422 without a position."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::a_write_back_posts_to_the_issue_comments_endpoint

attrs: doc = " The comment says what happened, in numbers and links. Nothing an agent"
doc = " wrote can appear in a thread other people are reading."
tests.name: forge::deliver::tests::the_write_back_body_is_numbers_and_links_only

attrs: doc = " The block opens with a blank line and its own header, so it reads as a"
doc = " section of its own wherever it is placed after the instruction block —"
doc = " including where the two are concatenated with no separator."
tests.name: forge::envelope::tests::the_block_opens_with_its_own_header_line

attrs: doc = " The classic breakout: the body fakes a fence-close, injects"
doc = " \"instructions\", then fakes a reopen. Escaping the stem neutralizes"
doc = " every fake — exactly one real begin and one real end survive."
tests.name: forge::envelope::tests::body_cannot_fake_fence_lines

attrs: doc = " The list, end to end: the `type=` split that makes real page numbers"
doc = " possible, `X-Total-Count` as the total, `Link: rel=\"next\"` as the only"
doc = " thing that says another page exists, and the row mapping."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::the_list_splits_by_type_and_pages_on_the_headers

attrs: doc = " Gitea has no merged STATE — a merged pull request reports `closed`, and"
doc = " only `pull_request.merged` tells them apart. Painting one \"closed\" is"
doc = " the whole failure this covers; the draft beside it is the other fact"
doc = " that only exists under that key on this payload."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::the_pr_tab_derives_merged_and_draft_from_the_pull_request_key

attrs: doc = " \"Assigned to me\" is a literal login (there is no `@me` here), resolved"
doc = " through `/user` and CACHED — otherwise every click on the pill spends a"
doc = " request to learn a name that cannot change."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::assigned_to_me_resolves_the_login_once_and_filters_by_it

attrs: doc = " The label filter's vocabulary. `truncated` has to come from the count"
doc = " header: Gitea clamps `limit` to its own maximum (50 by default), so \"we"
doc = " asked for 100 and got 100\" is a test that never fires, and a repository"
doc = " with 140 labels would silently look complete."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::labels_report_truncation_from_the_count_not_from_a_full_page

attrs: doc = " The comment collection is UNPAGINATED — Gitea hands over every comment"
doc = " there is — so the page is cut here, and `has_next` is a fact about the"
doc = " slice rather than a header to trust."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::comments_are_paged_locally_because_gitea_sends_them_all

attrs: doc = " The composer's own write, through the same mapper the reader uses: what"
doc = " the panel appends has to be one object with what the next page brings,"
doc = " or the optimistic append shows a second copy of what was just posted."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_posted_comment_comes_back_as_the_forge_stored_it

attrs: doc = " Two endpoints, picked by kind. `/pulls/{n}` is not interchangeable with"
doc = " `/issues/{n}` here: only its response carries `merged`, and a change"
doc = " somebody merged while the panel was open comes back merged rather than"
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_state_change_uses_the_right_collection_and_adopts_the_answer

attrs: doc = " Exact before loose. A repository holding two labels that differ only by"
doc = " case would otherwise get whichever one the page happened to list first —"
doc = " and the name being resolved came from a chip that showed exactly one of"
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_label_name_resolves_to_its_exact_match_before_a_loose_one

attrs: doc = " Gitea applies labels to a new issue by ID, so the names the dialog"
doc = " collected have to be resolved first. A name the repository does not have"
doc = " is dropped rather than refused — the same thing GitHub does with one,"
doc = " and the alternative is losing the text somebody wrote over a stale chip."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_new_issue_resolves_its_label_names_to_ids

attrs: doc = " The detail panel's own request: the counters Gitea computes only for a"
doc = " single pull request, plus the head commit's statuses folded into the one"
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_change_detail_carries_the_counters_and_the_checks

attrs: doc = " The file list, and the diff spliced onto it. `deleted` is the word that"
doc = " would otherwise read as a modification, and the renamed file's path has"
doc = " a space in it — which is why the patch is keyed off `+++` rather than"
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::changed_files_carry_gitea_statuses_and_a_spliced_patch

attrs: doc = " The cap is a hard stop MID-TRANSFER, not a size check afterwards."
doc = " The regression this pins is the whole reason `Content-Length` is not"
doc = " consulted: Gitea writes this endpoint straight to the socket, so a large"
doc = " diff arrives chunked with NO length header — exactly the case the cap"
doc = " exists for, and exactly the one a `text()`-then-measure would buffer in"
doc = " full before discarding. The mock therefore streams without a length and"
doc = " counts what it was actually asked for; the assertion is that the client"
doc = " hung up long before the end."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::an_oversized_diff_is_abandoned_mid_stream_rather_than_buffered

attrs: doc = " The splitter on its own: a rename (where `---` and `+++` disagree and"
doc = " only one of them is the path the file list reports), a deletion (which"
doc = " has no `+++ b/` to read at all), a C-quoted path (skipped rather than"
doc = " half-unquoted onto a neighbouring file) and a block with no hunk."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::the_diff_splitter_reads_the_path_off_the_header_lines

attrs: doc = " The menu is what the repository permits."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::merge_options_follow_the_repository_settings

attrs: doc = " A repository that permits exactly ONE of Gitea's three \"join it as it"
doc = " is\" styles, and not the plain merge commit."
doc = " The regression this pins: reading only `allow_merge_commits` leaves"
doc = " `methods` EMPTY here, the panel's fallback then offers plain \"Merge\","
doc = " and every press sends `do: merge` to a repository that forbids it — a"
doc = " 405 forever, on a repository that merges perfectly well. `Merge` has to"
doc = " be offered, and the STRATEGY has to say what it will really do."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_repository_with_only_one_join_style_still_gets_a_working_button

attrs: doc = " A repository that forbids all five: `Merge` is not offered, and the"
doc = " empty list is the honest answer (the panel falls back to one entry and"
doc = " lets Gitea refuse, which is what would happen anyway)."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_repository_that_permits_nothing_offers_nothing

attrs: doc = " An instance too old to report any of these flags keeps the menu it"
doc = " always had. `Option` is what carries \"Gitea did not say\" — defaulting"
doc = " the flags to `false` would answer \"nothing is permitted\" for a payload"
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::an_instance_that_reports_no_flags_permits_everything

attrs: doc = " The merge itself: `do` (lowercase, and required) plus the head the caller"
doc = " was looking at, and a re-read afterwards because Gitea answers with an"
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_merge_sends_do_and_the_head_then_re_reads_the_row

attrs: doc = " Delivery's lookup. Gitea's `/pulls` has no head filter, so the match is"
doc = " local — over a bounded scan that stops as soon as the forge runs out"
doc = " rather than always paying for its own ceiling."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::find_pulls_filters_by_head_locally_over_a_bounded_scan

attrs: doc = " Gitea has no `draft` parameter — a draft IS a title carrying one of the"
doc = " instance's work-in-progress prefixes, which is how its own UI toggles"
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_draft_pull_request_is_a_prefixed_title

attrs: doc = " A pull request whose fork is gone. Gitea answers with no head repository"
doc = " at all, and the placeholder that stands in has to FAIL `normalize_repo`"
doc = " — that refusal is what stops a task being created for a change whose"
doc = " commits would have nowhere to be pushed, hours before the push proves it."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::a_nameless_head_repository_is_refused_rather_than_worked

attrs: doc = " A title is arbitrary user text, and the prefix test slices it. Bytes"
doc = " through the middle of a code point PANIC, which is a crash on a title"
doc = " nobody would think twice about."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::the_draft_prefix_test_is_char_safe

attrs: doc = " Every request path a caller can influence goes through `normalize_repo`,"
doc = " and every item number is checked before it lands in one."
tests.name: forge::gitea::tests::bad_coordinates_are_refused_before_a_request_is_spent

attrs: doc = " The query string IS the feature: `is:issue` / `is:pr` is what moved the"
doc = " tab split from the client to the server, and one `repo:` qualifier is"
doc = " what keeps advanced-search's OR→AND change irrelevant here."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::query_names_one_repo_and_the_kind

attrs: doc = " Labels are ANDed as quoted qualifiers — unquoted, `help wanted` would"
doc = " split into a label named \"help\" plus a stray search term."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::label_filters_are_quoted_qualifiers

attrs: doc = " The box says \"search title and description\", so it must not double as a"
doc = " query box: typing `is:closed` searches for those words and does NOT"
doc = " widen the list, and a leading `-` does not negate a term."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::free_text_is_stripped_of_query_syntax

attrs: doc = " …and the scope has to be SAID. GitHub's default for free text is title,"
doc = " body AND comments, so without `in:` a match living only in a comment"
doc = " joins the list, the count and the page numbers — under a box that"
doc = " promises \"title and description\". GitLab's `search` already means"
doc = " title+description, so this is what makes the two forges agree."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::free_text_searches_only_the_title_and_the_body

attrs: doc = " Server-side filtering plus a real total: the page number and size go out"
doc = " verbatim and `total_count` comes back, which is what page numbers need."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::list_paginates_by_page_number_with_a_total

attrs: doc = " Out-of-range paging never reaches the API: `per_page=0` is a 422 there"
doc = " and `page=0` means different things at the two forges."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::paging_is_clamped_before_it_is_sent

attrs: doc = " A pull request's four display states all come off ONE payload: `draft`"
doc = " on the hit, and `merged_at` inside `pull_request` — GitHub reports a"
doc = " merged pull request as plain `closed`, so without that timestamp the"
doc = " merged and the abandoned ones would look identical."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::pull_request_rows_carry_draft_and_merged

attrs: doc = " Search only paginates the first [`SEARCH_RESULT_CAP`] results — past"
doc = " that the API errors, so \"next\" must stop rather than offer a button"
doc = " into a failure. A timed-out query is reported, not hidden."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::paging_stops_at_the_search_cap_and_reports_partial_results

attrs: doc = " `assignee=@me` would be a 422 — the login is resolved through `/user`"
doc = " exactly once and reused from the cache afterwards."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::assigned_me_resolves_login_once

attrs: doc = " 403 + exhausted quota is a rate limit (with its retry hint), NOT an"
doc = " auth failure — the UI shows a cooldown, not \"re-enter your token\"."
doc = " Search has its own, much smaller quota, so this path matters more now."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::exhausted_quota_classifies_as_rate_limit

attrs: doc = " Each named order reaches the API as its own `sort`+`order` pair. Without"
doc = " both halves \"oldest\" and \"newest\" would be the same request."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::every_sort_order_reaches_the_api

attrs: doc = " Labels and free text both go out on `q`, together with everything else —"
doc = " the filters compose rather than replacing each other."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::label_and_text_filters_go_out_together

attrs: doc = " The label vocabulary comes from the repository, on the CORE quota — and"
doc = " a full page is reported as such, because a filter list that silently"
doc = " stops at 100 reads as \"these are all the labels this repo has\"."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::labels_come_from_the_repository_and_admit_truncation

attrs: doc = " The thread comes from the ISSUE comments endpoint — the one that serves"
doc = " pull requests too — and each entry is normalized on the way out: the"
doc = " `updated_at` that merely repeats `created_at` is dropped (both are"
doc = " stamped on creation, so passing it through would mark every comment as"
doc = " edited) and a non-`http` avatar never reaches an ``."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::comments_come_from_the_issue_thread_and_are_normalized

attrs: doc = " The row's avatar goes through the same gate a comment's does — it lands"
doc = " in the same ``, so a `javascript:` URL is dropped rather than"
doc = " forwarded, and an author GitHub no longer has leaves no picture at all."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_rows_avatar_is_sanitized_like_a_comments

attrs: doc = " Paging follows the `Link` header, never \"the page came back full\" —"
doc = " which would promise an empty next page on every thread whose length is"
doc = " an exact multiple of the page size."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::comment_paging_follows_the_link_header

attrs: doc = " Coordinates a client made up must not read someone else's thread."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_bad_comment_target_is_rejected

attrs: doc = " A repository path the client made up must not become a search that"
doc = " silently reads a DIFFERENT repository."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_bad_repository_path_is_rejected

attrs: doc = " The reported bug, from the client's side: a self-hosted GitLab that"
doc = " codeg had classified as a GitHub Enterprise gets asked for `/api/v3`,"
doc = " and GitLab replies 410 saying exactly what it is."
doc = " That must not surface as \"forge API error 410: {...}\" — the raw dump the"
doc = " issue reporter saw. It is an identification, so it becomes"
doc = " [`ForgeError::WrongForge`] AND is written to the detection cache, which"
doc = " is what makes the caller's retry go to the GitLab client instead."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_gitlab_answering_a_v3_request_identifies_itself

attrs: doc = " A 410 that is NOT GitLab identifying itself stays an ordinary API error."
doc = " The body is the whole discriminator, so a bare status must not be enough"
doc = " Addressed as `localhost` rather than `127.0.0.1` on purpose: the"
doc = " detection cache is keyed by host and process-wide, so sharing a key with"
doc = " the test above would make the two race."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::an_unrelated_410_is_still_an_api_error

attrs: doc = " The composer gets the STORED comment back — id, author and permalink —"
doc = " not the text it sent. Those are what the thread keys, de-duplicates and"
doc = " links by, and an echo of the draft has none of them."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_posted_comment_comes_back_as_the_forge_stored_it

attrs: doc = " An issue and a pull request are edited through DIFFERENT endpoints, and"
doc = " the pull one is what carries the top-level `merged_at` — the only field"
doc = " that tells a merged change from a closed one."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_state_change_uses_the_collection_the_item_belongs_to

attrs: doc = " The menu is what the REPOSITORY permits. A method it has turned off"
doc = " answers 405 at merge time, so offering it would be offering a button"
tests.name: forge::github::tests::merge_options_drop_what_the_repository_forbids

attrs: doc = " Merging sends the method the caller picked, and the row comes from a"
doc = " RE-READ: GitHub's merge response carries `{sha, merged, message}` and no"
doc = " pull request at all, so there is nothing in it to build a row from."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_merge_sends_the_method_and_re_reads_the_row

attrs: doc = " The merge landed and the row could not be read back. That is NOT a"
doc = " failure: the change is on the base branch, and reporting an error would"
doc = " invite somebody to run an irreversible operation a second time."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_merge_whose_re_read_fails_is_still_a_merge

attrs: doc = " A refusal keeps GitHub's own sentence. \"Merge commits are not allowed on"
doc = " this repository\" is a fact only the forge knows, and a generic \"merge"
doc = " failed\" would send someone looking for a conflict instead of a setting."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_refused_merge_carries_the_forges_reason

attrs: doc = " A new issue is created from the forge's ANSWER, not from the draft: the"
doc = " number, the URL and the labels that actually stuck only exist once it"
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_new_issue_is_posted_and_comes_back_as_a_row

attrs: doc = " Branches, size and CI in one call — and the two check collections"
doc = " merged, because a repository genuinely uses one or the other and reading"
doc = " only `check-runs` shows \"no checks\" over a red external build."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::a_pull_detail_carries_its_branches_and_both_check_collections

attrs: doc = " A token that cannot read checks still reads the pull request. The"
doc = " section says it could not look — which is not the same claim as \"there"
doc = " are no checks\", and is why the panel can tell them apart."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::checks_it_cannot_read_are_unavailable_rather_than_empty

attrs: doc = " Half an answer is its own outcome. GitHub gates check runs and commit"
doc = " statuses behind two DIFFERENT fine-grained permissions, so a token with"
doc = " only one of them gets a 403 from one endpoint and an honest empty list"
doc = " from the other — and \"no checks ran\" over a red Actions run is exactly"
doc = " the claim `available` exists to prevent."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::one_readable_check_collection_is_a_partial_answer

attrs: doc = " Both collections readable: a complete answer, whether or not it is empty."
tests.name: forge::github::tests::two_readable_check_collections_are_a_complete_answer

attrs: doc = " The file list is what \"what does this touch\" is read off, so a rename"
doc = " keeps both paths and a binary reports no line counts rather than zeroes"
tests.name: forge::github::tests::changed_files_carry_their_status_and_flag_binaries

attrs: doc = " The four vocabularies folded into one. `conclusion` is meaningless"
doc = " until the run completes, and a `null` there on a queued run must not"
tests.name: forge::github::tests::check_vocabularies_fold_into_five_states

attrs: doc = " A subgroup path is ONE percent-encoded segment; anything else addresses"
doc = " a route that does not exist. The row shape (iid, description, GitLab's"
doc = " `opened`) is normalized to what the workbench renders."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::issues_come_from_the_encoded_project_path

attrs: doc = " GitLab's `state=closed` excludes merged merge requests. The workbench's"
doc = " closed tab has to show them (GitHub's does), so the query asks for"
doc = " everything and the open ones are dropped here."
doc = " That local narrowing is exactly why this query must report NO total: the"
doc = " `X-Total` the server sends counts the open rows the user cannot see, so"
doc = " page numbers built from it would be wrong. `locked` displays as open, so"
doc = " it is dropped alongside `opened` — otherwise the closed tab would show a"
doc = " row the icon then draws green."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::the_closed_tab_shows_merged_and_withholds_the_untrustworthy_total

attrs: doc = " The open tab is a plain `state=opened` query, so its count is honest —"
doc = " and a draft merge request has to arrive marked as one."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::the_open_tab_counts_and_carries_the_draft_flag

attrs: doc = " Search text, labels and the sort order all reach the collection URL."
doc = " Unlike GitHub there is no query syntax to strip — `search` is plain text"
doc = " over title and description — but the params still have to be there."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::text_label_and_sort_filters_reach_the_url

attrs: doc = " `user_notes_count`, not `notes`: the latter counts the system events"
doc = " (\"changed the milestone\"), which is not what a discussion badge means."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::rows_carry_the_human_comment_count

attrs: doc = " The label vocabulary for the filter, from the project's own labels."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::project_labels_are_listed

attrs: doc = " `notes` is not \"comments\": GitLab files its own events there too, and"
doc = " they are exactly what `user_notes_count` — the number the row shows —"
doc = " leaves out. Dropping them here is what keeps the thread and the count"
doc = " above it describing the same thing."
doc = " The order has to be ASKED for: GitLab's own default for notes is"
doc = " descending, which would read the conversation backwards and make \"load"
doc = " more\" append older comments under newer ones."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::notes_drop_the_system_events_and_read_oldest_first

attrs: doc = " The row's avatar goes through the same gate a note's does — it lands in"
doc = " the same ``, so a `javascript:` URL is dropped rather than"
doc = " forwarded, and an author GitLab no longer has leaves no picture at all."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_rows_avatar_is_sanitized_like_a_notes

attrs: doc = " `has_next` is the FORGE's answer, not \"did anything survive filtering\"."
doc = " A page of nothing but system events is empty of comments and still has"
doc = " the rest of the discussion behind it — inferring from the row count"
doc = " would end the thread there."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_page_of_only_system_events_still_reports_more

attrs: doc = " Issue notes and merge-request notes are DIFFERENT collections over"
doc = " DIFFERENT numbering — the same rule the write side follows. Reading the"
doc = " wrong one does not fail loudly; it answers with a real item's"
doc = " discussion that is not the one on screen."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::notes_are_read_from_the_collection_the_item_belongs_to

attrs: doc = " The single-merge-request payload is what a task is checked out from:"
doc = " `diff_refs.head_sha` wins over `sha`, and a fork's real path is"
doc = " resolved so the refusal can name it."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_merge_request_is_looked_up_by_iid

attrs: doc = " The delivery's lookup: by source branch, in any state, mapped into the"
doc = " same shape the four-way match already knows."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::merge_requests_are_found_by_source_branch

attrs: doc = " GitLab has no `draft` parameter — the title carries it, which is also"
doc = " how its own UI models a draft."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_draft_merge_request_is_a_prefixed_title

attrs: doc = " Issue notes and merge-request notes are DIFFERENT endpoints; sending"
doc = " one to the other is a 404 against a number that exists in the other"
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::notes_go_to_the_collection_the_item_belongs_to

attrs: doc = " Every request URL is now built here from the resolved api_base, so the"
doc = " only thing the client still supplies is coordinates — and a project path"
doc = " it made up must be refused rather than turned into a URL."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_crafted_project_path_is_rejected

attrs: doc = " A payload that does not say which project the source lives in cannot be"
doc = " shown to be ours — \"unknown\" must not read as \"same repository\"."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::an_unstated_source_project_is_not_this_repository

attrs: doc = " Issues and merge requests are separate collections here, and the change"
doc = " is a VERB (`state_event`) rather than a target state — sending GitHub's"
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_state_change_puts_a_verb_on_the_right_collection

attrs: doc = " GitLab's merge endpoint takes NO method — the project picks between a"
doc = " merge commit, a rebase-merge and a fast-forward — so the only choice"
doc = " offered is whether to squash, and `squash_option` decides even that."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::merge_options_offer_only_the_squash_choice_the_project_allows

attrs: doc = " One request, unlike GitHub's two: the merge answers with the merge"
doc = " request itself, so the row comes straight out of the write."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_merge_sends_squash_explicitly_and_reads_the_row_from_the_answer

attrs: doc = " Labels go out COMMA-JOINED here, not as a JSON array — GitHub's shape"
doc = " would apply no labels at all, silently."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_new_issue_comma_joins_its_labels

attrs: doc = " Branches, the fork's real name, a tri-state merge status and the head"
doc = " pipeline's jobs — everything the panel shows that the list row does not."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_merge_request_detail_carries_its_branches_and_pipeline

attrs: doc = " Three ways the CI section can be right, and they are all different."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_pipeline_it_cannot_read_is_unavailable_and_no_pipeline_is_empty

attrs: doc = " GitLab counts nothing per file, so the `+`/`−` come off the diff hunk it"
doc = " ships — and an empty one is binary content, which has no counts at all."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::changed_files_are_counted_off_the_diff_hunk

attrs: doc = " An instance older than 15.7 has no `/diffs`. The unpaginated `/changes`"
doc = " answers instead and is sliced here, so the panel's footer behaves the"
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::a_missing_diffs_endpoint_falls_back_to_changes

attrs: doc = " GitLab's eleven job statuses over the five the strip draws, and the"
doc = " tri-state merge status that is the whole reason `mergeable` is optional."
tests.name: forge::gitlab::tests::job_statuses_and_merge_statuses_fold_into_the_shared_vocabulary

attrs: doc = " Nothing configured must compose to nothing: the trigger appends this"
doc = " only when it is `Some`, so `Some(\"\")` here would put an empty section"
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::an_unconfigured_panel_contributes_no_text

attrs: doc = " `all` first, then the scenario's own — the reading order of a policy:"
doc = " what always applies, then what applies here."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::the_all_key_joins_the_scenarios_own_text

attrs: doc = " Saving is where the blanks go, so the reader never has to know about"
doc = " them — and a scenario name with only whitespace typed into it does not"
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::saving_drops_blank_entries_and_trims_the_rest

attrs: doc = " Over the cap is refused, not truncated: this text rides in every task"
doc = " the panel mints, and silently keeping half of an instruction is worse"
doc = " than not keeping it at all."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::an_oversized_instruction_is_refused_by_name

attrs: doc = " The cap counts CHARACTERS, not bytes — a Chinese instruction is not"
doc = " three times shorter than an English one."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::the_cap_counts_characters_not_bytes

attrs: doc = " A folder's own row REPLACES the global one; it does not layer on top of"
doc = " it. The `all` text is the trap: a folder that set a scenario prompt and"
doc = " nothing else must not keep inheriting the global standing text, or"
doc = " \"this folder has its own settings\" would mean something different here"
doc = " than it does in the task settings dialog one click away."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::a_folders_own_settings_replace_the_global_row_wholesale

attrs: doc = " \"Use the global defaults\" is a DELETE, and the global row is the one"
doc = " scope that cannot give that answer."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::dropping_a_folders_row_puts_it_back_on_the_global_one

attrs: doc = " The cap applies to a folder's own row too — a per-folder save is not a"
doc = " way around the limit the global row is held to."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::a_folder_save_is_validated_like_the_global_one

attrs: doc = " A blob from an older build carries none of the newer fields, and one"
doc = " from a newer build carries fields this one has never heard of. Both"
doc = " must decode — the second is what a user gets by downgrading."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::stored_blobs_decode_across_versions

attrs: doc = " Folder ids survive the round trip as ids. JSON has no integer keys, so"
doc = " they go out as strings — and a store that could not read its own output"
doc = " would lose every override on the next load."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::folder_keys_survive_the_json_round_trip

attrs: doc = " Through a real database, because [`save`] is a READ-MODIFY-WRITE: the"
doc = " pure tests above prove the arithmetic, and this proves the load and the"
doc = " store are the same blob — one key typo and every save would land on"
doc = " something the next load never reads."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::scopes_persist_independently_across_saves

attrs: doc = " The upgrade path: a blob written before the panel had scopes is already"
doc = " sitting under this key. It must be READ as the global row, and the next"
doc = " save must carry it forward rather than write an empty store over it —"
doc = " the one way this change could silently discard a user's settings."
tests.name: forge::settings::tests::a_legacy_blob_becomes_the_global_row_and_survives_the_next_save

attrs: doc = " `NoAccount` is the one forge failure the UI turns into an action, and"
doc = " it can only do that if the i18n key and BOTH params survive the trip to"
doc = " the client. Serialize as well as convert: the frontend reads the JSON,"
doc = " not the struct, and `skip_serializing_if` on those two fields means a"
doc = " conversion that forgot to set them looks identical from Rust."
tests.name: forge::tests::no_account_carries_i18n_key_and_params_over_the_wire

attrs: doc = " GitHub answers with canonical casing (`microsoft/TypeScript`) while"
doc = " keys/remotes are lowercase — comparisons must not care, and `.git`"
doc = " remote suffixes must not split identity either."
tests.name: forge::tests::same_repo_is_case_insensitive_and_suffix_tolerant

attrs: doc = " An unknown provider is refused rather than defaulted: picking GitHub"
doc = " for a value we do not understand would run a task's writes against the"
doc = " wrong API with the wrong credentials."
tests.name: forge::tests::provider_parsing_refuses_what_it_does_not_know

attrs: doc = " Item URLs and head refs are the two places the two forges disagree in a"
doc = " way a task cannot survive: a GitLab link with GitHub's path 404s, and a"
doc = " GitHub head ref simply does not exist on a GitLab server."
tests.name: forge::tests::provider_shapes_urls_and_head_refs_its_own_way

attrs: doc = " The push URL and every stored link come from this one derivation: a"
doc = " bare `server_host` would drop both the scheme and a non-default port,"
doc = " which is exactly what a self-hosted instance has."
tests.name: forge::tests::the_web_origin_comes_from_the_api_base

attrs: doc = " A name and a picture, and — the point of the type — nothing else. The"
doc = " identity is built from the same value that holds the token, and it is"
doc = " serialized straight to a webview."
tests.name: forge::tests::an_identity_is_a_name_and_a_picture_and_carries_no_secret

attrs: doc = " Paging comes off the wire and reaches two APIs that reject different"
doc = " halves of the nonsense: `per_page=0` is a 422 at GitHub and an empty"
doc = " page at GitLab, and `page=0` means page 1 at one of them only."
tests.name: forge::tests::client_supplied_paging_is_clamped_into_range

attrs: doc = " The repository is an ARGUMENT, not a field of the client's payload:"
doc = " whatever filters arrive, the request is built against the repository the"
doc = " server resolved from the folder's remote."
tests.name: forge::tests::a_request_takes_its_repository_from_the_caller_and_normalizes_the_rest

attrs: doc = " Both caps are real API limits, not taste: GitHub rejects a `q` over 256"
doc = " characters outright, and each extra label lengthens it further."
tests.name: forge::tests::search_and_label_filters_are_capped

attrs: doc = " The two forges spell the same colour differently — GitHub sends bare"
doc = " `d73a4a`, GitLab `#d9534f` — so one normalized `#rrggbb` is what the UI"
doc = " gets. Anything that is not hex is refused rather than passed along:"
doc = " GitLab accepts CSS colour names on write, and this value is handed"
tests.name: forge::tests::label_colours_are_normalized_and_non_hex_is_refused

attrs: doc = " A count is a LIST asked for one row: neither forge counts these"
doc = " collections on its own endpoint. The tab is the only thing that differs"
doc = " between the switcher's two probes — every filter carries over, or the"
doc = " badge would describe a result set nobody is looking at."
tests.name: forge::tests::a_count_probe_is_the_smallest_page_of_the_same_filters

attrs: doc = " A badge is a bare digit with nowhere to add a caveat, so a count that"
doc = " needs one is withheld instead. The list keeps the caveat — and the"
doc = " count — because it has a footer to say it in."
tests.name: forge::tests::an_incomplete_search_offers_no_count_to_a_badge

attrs: doc = " The three answers the CI section has to keep apart. `partial` is the one"
doc = " GitHub forces: its checks live in two collections behind two separate"
doc = " fine-grained permissions, so half an answer is a real outcome."
tests.name: forge::tests::a_half_read_check_list_is_neither_complete_nor_unavailable

attrs: doc = " Four named orders, because the two forges accept different field sets"
doc = " and spell the shared ones differently. `newest` is the default — the"
doc = " same one github.com's issue list opens on."
tests.name: forge::tests::sort_orders_map_to_a_field_and_a_direction

attrs: doc = " A comment request carries only COORDINATES, and both halves are"
doc = " checked here rather than in either provider client: on GitLab the kind"
doc = " picks the collection, so a wrong one reads a real item's discussion"
doc = " that is not the one on screen, and out-of-range paging is a 422 at"
doc = " GitHub and an empty page at GitLab."
tests.name: forge::tests::a_comment_request_validates_its_item_and_clamps_its_paging

attrs: doc = " Both forges stamp an `updated_at` on creation, so its mere presence"
doc = " says nothing. Passing it through unfiltered would put \"edited\" on every"
tests.name: forge::tests::only_a_real_edit_carries_an_updated_timestamp

attrs: doc = " A comment is written by a human into a box and then published where"
doc = " other people read it, so the two things that can go wrong are checked"
doc = " before a request is spent: nothing at all, and more than the forge will"
doc = " take. Whitespace-only counts as nothing — both forges accept it and"
doc = " render a blank card this app has no way to delete."
tests.name: forge::tests::a_comment_draft_must_carry_text_and_a_real_item

attrs: doc = " Close and reopen are VERBS on the wire at GitLab and a target state at"
doc = " GitHub — the same button, two vocabularies, and neither API accepts the"
tests.name: forge::tests::a_state_action_speaks_each_forges_own_wire_vocabulary

attrs: doc = " A title is required and capped; a body is optional and DROPPED when"
doc = " blank rather than sent as an empty string — GitHub stores that as a"
doc = " body and the issue then renders an empty description block."
tests.name: forge::tests::a_new_issue_needs_a_title_and_normalizes_the_rest

attrs: doc = " GitLab ships a diff and no counters, so the `+12 −3` beside each file is"
doc = " counted here. `+++` / `---` are the file headers: counting them would"
doc = " add one to each side of every single file in the list."
tests.name: forge::tests::diff_line_counting_skips_the_file_headers

attrs: doc = " \"Nothing ran\" and \"we could not look\" are different answers and the"
doc = " panel says different things about them — collapsing the two prints \"no"
doc = " checks\" over a repository whose pipeline is red."
tests.name: forge::tests::an_unavailable_check_list_is_not_an_empty_one

attrs: doc = " A file page comes off the wire with the same clamping every other paged"
doc = " request gets, and a change is addressed by a real number."
tests.name: forge::tests::change_queries_validate_their_item_and_clamp_their_paging

attrs: doc = " These strings reach an `href` and an ``, and they come from"
doc = " whatever instance the account points at. Only the two schemes those"
doc = " attributes should ever carry survive."
tests.name: forge::tests::forge_supplied_urls_keep_only_the_web_schemes

attrs: doc = " Issue bodies are arbitrary UTF-8; a byte slice could split a code point"
tests.name: forge::tests::body_truncation_is_char_safe

attrs: doc = " The client holder is keyed by the proxy env fingerprint: same"
doc = " fingerprint reuses the pool, a changed fingerprint rebuilds — this is"
doc = " what makes a runtime proxy switch take effect without a restart."
tests.name: forge::tests::http_client_rebuilds_when_proxy_fingerprint_changes

attrs: doc = " Production change that must fail this test: slicing `url[..7]`/`url[..8]`"
doc = " on a legal UTF-8 `str` whose byte 7 sits inside `é` (2-byte)."
tests.name: git_credential::tests::sanitize_http_remote_does_not_panic_on_unicode_prefixed_https

attrs: doc = " Production change that must fail this test: leaving userinfo, `?query`,"
doc = " or `#fragment` in log text, or rejecting mixed-case `HTTPS://`."
tests.name: git_credential::tests::sanitize_http_remote_strips_userinfo_query_fragment_from_mixed_case
