attrs: doc = " Production change that must fail this test: assuming scheme prefixes"
doc = " exist and slicing without a length/`get` check."
tests.name: git_credential::tests::sanitize_http_remote_does_not_panic_on_short_strings

attrs: doc = " Production change that must fail this test: `url[..8]` on a legal `str`"
doc = " whose byte 8 is not a character boundary (`中` is 3 bytes; 3 × 3 = 9)."
tests.name: git_credential::tests::sanitize_http_remote_does_not_panic_on_utf8_char_boundary_str

attrs: doc = " Production change that must fail this test: case-sensitive `starts_with`"
tests.name: git_credential::tests::parse_http_remote_accepts_mixed_case_clone_urls

attrs: doc = " End-to-end check of the server-mode credential helper lookup path."
doc = " Sets up a real on-disk SQLite DB, seeds a GitHub account row, writes"
doc = " a token to the file-based store, then exercises `lookup_credential`"
doc = " the same way `run_credential_helper` does. Compiled only in"
doc = " server-mode builds (`cargo test --no-default-features`) because the"
doc = " Tauri-mode token store hits the OS keyring, which we can't safely"
tests.name: git_credential::tests::test_credential_helper_e2e_server_mode

attrs: doc = " A submodule's `.git` file points at a FULL repository (its own"
doc = " `objects/`) with no `commondir` marker. It is not a worktree of the"
doc = " superproject and must not be grouped under it."
tests.name: git_repo::tests::main_worktree_root_is_none_for_a_submodule

attrs: doc = " A worktree of a BARE repo: `commondir` names the repository directory"
doc = " itself, so there is no main working tree to group under."
tests.name: git_repo::tests::main_worktree_root_is_none_for_a_bare_repo_worktree

attrs: doc = " git writes an absolute `gitdir:`, but a hand-written relative one is"
doc = " legal and resolves against the worktree directory."
tests.name: git_repo::tests::main_worktree_root_accepts_a_relative_gitdir_pointer

attrs: doc = " Simulated install failure after live file was moved aside must restore"
doc = " the previous store (no wipe / no permanent Absent)."
tests.name: keyring_store::tests::publish_restores_backup_when_install_fails

attrs: doc = " If restore itself fails, leave `.bak` so a later read reports Unavailable"
doc = " (or recovers) rather than silent Absent."
tests.name: keyring_store::tests::missing_live_with_backup_is_unavailable_or_recovered

attrs: doc = " Concurrent RMW + readers under the process mutex must never observe"
tests.name: keyring_store::tests::concurrent_reads_never_see_truncated_json

attrs: doc = " Foreign `get_token_state` must not ack a claim-owned read watch."
doc = " Holds SuiteGuard so arm/reset cannot race a parallel suite's claim watch."
tests.name: keyring_store::tests::read_attempt_ack_requires_claim_gen

attrs: doc = " One line can both open a new day and blow its entire budget (small"
doc = " configured ceiling). Both notices are then due, and dropping the rollover"
doc = " one would silently lose the closed day's tally — the exact"
doc = " \"logs disappeared and nothing said why\" failure this module prevents."
tests.name: logging::budget::tests::rollover_and_exhaustion_in_one_line_report_both

attrs: doc = " `tracing_appender` re-opens an existing dated file with `append(true)`"
doc = " (`rolling.rs:791`), so a restart lands in a file that already has bytes."
doc = " Starting the count at zero handed out a fresh ceiling per launch — and"
doc = " this app restarts itself (the `--supervise` worker, auto update), so a"
doc = " crash loop could grow one file without bound."
tests.name: logging::budget::tests::resuming_counts_bytes_already_in_todays_file

attrs: doc = " The day is read on EVERY line, so the very first line after midnight"
doc = " reopens the budget. An earlier draft amortized the clock read over 64 KiB"
doc = " of offered bytes, which meant a sparse-traffic app could stay latched for"
doc = " hours — or days — of wall time past the rollover, silently dropping a"
tests.name: logging::budget::tests::writer_reopens_on_the_first_line_of_the_new_day

attrs: doc = " Two readers now reconstruct this name (the budget's resume measurement"
doc = " and the panic hook's synchronous append), so the scheme is pinned rather"
doc = " than left implicit in each of them."
tests.name: logging::budget::tests::daily_file_name_matches_the_appenders_scheme

attrs: doc = " The specific accident the `tungstenite` ceiling exists to prevent: a user"
doc = " raises the level to trace to diagnose a remote-workspace connection, and"
doc = " the WS handshake dump takes their bearer token and every custom header —"
doc = " the Cloudflare Access secret the feature exists to carry — to disk with"
doc = " it. Both filter paths have to hold, since the env override builds its own."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::a_global_trace_cannot_capture_the_websocket_handshake_dump

attrs: doc = " The crate ceiling stops the accident; this stops the deliberate act."
doc = " A firehose ceiling is meant to be re-openable by naming a submodule —"
doc = " that is how `tungstenite::protocol=trace` stays available for frame"
doc = " debugging. A credential dump is not, so the exact target it is emitted"
doc = " on carries its own backstop, which wins at equal specificity, and no"
doc = " target is more specific than the module holding the `trace!`."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::the_handshake_dump_cannot_be_reopened_even_by_naming_its_target

attrs: doc = " Why the level table cannot be the whole answer, pinned as a fact rather"
doc = " than an argument: `EnvFilter` ranks a field-qualified directive above a"
doc = " plain target one, and the dump is a formatted event so it has a"
doc = " `message` field to qualify on. The first assertion shows the ceiling"
doc = " losing; the second shows what actually holds the line."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::a_field_qualified_directive_defeats_the_ceiling_but_not_the_denial

attrs: doc = " The panic record reaches the rolling file by its own synchronous write,"
doc = " so the file layer must skip it — otherwise every survivable panic (most"
doc = " of them: tokio catches panics in spawned tasks) is in the log twice."
doc = " Scoped to that one target, and to that one sink."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::the_file_sink_skips_only_the_record_the_panic_hook_already_wrote

attrs: doc = " The predicate above is only half the claim; this exercises the wiring,"
doc = " with the same two global filters the real subscriber is built from and"
doc = " the most permissive directive anyone could write for the dump."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::the_denial_layer_drops_the_dump_and_nothing_else

attrs: doc = " The panic filter is PER-LAYER, which is the whole point: the file sink"
doc = " must lose the record it already holds while every other sink keeps it."
doc = " A global filter here would have silenced the panic on stderr and in the"
doc = " Logs viewer too — which is the opposite of what this module is for."
doc = " Built with the same layer stack `build_subscriber`'s file arm uses, so"
doc = " this exercises the wiring and not just the predicate."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::the_file_layer_alone_loses_the_record_the_hook_already_wrote

attrs: doc = " A backstop is a CEILING, not a pin. `LogLevel::Off` is documented as"
doc = " \"disables capture entirely\", so a bare `target=warn` appended after it —"
doc = " which is what this used to emit — made \"logging off\" still write, and"
doc = " two of agent_client_protocol's `warn!` sites fire per message under a misbehaving agent."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::off_means_off_and_backstops_never_raise_verbosity

attrs: doc = " The env path has no single global level to clamp against, so the ceiling"
doc = " is resolved per target against the expression itself. Clamping only when"
doc = " the whole expression was a bare level (the first attempt) left the two"
doc = " cases below still emitting `agent_client_protocol=warn` — overruling an explicit request"
doc = " for silence on a per-message path."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::env_override_clamps_per_target_not_just_bare_levels

attrs: doc = " `from.trim()` for its indices but slices the untrimmed `from`"
doc = " and becomes the inert target `\"info \"`. A resolver that trimmed read it as"
doc = " the global `Info` and emitted a ceiling for something the filter had"
doc = " granted nothing — louder than asked."
doc = " Asserted on the **parsed filter**, not just the resolver, so the two can't"
tests.name: logging::init::tests::padded_directives_are_inert_to_both_the_filter_and_the_ceiling

attrs: doc = " `parse_lossy` DROPS a directive whose level is invalid — it does not"
doc = " reinterpret it. Treating an unparseable level as `Trace` made the ceiling"
doc = " louder than the expression: EnvFilter kept only the global, and we appended"
doc = " a `warn` for a target it had discarded."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::an_invalid_level_drops_the_directive_instead_of_widening_it

attrs: doc = " The forms `EnvFilter` accepts that a naive \"is it a bare level?\" reader"
doc = " misses. Each of these used to resolve to `Off` and thus emit `agent_client_protocol=off`,"
doc = " silently disabling a target the expression had asked to see."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::env_level_for_target_understands_every_directive_form

attrs: doc = " The other direction: a user turning a clamped target DOWN must be obeyed."
doc = " The backstop exists to refuse \"louder\", never \"quieter\"."
tests.name: logging::init::tests::a_quieter_per_target_override_beats_the_backstop

attrs: doc = " The record's target must escape the `codeg_lib::logging=off` backstop"
doc = " that every constructed filter carries. Emitting from the module path"
doc = " would land inside it and silently drop the one line the hook exists to"
doc = " write, with no symptom other than the original silence."
tests.name: logging::panic_hook::tests::the_panic_target_escapes_the_logging_backstop

attrs: doc = " The synchronous append is not covered by the daily log budget (it runs"
doc = " on the near side of the appender's channel), so it carries a ceiling of"
doc = " its own — otherwise a task that panics on every turn of a restart loop"
doc = " writes unbudgeted 20 KB records forever, which is the storm the budget"
tests.name: logging::panic_hook::tests::the_append_budget_stops_the_file_growing_without_end

attrs: doc = " The reservation is what makes concurrent panics safe: `fetch_add` gives"
doc = " each caller a distinct `before`, so the records that fit are written"
doc = " once each and the boundary is crossed by exactly one of them, however"
doc = " many threads are dying at the same moment."
tests.name: logging::panic_hook::tests::concurrent_reservations_spend_the_budget_exactly_once

attrs: doc = " The capture path, exercised against a real panic. `PanicHookInfo` cannot"
doc = " be constructed outside one, so this installs a hook of its own (not"
doc = " [`install`], which is process-global and permanent) and unwinds into it."
tests.name: logging::panic_hook::tests::a_real_panic_yields_payload_location_and_backtrace

attrs: doc = " Settings rows written before stage prompts existed must keep decoding —"
doc = " the column is one JSON blob, so a missing key is the migration."
tests.name: models::work_task::tests::legacy_settings_json_decodes_without_stage_prompts

attrs: doc = " Whatever the proxy's source, an agent handed one also gets the loopback"
tests.name: network::proxy::tests::a_proxied_launch_always_carries_the_loopback_exception

attrs: doc = " A per-agent `NO_PROXY` joins the list the child inherits instead of"
doc = " replacing one spelling of it — the lowercase one would otherwise keep"
doc = " codeg's list, and curl, Bun, Python and Node read that one first."
tests.name: network::proxy::tests::a_per_agent_bypass_list_joins_the_inherited_one_in_both_spellings

attrs: doc = " Both inherited spellings count, even when an external environment set"
tests.name: network::proxy::tests::both_inherited_spellings_are_kept

attrs: doc = " No proxy in the launch, nothing to bypass: the per-agent row and the"
doc = " inherited list reach the child exactly as they did before."
tests.name: network::proxy::tests::a_launch_without_a_proxy_is_left_alone

attrs: doc = " Per-agent and inherited lists are read by the same rules as the"
doc = " settings' own: a full-width or ideographic comma separates, and every"
doc = " entry — a `*.x` one included — reaches the agent as written."
tests.name: network::proxy::tests::a_launch_list_is_read_by_the_settings_rules

attrs: doc = " `*` from any source wins alone: inside a list Python and curl skip it."
tests.name: network::proxy::tests::a_wildcard_anywhere_bypasses_everything

attrs: doc = " Users paste the base URL either way; both must hit the same path."
tests.name: network::webdav::tests::trailing_slash_in_the_configured_url_changes_nothing

attrs: doc = " The whole point of hand-rolling these errors instead of wrapping"
tests.name: network::webdav::tests::rendered_errors_never_contain_credentials_or_host

attrs: doc = " A crashed watch's port stops validating immediately (not only after the"
doc = " 60s sweep) — the liveness check is on the request path."
tests.name: office_watch::tests::validate_rejects_dead_child_without_sweep

attrs: doc = " A dead entry that still squats a port the OS re-assigned to a new live"
doc = " watch must not shadow it: lookups skip the dead one and find the live one."
tests.name: office_watch::tests::dead_entry_does_not_shadow_reused_port

attrs: doc = " Ref-count sharing + teardown, using a long-lived stand-in child instead"
doc = " of a real officecli (unix-only: a portable never-exiting child)."
tests.name: office_watch::tests::ref_count_sharing_and_teardown

attrs: doc = " The sweep reaps a dead child, leaves a live desktop preview alone, and"
doc = " reaps an abandoned web preview (proxied, no SSE leases, past the grace)."
tests.name: office_watch::tests::sweep_reaping_rules

attrs: doc = " A recorded prompt is read as raw JSON (it must survive bytes written by"
doc = " older builds) while a `session/load` chunk arrives already typed. Two"
doc = " readers, one meaning: the same content has to produce the same block"
doc = " whichever door it comes through, or history would contradict itself"
doc = " depending on whether codeg recorded the turn or the agent replayed it."
tests.name: parsers::acp_native::tests::the_typed_and_raw_readers_agree_on_the_same_content

attrs: doc = " The parsed title is the AUTHORITATIVE one — `commands::conversations`"
doc = " writes it over any unlocked title the row holds, including one the agent"
doc = " published itself. So it stays prose-only: an attachment-only prompt"
doc = " reports no title here and is named by the first-prompt SEED instead"
doc = " (`acp::manager::delegation_child_title_seed`), which only ever fills a"
doc = " row that has no title at all."
tests.name: parsers::acp_native::tests::the_parsed_title_is_prose_only_and_never_an_attachment_name

attrs: doc = " An everyday file name is not a safe Markdown fragment. The marker is"
doc = " escaped the way the composer escapes its own `@`-file links, so the"
doc = " frontend's reference-link parser recovers the real path instead of"
doc = " showing raw `[…](…)` source with the link broken at the first space."
tests.name: parsers::acp_native::tests::markers_for_awkward_paths_stay_well_formed_links

attrs: doc = " A replay whose user message puts the attachment BEFORE the prose (the"
doc = " order an agent that front-loads file context stores it in). The marker is"
doc = " a whole block, so the sentence after it must not be glued onto the end of"
doc = " its markdown link — the live projection emits one block per prompt block,"
doc = " and the transcript has to read the same way."
tests.name: parsers::acp_native::tests::replayed_prose_after_an_attachment_marker_stays_its_own_block

attrs: doc = " The regression the attachment fix turns on: a user message carrying only"
doc = " an attachment used to project to nothing, so it neither ended the"
doc = " previous assistant turn nor appeared at all — the next reply merged into"
tests.name: parsers::acp_native::tests::an_attachment_only_replayed_chunk_ends_the_previous_assistant_turn

attrs: doc = " The live user turn is projected by `acp::types::user_blocks_from_prompt`;"
doc = " this parser re-derives the same mapping from the recorded wire bytes."
doc = " They are two implementations of one contract — a viewer watching live and"
doc = " a reader after a refresh must see the same message — so pin them"
doc = " together over the block shapes codeg's composer actually sends."
tests.name: parsers::acp_native::tests::history_projection_matches_the_live_user_message_projection

attrs: doc = " A `delegate_to_agent` call from the codeg-mcp companion must replay"
doc = " under its wire name. The frontend's tool-kind classifier"
doc = " naming conventions and renders the delegation card from it — the same"
doc = " path the live session takes — so the projection must pass the reported"
doc = " title through verbatim rather than genericizing or rewriting it."
tests.name: parsers::acp_native::tests::a_delegation_call_replays_under_its_wire_name

attrs: doc = " The write-side whitelist and the read-side match arms are two"
doc = " hand-maintained views of one set. This asserts they agree by RUNNING the"
doc = " projection over each variant rather than by restating either list, so"
doc = " teaching `apply_update` a new variant without whitelisting it (or the"
doc = " reverse) fails here instead of silently costing that content forever."
tests.name: parsers::acp_native::tests::recorded_updates_are_exactly_the_ones_the_projection_reads

attrs: doc = " The whole safety argument for a verbatim anchor: the CLI indents the"
doc = " report, so a forged copy inside it cannot reach column zero. A match that"
doc = " ignored the line boundary would truncate the report at the forgery."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::a_forged_header_inside_the_report_is_not_an_anchor

attrs: doc = " A resume replays the surviving history into the SAME transcript,"
doc = " boundary records included — byte-identical, original uuid and timestamp"
doc = " intact. One real 19,435-line transcript holds 22 boundary records for 7"
doc = " compactions, one of them written six times; without dedup that session"
doc = " draws six identical dividers in a row."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::a_replayed_compact_boundary_draws_only_one_divider

attrs: doc = " The gauge after a `/compact` with nothing said since."
doc = " The boundary carries no usage of its own, so the plain"
doc = " last-turn-with-usage rule walks past it to the pre-compaction reply and"
doc = " reports a window that no longer exists — measured on a real transcript,"
doc = " 108,307 for a window the boundary itself puts at 4,462. Live is right"
doc = " because the adapter answers the boundary with `usage_update {used:"
doc = " post_tokens}`; history has to agree."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::compaction_post_tokens_become_the_context_gauge

attrs: doc = " The user typed `/compact`; the divider is what it produced. Live, codeg"
doc = " echoes the prompt above the divider — so history has to as well, and at"
doc = " the same place, which is NOT where the CLI wrote the echo."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::the_compact_prompt_is_emitted_above_the_divider_it_caused

attrs: doc = " `/compact <instructions>` is a real form, so the emitted prompt is the"
doc = " reconstructed command line rather than a fixed `/compact` label."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::the_compact_prompt_keeps_the_instructions_it_was_given

attrs: doc = " An automatic compaction has no prompt to show, and the slot it leaves"
doc = " open must not be claimed by an unrelated command much later on."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::an_automatic_compaction_gets_no_prompt_and_leaves_no_slot_behind

attrs: doc = " A resume replays the whole block verbatim. The boundary is deduped by"
doc = " uuid, and the prompt must not be re-attached to the surviving divider —"
doc = " the replayed summary is the only thing that lands after it."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::a_replayed_compact_block_emits_the_prompt_once

attrs: doc = " A compaction is a boundary between turns, so history has to draw the"
doc = " same divider the live ACP stream does — claude-agent-acp 0.75.0 streams"
doc = " `_meta.contextCompaction`, and without the parser half the card would"
doc = " appear during the turn and disappear when the conversation is reopened."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::compact_boundary_becomes_a_compaction_divider_turn

attrs: doc = " `manual` is already the wire spelling, so only `auto` is renamed — and a"
doc = " record whose metadata never arrived still marks the boundary, because"
doc = " the card degrades to its plain label when the counts are missing."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::compaction_trigger_is_renamed_only_for_auto

attrs: doc = " Cancelling a turn makes Claude Code append a `user` record reading"
doc = " `[Request interrupted by user]`. It is addressed to the MODEL — it"
doc = " explains why a tool call has no result — so it is dropped: as a chat"
doc = " bubble it puts words in the user's mouth, and a user record is a turn"
doc = " boundary, so it also opens an empty trailing turn. Both parse paths"
doc = " (batch detail + the watcher's accumulator) must drop it, and neither"
doc = " may drop a real message that merely quotes the phrase."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::interrupt_bookkeeping_records_never_render_as_user_messages

attrs: doc = " a user-prompted launch, then a `<task-notification>` continuation."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::task_notification_continuation_is_background_task_origin

attrs: doc = " `/clear` writes a sibling `{new-uuid}.jsonl` whose first records carry"
doc = " the command tags, starting when the old file stops. Detection must"
doc = " return that successor — not an unrelated later session in the same"
doc = " project dir, and not a file that merely exists."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::find_clear_rollover_successor_picks_the_new_transcript

attrs: doc = " Reopen looks up the OLD session id (still on conversation.external_id)."
doc = " The reader must follow the rollover so post-clear turns are what"
doc = " reload shows; pre-clear content stays on the abandoned file."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::get_conversation_follows_clear_rollover_to_the_new_file

attrs: doc = " The fork point codeg sends must be the id the ADAPTER would look up."
doc = " claude-agent-acp's `messageIdForGrouping` takes the API message id when"
doc = " the record has one, so an assistant turn must carry that — not the"
doc = " record uuid `MessageTurn::id`-adjacent code uses everywhere else."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::assistant_turns_carry_the_api_message_id_as_the_fork_point

attrs: doc = " `messageIdForGrouping` falls back to the record uuid when the message"
doc = " carries no id, and so must codeg — otherwise those turns would silently"
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::assistant_turns_fall_back_to_the_record_uuid

attrs: doc = " The real `/goal` shape (Claude Code 2.1.x): the command record, its"
doc = " `<local-command-stdout>`, then an `isMeta` STRING hook instruction that"
doc = " the model answers directly. None of that is the expanded-prompt shape,"
doc = " so the old \"decide on the very next record\" rule dropped the command —"
doc = " the user's message vanished from history and the reply was left with no"
doc = " prompt above it to anchor the in-flight suppression on."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::goal_command_renders_as_the_prompt_of_the_turn_it_drove

attrs: doc = " A `/goal` used to render a capsule while streaming (the adapter publishes"
doc = " `_meta.goal` snapshots) and NOTHING on reload, because the parser had no"
doc = " idea the CLI records goal transitions as `goal_status` attachments. It"
doc = " does now — and the card has to land BELOW the prompt that set it, which"
doc = " the record order fights: the CLI writes the attachment BEFORE the `/goal`"
doc = " command record, and a user turn ends the assistant block the card groups"
doc = " into, so opening it in stream order would leave a capsule above the"
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::goal_card_opens_below_the_prompt_that_set_it

attrs: doc = " The Stop hook reports every one of its blocks as a `goal_status`"
doc = " attachment. With the run already open those restate what is on screen —"
doc = " pushing a card per iteration would spray the transcript with duplicates."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::a_restated_goal_does_not_open_a_second_card

attrs: doc = " A feed can START mid-goal: the watcher baselines at the end of whatever"
doc = " was already on disk, and a session Claude Code resumed re-arms the hook"
doc = " without writing a fresh arming record. Then the Stop hook's own"
doc = " restatement is the only evidence a goal is running, and the card has to"
doc = " come from it — Claude Code reads these records the same way (an"
doc = " attachment that is neither met nor failed means the goal is still on)."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::a_feed_that_starts_mid_goal_opens_the_card_from_a_restatement

attrs: doc = " Re-aiming a goal before the first one ever reached a reply replaces it."
doc = " That is what the live view shows for the same session: both openings are"
doc = " published, but they land in one assistant block, where a second `active`"
doc = " goal takes over the open run instead of stacking a second capsule. (When"
doc = " each `/goal` DOES drive its own reply the two openings are separated by a"
doc = " user turn, nothing merges them, and both cards render — that path is"
doc = " unaffected because the first is released at its own reply.)"
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::re_aiming_before_any_reply_leaves_one_card

attrs: doc = " A feed can also join a goal only in time to see it END — the watcher"
doc = " baselines mid-run, or the arming record lives in a transcript this one"
doc = " was resumed from. The close is written on its own rather than invented an"
doc = " opening for it: a lone `update_goal` renders as a finished goal card,"
doc = " which is exactly what the transcript says happened, and a synthesized"
doc = " opener would claim a run this feed never witnessed."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::joining_a_goal_at_its_end_writes_the_close_alone

attrs: doc = " A goal the model judged impossible ends as `blocked` — the goal"
doc = " extension's own vocabulary for a failed goal, which the card labels and"
doc = " tones as an error. \"failed\" is not in that vocabulary and would render as"
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::an_impossible_goal_closes_the_run_as_blocked

attrs: doc = " Clearing a goal is written as `met` with the arming flag set, so it ends"
doc = " the run like an achieved one. Cleared before any reply, the open is still"
doc = " waiting to be released — it has to come out WITH the close, or the"
doc = " transcript keeps a terminal card that ends no run."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::clearing_before_any_reply_still_renders_the_whole_run

attrs: doc = " Attachments are how the CLI hands the model context it did not ask for —"
doc = " agent listings, skill listings, task reminders. None of them are"
doc = " conversation, and a `goal_status` with no condition names no goal."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::other_attachments_never_reach_the_transcript

attrs: doc = " Evidence the command drove a turn can also arrive as an interrupt"
doc = " marker: it is only ever written against a request that was running. The"
doc = " turn may have no output at all, which is exactly when its prompt is the"
doc = " only thing left to explain it."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::interrupted_command_turn_keeps_its_prompt

attrs: doc = " The fallback evidence, for a shape the stronger rules can't see: no"
doc = " `promptId` to correlate an injection with (nothing in today's corpus"
doc = " reaches this — every real command resolves at its expansion, injection or"
doc = " interrupt — but a CLI that stops stamping submission ids must degrade to"
doc = " a visible prompt, not to the invisible-user-message bug)."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::a_reply_alone_still_resolves_a_command_with_no_submission_id

attrs: doc = " The degradation path must stay coherent end to end: with no submission"
doc = " ids anywhere, the command's OWN injection is indistinguishable from a"
doc = " foreign one, so it must not be treated as a refutation — otherwise the"
doc = " record that proves the command drove a turn is the very thing that"
doc = " discards it, and the reply-based fallback never gets to run."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::a_command_survives_its_own_injection_when_nothing_carries_an_id

attrs: doc = " A stale buffered command must not be adopted by an unrelated turn. The"
doc = " accumulator is also fed incrementally by the background watcher, which"
doc = " never ends its feed, so a client command can sit buffered indefinitely —"
doc = " and the reply that eventually arrives may belong to a cron prompt that"
doc = " landed in between. The foreign injection retires it."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::a_foreign_injection_retires_a_stale_buffered_command

attrs: doc = " A `<task-notification>` settling mid-wait owns the reply that follows it"
doc = " (background work reporting back), so it refutes the buffered command"
doc = " rather than letting it claim that reply's prompt slot."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::task_notification_refutes_a_buffered_command

attrs: doc = " A client-only command stays hidden even when the CLI writes several"
doc = " inert records before the next prompt — the lookahead walks past command"
doc = " output and attachments without deciding, and only the real prompt does."
tests.name: parsers::claude::tests::client_command_stays_hidden_across_inert_records

attrs: doc = " The whole point: cline 3.x moved its transcripts from"
doc = " `sessions/<id>/<id>.messages.json`, and a parser still reading the old"
doc = " location returns zero turns for every session — which is what the"
doc = " conversation view renders as \"no messages\", and what leaves a finished"
doc = " reply with no model, no tokens and no timestamp under it."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::a_3x_session_is_read_from_the_sessions_directory

attrs: doc = " Listing is what the folder fallback searches when the recorded"
doc = " `external_id` no longer resolves, so it has to see 3.x sessions too."
doc = " One directory is one conversation: an agent-team teammate writes a"
doc = " SIBLING `<other>.messages.json` into the same directory, and a spawned"
doc = " sub-agent gets no manifest at all, so neither may become a second row."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::listing_reports_one_conversation_per_session_directory

attrs: doc = " `messages_path` in the manifest is the absolute path the WRITING"
doc = " process saw. It stops being true the moment the store moves — a"
doc = " restored backup, `CLINE_DIR`, a test fixture — so the conventional"
doc = " path next to the manifest has to win, or a relocated store reads as"
doc = " empty for every session in it."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::a_stale_recorded_messages_path_does_not_hide_the_transcript

attrs: doc = " Tool results arrive as `role:\"user\"` messages alongside the automated"
doc = " filler cline writes next to them. The result belongs on its own system"
doc = " turn (that is where the renderer pairs it with the `tool_use` above);"
doc = " the filler is not something the user said and must not be painted as a"
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::a_tool_result_is_split_off_from_the_message_carrying_it

attrs: doc = " A user message with no wrapper and no tool result is the shape a future"
doc = " cline would write if it stopped wrapping prompts. Treating the wrapper"
doc = " as mandatory would swallow the prompt silently, so it is a preference,"
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::an_unwrapped_lone_prompt_is_still_shown

attrs: doc = " Same trap as the pre-3.x stripper, on the tags that replaced those. A"
doc = " user quoting `</user_input>` puts a closing tag ahead of the opener it"
doc = " appears to close; rebuilding the message around that earlier tag"
doc = " splices the opening tag back in and makes the string LONGER every pass,"
doc = " so the loop never ends and memory runs out. A regression here HANGS the"
doc = " run rather than failing it, which is why both shapes are pinned."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::a_quoted_closing_tag_does_not_hang_the_session_cleanup

attrs: doc = " An unclosed opener is left alone rather than eating the rest of the"
doc = " message: the transcript of a session still being written ends mid-tag."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::an_unclosed_session_wrapper_keeps_its_text

attrs: doc = " A user asking about the wrapper puts `</environment_details>` in their"
doc = " own text, ahead of the block Cline appends. Closing the block at that"
doc = " earlier tag re-splices the opening tag into the result and makes the"
doc = " string longer on every pass, so the loop never ends: opening the"
doc = " conversation used to hang the parse and grow memory without bound."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::a_quoted_closing_tag_does_not_hang_the_environment_strip

attrs: doc = " Same slip in the `<task>` loop reads a reversed byte range instead of"
doc = " looping, because the close tag ends up before the open tag's inner"
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::a_leading_closing_task_tag_does_not_panic

attrs: doc = " Nested wrappers must still collapse to their innermost content, which is"
doc = " the behaviour the first closing tag after the opening one already gave."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::nested_task_wrappers_collapse

attrs: doc = " An unclosed opening tag still truncates at it, and an unclosed `<task>`"
doc = " still leaves the message alone rather than dropping the rest of it."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::unclosed_openers_keep_their_old_behaviour

attrs: doc = " `# task_progress RECOMMENDED` runs to the next section. A markdown"
doc = " heading is a section, so a heading between the block and the next tag"
doc = " ends it. Preferring `\\n<` regardless of position swallowed everything"
doc = " in between, here the whole `# Notes` section. The tag has to be one the"
doc = " earlier loops leave alone, which is every Cline tool tag."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::the_task_progress_block_ends_at_the_first_boundary

attrs: doc = " The block Cline really sends, so the boundary above is pinned against"
doc = " the shape it exists for and not only against the synthetic one. Cline"
doc = " pushes the focus-chain instructions as their own content part"
doc = " `userContent.push`), and no line inside them opens with `#` or `<`, so"
doc = " both searches come back empty and the whole block runs off the end of"
doc = " the string. Ending at the first boundary therefore changes nothing for"
doc = " a real transcript. Text mirrors cline's"
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::the_real_task_progress_block_is_removed_whole

attrs: doc = " Every index this file splices on comes from `str::find` and is a byte"
doc = " offset, so a message in a non-ASCII script has to come through intact:"
doc = " an offset that lands inside a multi-byte character panics with `byte"
doc = " index is not a char boundary` on the very next slice."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::multibyte_text_around_the_markers_survives

attrs: doc = " Feedback quoted ahead of the real block used to come back as `None`,"
doc = " because the closing tag found first sat before the opening one."
tests.name: parsers::cline::tests::feedback_is_read_from_its_own_closing_tag

attrs: doc = " codex-acp 1.8.0 forks BY REFERENCE: the child's rollout carries no"
doc = " alone it parses to zero turns, which is what put \"this session has no"
doc = " messages\" under every `[Fork] …` row. The parent's stream below the cut"
doc = " has to be spliced in."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_by_reference_fork_inherits_the_parent_history_up_to_the_cut

attrs: doc = " The OLD fork shape replays the parent inline and carries no"
doc = " `forked_from_ordinal_exclusive`. Splicing there would show every"
doc = " inherited turn twice, so the pointer alone must not trigger it."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::an_inline_replayed_fork_is_not_spliced_again

attrs: doc = " A reverted thread renders the prefix its CURRENT rollout inherits, then"
doc = " that rollout's own continuation — not the original file (stale, and"
doc = " still carrying the abandoned turn), and not the new file alone (which"
doc = " holds no history before the cut)."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_reverted_thread_renders_its_inherited_prefix_then_the_continuation

attrs: doc = " Both rollouts of a reverted thread carry its id, but only the current"
doc = " one is the conversation: the list shows the thread once, counted and"
doc = " titled from its effective history."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_reverted_thread_lists_once_from_its_current_rollout

attrs: doc = " Every revert adds a rollout, and a revert inside the previous revert's"
doc = " own turns points at THAT rollout — so a thread edited twice is three"
doc = " files deep, and each keeps only its part."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_thread_reverted_twice_keeps_each_rollouts_part

attrs: doc = " A revert further back than the previous revert's first turn points past"
doc = " that rollout, straight at the original: the rollout in between is"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_revert_behind_an_earlier_revert_discards_that_rollout

attrs: doc = " A fork of a reverted thread points at the rollout the parent was using"
doc = " when it forked — its revert, not the original that still carries the"
doc = " parent's thread id in its filename and the turns the revert dropped."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_fork_of_a_reverted_thread_inherits_the_history_it_was_cut_from

attrs: doc = " Reverting a fork keeps the fork's `forked_from_*` (its logical parent"
doc = " and cut) while `history_base` moves to the fork's own earlier rollout."
doc = " Following the fork pointer instead would skip every turn the fork took"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_reverted_fork_keeps_its_own_turns_from_before_the_revert

attrs: doc = " (codex's own reader still derives the cut from `history_base` for them)."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_fork_pointing_only_through_history_base_inherits_its_parent

attrs: doc = " Nothing caps the chain: a thread edited over and over is a long lineage,"
doc = " and dropping its root would lose the start of the conversation."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_long_revert_lineage_is_followed_to_its_root

attrs: doc = " A pointer is resolved by the rollout id the filename encodes. With the"
doc = " original rollout gone, a pointer to it has nothing to resolve to — a"
doc = " substring match would find the revert itself, which carries the same"
doc = " thread id in its name."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_pointer_never_resolves_to_a_rollout_that_merely_shares_the_thread_id

attrs: doc = " Malformed pointers that loop back end the chain instead of spinning."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_history_pointer_cycle_renders_what_it_reached

attrs: doc = " An inherited rollout that is there but fails to open fails the read, and"
doc = " nothing from that failure is remembered: once the file opens again the"
doc = " thread lists and renders whole. Rendering what was reached instead would"
doc = " have the summary cache, keyed on the unchanged current rollout, keep"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::an_inherited_rollout_that_fails_to_open_is_retried_not_remembered

attrs: doc = " `fork_turns` copies the PARENT's history into the child's head, and that"
doc = " copy carries the parent's own `session_meta` — on a real machine 23 of 46"
doc = " sub-agent rollouts hold a second header. That header declares no parent"
doc = " of its own, so reading `session_meta` last-record-wins clears the child's"
doc = " `parent_id` and the rollout lists as an importable root again. The FIRST"
doc = " header decides, exactly as `parse_codex_subagent_stats` already does via"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::replayed_parent_header_does_not_clear_the_child_parent_id

attrs: doc = " A by-reference fork keeps its history in the parent file, so"
doc = " `rollout_lines` splices the parent's lines in — including the parent's"
doc = " own `session_meta`. Reading identity last-record-wins then files the"
doc = " CHILD's summary under the PARENT's id and cwd: two rollouts claiming one"
doc = " id, which the conversation list dedups down to one and the fork"
doc = " disappears. Every identity field latches on the first header, not just"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::spliced_parent_header_does_not_steal_the_forked_child_identity

attrs: doc = " Both on-disk sub-agent shapes must surface `parent_id`, because that is"
doc = " the only thing keeping these rollouts out of the importer's root list"
doc = " The STRUCTURED case is the one that matters most: it is the shape every"
doc = " real sub-agent rollout carries, while the flat mirror only accompanies"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::native_parent_thread_is_preserved_in_list_and_detail

attrs: doc = " codex 0.129+ writes a generated image both as `event_msg.image_generation_end`"
doc = " and `response_item.image_generation_call`, sharing the same call_id/id."
doc = " The parser must surface exactly one ContentBlock::ImageGeneration per id."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::image_generation_end_and_call_dedupe_by_id

attrs: doc = " `event_msg.image_generation_end` ought to honor an explicit `mime_type`"
doc = " field when codex writes one (defensive fallback to image/png otherwise)."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::image_generation_end_honors_explicit_mime_type

attrs: doc = " Manual smoke check against a real codex JSONL captured locally."
doc = " `#[ignore]` so it doesn't run in CI; activate with"
doc = " while iterating on the parser locally."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::image_generation_smoke_real_session

attrs: doc = " When `revised_prompt` is absent in the payload, the parser must emit"
doc = " `revised_prompt: None` (codex's `imagegen` skill does not always echo"
doc = " the prompt back, e.g. when status=\"failed\")."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::image_generation_end_omits_revised_prompt_when_missing

attrs: doc = " Subagents in codex run inside the parent's JSONL, but their own"
doc = " transcripts are written to a separate `agent-<id>.jsonl`, so parent"
doc = " narration (messages / reasoning) is never gated on `active_agent_count`."
doc = " image_generation is the exception: a generated image carries no agent"
doc = " attribution, so one emitted inside a subagent window must be suppressed"
doc = " (`active_agent_count > 0`), otherwise the subagent's image leaks into the"
doc = " parent timeline as an inline ContentBlock::ImageGeneration."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::image_generation_inside_subagent_is_suppressed_in_parent

attrs: doc = " Codex surfaces one model response's reasoning twice: as per-section"
doc = " `event_msg.agent_reasoning` events (one per `**Header**` section) AND as a"
doc = " single `response_item.reasoning` whose `summary` array groups the same"
doc = " sections. History must render ONE 思考 card (live parity), so the grouped"
doc = " summary is parsed and the split events it restates are dropped — never one"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::reasoning_summary_groups_sections_into_single_thinking_block

attrs: doc = " A reasoning item with an empty (encrypted-only) summary carries no"
doc = " surfaced text — the common case in real rollouts — and must produce no"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::empty_reasoning_summary_emits_no_thinking_block

attrs: doc = " Defensive fallback: an interrupted rollout whose `agent_reasoning` events"
doc = " were written but that ended before the grouped `response_item.reasoning`"
doc = " summary must still surface the streaming reasoning — flushed at EOF as ONE"
doc = " joined Thinking block, not lost."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::streaming_reasoning_without_summary_flushes_as_one_block

attrs: doc = " Same fallback, but the reasoning is followed by more content with no"
doc = " grouped summary (schema drift): the flushed Thinking block must stay in"
doc = " order — before the assistant message that follows it, never appended last."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::streaming_reasoning_without_summary_keeps_order_before_next_message

attrs: doc = " One `response_item.reasoning` covers ONE model response. A long think"
doc = " spans several, so codex writes several of them back to back with nothing"
doc = " visible in between (up to 28 in a real rollout) — and live streams that"
doc = " as a single growing thought. History must too: the run is one 思考 card,"
doc = " and only a visible record (here a tool call) starts the next one."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::consecutive_reasoning_items_merge_into_one_thinking_block

attrs: doc = " An empty (encrypted-only) summary restates nothing, so it must not let a"
doc = " LATER summary — which only ever covers the sections after it — take the"
doc = " buffered sections before it down with the ones it supersedes."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::an_empty_reasoning_summary_mid_run_keeps_the_sections_before_it

attrs: doc = " A `token_count` that lands inside an open reasoning run reports what the"
doc = " response that produced that reasoning spent. The run's card does not"
doc = " exist yet, so the round must wait for it instead of being billed to the"
doc = " turn before — which would move real spend onto an unrelated reply."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_token_count_inside_a_reasoning_run_bills_the_runs_own_card

attrs: doc = " Multi-wait, no close (the real codex polling pattern): every parent"
doc = " narration in the active window must survive (incl. the final answer with"
doc = " no close), each `wait_agent` becomes its own `collab_agent` capsule built"
doc = " from only the agents IT returned, and the result text moves off the spawn"
doc = " execution capsule into those wait capsules."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::subagent_waits_emit_independent_collab_capsules_and_keep_narration

attrs: doc = " A sub-agent closed without ever being waited on: there is no wait capsule"
doc = " to host the result, so the execution capsule falls back to showing the"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::subagent_close_without_wait_falls_back_to_execution_capsule

attrs: doc = " A sub-agent closed (no wait) with a non-`completed` terminal result must"
doc = " keep that result AND mark the execution capsule failed — no data loss and"
doc = " live/history parity for errored no-wait closes."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::subagent_errored_close_without_wait_marks_execution_error

attrs: doc = " An errored wait marks BOTH its own wait capsule and the execution capsule"
doc = " as failed (the result text still lives only on the wait capsule)."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::subagent_errored_wait_marks_execution_error

attrs: doc = " The spawn execution capsule's input carries the sub-agent's `agent_id`"
doc = " (UUID), so the card can badge it uniformly with the wait capsule."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::subagent_spawn_capsule_input_carries_agent_id

attrs: doc = " A refused MCP call still lets the SCRIPT finish, so the wrapper's own"
doc = " `Script completed` says nothing about the call inside it. The card has to"
doc = " settle on the semantic item's outcome or it contradicts the result block"
doc = " written beside it. Shape taken verbatim from a real rollout: codeg-mcp"
doc = " refuses a `delegate_to_agent` past the delegation depth limit."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_failed_semantic_mcp_item_settles_its_card_as_failed

attrs: doc = " A tool whose SUCCESSFUL answer merely reads like a failure — it wraps a"
doc = " command and prints its exit code, or opens with `Error:` — must not be"
doc = " painted as a failed call. The record says `isError: false` outright, and"
doc = " an authoritative field beats the text heuristic that exists only because"
doc = " a script card has none."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::an_explicit_success_survives_output_text_that_reads_like_an_error

attrs: doc = " The semantic path throws the wrapper's printed output away, so a result"
doc = " that carries no text of its own must still be given something to say —"
doc = " otherwise a completed call reloads as a card with an empty body where"
doc = " the script card used to show the run."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_textless_semantic_result_still_says_something

attrs: doc = " The guard that keeps every correlation honest: a script that mixes an"
doc = " MCP call with a shell call publishes only ONE semantic item, so the"
doc = " items cannot be zipped onto the call sites. Real shape — a status poll"
doc = " racing a `write_stdin` — from a rollout on disk. The script card (or its"
doc = " static decomposition) has to keep the turn rather than let the lone item"
doc = " claim a site it may not own."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_script_mixing_mcp_and_shell_calls_keeps_its_static_reading

attrs: doc = " A script that threw keeps its own card even when its one MCP call did"
doc = " publish a semantic item. The wrapper's `Script error:` text is the whole"
doc = " story of that turn — which line threw, and after which call — and the"
doc = " semantic path DISCARDS it. The count gate cannot stand in for this: a"
doc = " script can throw after its last call answered, leaving exactly as many"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_thrown_script_keeps_its_own_card_over_a_matching_semantic_item

attrs: doc = " The sink is what makes a preview bounded: it has to STOP the writer, not"
doc = " grow to fit it. Without the refusal, `serde_json` would keep handing it"
doc = " the rest of a base64 blob."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_budgeted_sink_stops_at_its_budget

attrs: doc = " Reading a value through a budget must be INDISTINGUISHABLE from"
doc = " serializing the whole thing and cutting it — otherwise the bound is a"
doc = " behavior change wearing a performance fix's clothes. The cases that can"
doc = " tell them apart: a value that fits, one landing exactly on the cap, one"
doc = " far past it, and one whose characters are multi-byte, where the byte cut"
doc = " lands mid-character and decoding leaves a replacement char behind."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_budgeted_preview_reads_exactly_like_an_unbounded_one

attrs: doc = " The marker search reads a block's own outcome fields and stops there."
doc = " Walking on into `data` would read the PAYLOAD — the base64 the cap"
doc = " refuses to copy, which the text heuristic would then lowercase into a"
doc = " second copy of itself. This pins the VERDICT that follows from that (a"
doc = " payload reading like an error is still just bytes); what it cannot see"
doc = " is the cost, so the reasoning lives on `blocks_report_failure`."
doc = " (Under the cap nothing is cut, so the ordinary preview path parses the"
doc = " whole thing exactly as it always has — that is not this arm's business.)"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::an_oversized_block_payload_is_never_read_as_an_outcome

attrs: doc = " The block fallback IS truncated, so its outcome must not be read back"
doc = " out of the cut string — the blocks themselves decide. Same failure as"
doc = " the structured case: parse a truncated document and you get nothing,"
doc = " and nothing reads as success."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_long_block_failure_survives_its_own_truncation

attrs: doc = " Why the structured answer is the one preview that is NOT truncated: it"
doc = " is read twice. The card shows it, and the error heuristic re-parses it"
doc = " — a preview opening with `{` is parsed back into JSON and searched for"
doc = " a failed `status`. Cut that JSON and the parse fails silently, and a"
doc = " call that reported failure settles GREEN. The padding is what makes the"
doc = " record longer than any cap worth applying, and it sorts before `status`"
doc = " so a cut would take the status with it."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_long_structured_failure_is_not_cut_into_a_success

attrs: doc = " The outcome precedence, stated once against the fields themselves rather"
doc = " than through four rollouts: a stated failure outranks a stated success,"
doc = " a stated success outranks output text that merely reads like a failure,"
doc = " and the text heuristic still decides a record that states nothing."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_semantic_records_stated_outcome_outranks_its_output_text

attrs: doc = " `text(x.output); text(\\`exit_code=…\\`)` — two chunks per call, so the 1:1"
doc = " count fails and the whole thing used to stay one script card."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_trailing_chunk_per_call_still_splits_per_call

attrs: doc = " The other half of the shape: a `---RESULT n---` header ahead of each"
doc = " output. The counter differs per call, so the repeat is only visible with"
doc = " digits blinded — and each chunk of the group is unwrapped on its own, so"
doc = " an envelope behind a header still reads as a terminal."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_numbered_header_per_call_still_splits_per_call

attrs: doc = " The adversarial version of the shape above: the second command's own"
doc = " stdout IS `exit_code=0`, so slot 1 of every assumed pair repeats and the"
doc = " chunk content alone stops telling the two loops apart. Only the script"
doc = " says which it is — two loops, so no grouping."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_command_whose_output_mimics_the_marker_does_not_force_a_grouping

attrs: doc = " Dividing evenly is NOT the proof. This script prints every output and"
doc = " then every exit code — the same 6 chunks for 3 calls as the interleaved"
doc = " shape above, in an order where grouping them in pairs would pin call 2's"
doc = " output to call 1's card. Only the script says which shape it is."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::chunks_that_merely_divide_evenly_are_not_grouped

attrs: doc = " One call, one line, and the line is the raw result object — the shape"
doc = " that used to leave a card whose entire body was `{\"chunk_id\":…}`."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_collapsed_single_call_blob_still_shows_its_output

attrs: doc = " Past the cap codex drops whole lines — and it drops them from the middle,"
doc = " so a survivor's position no longer names its call. Measured: with a line"
doc = " missing, 13 of 57 checkable lines belong to a different command than"
doc = " their position claims. Splitting anyway would put a command's output"
doc = " under another command's title, so the script card stays."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_collapsed_blob_missing_a_line_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " The same banner fronts the far more common case: ONE command whose own"
doc = " stdout was too long. Its lines are stdout, not `text()` results, and"
doc = " splitting them would shred one command's output across every card."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_truncated_command_output_is_not_read_as_one_line_per_call

attrs: doc = " Fewer `text()` chunks than calls means chunk *i* is NOT provably call"
doc = " *i*'s output — keep one script card rather than misattribute."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::code_mode_mismatched_chunks_keep_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " An interrupted turn never writes the output record; the script card must"
doc = " stay where it was rather than vanish or jump to the end."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::code_mode_call_without_output_keeps_its_script_card

attrs: doc = " The unified-exec `wait` tool shares code mode's array output shape; it"
doc = " used to render as a raw `[{\"text\":\"Script completed…` JSON blob."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::wait_tool_output_is_joined_text_not_raw_json

attrs: doc = " A call that gets a card of its own — here a `wait` that also kills the"
doc = " session — is titled by the command it is acting on, not by the bare tool"
doc = " name. (A call that only collects output gets no card at all; see"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::wait_carries_the_command_whose_session_it_polls

attrs: doc = " A `wait` / `write_stdin` that only collects output is the earlier command"
doc = " still running — not a second command. Before this, a `cargo test` cut"
doc = " short by unified-exec's yield showed as two adjacent cards with the same"
doc = " title, the first holding a few lines of output and the second holding"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::polling_a_background_session_appends_to_the_card_of_its_command

attrs: doc = " The chunk envelope in its object form — what a script that prints its"
doc = " `exec_command` result verbatim leaves behind. Unwrapped to the output it"
doc = " carries, exactly like the string form's header is stripped, so a folded"
doc = " session does not read as JSON followed by terminal output."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_code_mode_exec_result_shows_its_output_not_its_envelope

attrs: doc = " Keystrokes are an action, not a poll: they earn a card, and everything"
doc = " the session prints afterwards belongs below that card rather than folded"
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::keystrokes_get_a_card_and_end_the_folding

attrs: doc = " A command's own JSON stdout may well carry `chunk_id` and `output`."
doc = " Truncating it to the `output` field would silently drop the rest, so the"
doc = " whole envelope shape has to be there before anything is unwrapped."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::json_stdout_that_only_resembles_an_envelope_is_left_whole

attrs: doc = " One `tools.exec_command` call site driven by a loop is many commands. The"
doc = " first command literal in the source is then just a guess, and a session"
doc = " some later command started would be titled — and folded — under it."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_looped_call_site_attributes_no_session

attrs: doc = " The numeric session id and the hex chunk id name the same cell. Once a"
doc = " keystroke earns a card, a poll arriving through the *other* spelling must"
doc = " not still fold its output in above that card."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::an_action_ends_the_folding_for_every_alias_of_its_session

attrs: doc = " codex names sessions after pids, and pids come back around. Whichever"
doc = " command announced an id last owns it: its polls must land on its own"
doc = " card, never on the card of the command that held the id before."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_reused_session_id_binds_to_whoever_announced_it_last

attrs: doc = " A `wait` answers with what the script printed SINCE it parked, not with"
doc = " the whole run. Rewriting the cards from that answer alone would drop"
doc = " whatever the script had already printed — and decompose against a chunk"
doc = " count missing its front, so a two-call script could end up undecomposable"
doc = " and leave its `call_1#i` cards without results."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_deferred_script_keeps_what_it_printed_before_the_wait

attrs: doc = " The reported card: truncation ate two separators, so the span after"
doc = " `formula-service` holds three commands' output with no boundary. The"
doc = " commands it provably brackets still get their own output; the ones whose"
doc = " separator is gone say so instead of being handed someone else's."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_truncated_separator_leaves_its_command_without_output

attrs: doc = " A command that printed the separator itself makes the line ambiguous;"
doc = " the whole candidate is refused rather than cutting on the wrong one."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_repeated_separator_line_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " Only a line some separator actually predicts can make a candidate"
doc = " ambiguous. Two commands printing the same ordinary line is the normal"
doc = " case — `index_body_lines` marks it repeated, but nothing looks it up."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_repeated_output_line_still_splits

attrs: doc = " One separator divides nothing: it would hand the whole blob to the first"
doc = " command and leave the rest blank."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::a_single_surviving_separator_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " Separators in the wrong order are not this script's separator run."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::separators_out_of_order_keep_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " Scripts that number their results instead of naming them split the same"
doc = " way — the hole is the loop index."
tests.name: parsers::codex::tests::numbered_separators_split_a_collapsed_blob

attrs: doc = " Same two `text()` calls, same chunk count — but two passes, so the chunks"
doc = " arrive output-output-exit-exit and cannot be grouped per call."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::two_passes_over_the_results_do_not_group

attrs: doc = " The same two passes with the calls hoisted into helpers: the `text()`"
doc = " calls now sit side by side at the top of the script, so only the loop"
doc = " body — not their neighbourhood — tells the shapes apart."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::text_calls_hoisted_out_of_the_loop_do_not_group

attrs: doc = " The loop header names the binding, but the array it walks was turned"
doc = " around in place before it got there — so group *i* is call *n - 1 - i*"
doc = " even though every other check passes."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_results_array_reordered_before_the_loop_does_not_group

attrs: doc = " `++` is an update, not two `+` in a row — and it can move the counter"
doc = " out from under the very read that names the call."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_prefix_update_inside_an_argument_does_not_group

attrs: doc = " `forEach` takes a second argument, and it runs before the first"
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_foreach_second_argument_does_not_group

attrs: doc = " The calls are recovered in source order, so the array `Promise.all`"
doc = " receives has to be the one written at the call sites — reordered from"
doc = " outside, or from within by a spread."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_reordered_promise_all_argument_does_not_group

attrs: doc = " `` tag`…` `` calls `tag`. Reading it as a string would let the body run"
doc = " code the grammar never sees."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_tagged_template_is_not_a_string

attrs: doc = " A literal that never closes means the rest cannot be read with any"
doc = " confidence — say nothing, and do not panic saying it."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::malformed_literals_are_refused_without_panicking

attrs: doc = " `${…}` is code, not text. A mutation hidden in one is still a mutation."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_mutation_inside_a_template_hole_does_not_group

attrs: doc = " `forEach` hands its callback the array itself as a third argument, which"
doc = " is an alias no lexical check on `r` can see."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_foreach_callback_taking_the_array_does_not_group

attrs: doc = " Every `text()` is inside the one loop body, but they run from a callback"
doc = " scheduled per iteration, so what they print need not arrive in the order"
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::deferred_work_inside_the_loop_does_not_group

attrs: doc = " The counter is what makes the index form ordered. Writing to it — or to"
doc = " the slot it reads — takes that away."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::writing_to_the_counter_or_its_slot_does_not_group

attrs: doc = " One loop, contiguous groups — but walking the results backwards, so"
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_reversed_walk_does_not_group

attrs: doc = " `//text()` is an XPath inside a command string, not a call site — 11 of"
doc = " the sampled candidate scripts pass exactly this to `xmllint`."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::text_inside_a_command_string_is_not_a_call_site

attrs: doc = " One call SITE is not one invocation, and arguments reached through a"
doc = " variable are only that variable's FIRST value — `job.cmd = cmd` inside a"
doc = " loop runs commands this scanner never sees. `args_inline` is what"
doc = " separates a recovered command that provably ran from one that is a"
doc = " guess; only the former may be credited with a background session."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::arguments_reached_through_a_variable_are_not_proof_of_what_ran

attrs: doc = " A `wait` may address the cell by the envelope's hex chunk id instead of"
doc = " the numeric session id inside it. Both spellings appear in real"
doc = " transcripts for the same cell."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::chunk_ids_are_read_from_both_envelope_forms

attrs: doc = " Substituted arguments were not written at the call site, so they must"
doc = " not be treated as proof of what ran — `register_shell_sessions` reads"
doc = " this flag to decide whether a background session may be attributed."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::expanded_calls_never_claim_inline_arguments

attrs: doc = " Everything below is a way the parameters could stop holding their row's"
doc = " values before the call happens. None of them may expand."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_call_between_the_binding_and_the_tool_call_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " A `${…}` hole is code. Skipping template literals the way the string"
doc = " scanners do would let this one through."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_reassigning_template_hole_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " A template's literal text is not code, but the comment scanner cannot"
doc = " tell: the `//` of a URL would start a line comment and swallow the rest"
doc = " of the line — the `${cmd = …}` included."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_template_hiding_a_reassignment_behind_a_url_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " `let cmd = …` is a declaration by every syntactic measure, and shadows"
doc = " the row's `cmd` all the same."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_declaration_shadowing_a_parameter_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " A declaration that shadows nothing is still fine."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_declaration_of_a_fresh_name_still_expands

attrs: doc = " `Array.map`'s second argument is `thisArg`: it is evaluated ONCE, not"
doc = " per row. Expanding it per row would invent commands that never ran, so"
doc = " it stays the single call it is."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_call_in_the_maps_second_argument_is_not_expanded_per_row

attrs: doc = " A regex body is not code, and must not be read as any. `//` inside a"
doc = " character class would otherwise open a line comment and swallow the"
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_regex_hiding_a_reassignment_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " An unbalanced bracket inside a regex would leave the depth counter"
doc = " raised, hiding the `,` that ends the callback."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_regex_bracket_does_not_hide_the_maps_second_argument

attrs: doc = " A `${…}` hole is code wherever it appears, including in the template a"
doc = " script builds while walking the table."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_template_hole_reordering_the_table_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " The templates these scripts actually write name the row bindings, not"
doc = " the table, and must keep working."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_template_naming_the_row_bindings_still_expands

attrs: doc = " The rows the callback sees are not the rows as written once something"
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_table_reordered_before_the_walk_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " Reaching the table from inside the callback can reorder it mid-walk."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_table_touched_inside_the_walk_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " Reading the table AFTER the walk is how these scripts label their"
doc = " output, and cannot affect what the walk saw."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::reading_the_table_after_the_walk_still_expands

attrs: doc = " `tools.exec_command({cmd} && job)` runs `job`, not the literal."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::arguments_that_are_not_the_whole_argument_keep_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " A single row is a single call; the plain scanner already covers the"
doc = " shapes it can, and one row proves nothing about repetition."
tests.name: parsers::codex_code_mode::tests::a_one_row_table_keeps_the_script_card

attrs: doc = " ACP-written stores carry no root `turn_timings` and no"
doc = " `lastUsedModel`; the turn clock must come from the tool calls'"
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::synthesizes_turn_clock_from_tool_call_stamps

attrs: doc = " Tool-free turns have no clock anywhere in the store (no root"
doc = " `turn_timings`, no tool stamps, no message timestamps — verified on"
doc = " real ACP sessions). codeg's own turn-span journal fills them, and the"
doc = " alignment is tail-anchored: a leading turn recorded before the journal"
doc = " feature existed stays honestly clockless."
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::fills_tool_free_turn_clock_from_timing_journal

attrs: doc = " Real-device bug (session 118b6805): a 16s turn whose only clock was a"
doc = " sub-second tool span rendered \"0 秒\". A matched journal line REPLACES"
doc = " the tool-span fallback — the span covers first-tool-start →"
doc = " last-tool-end only, while the journal measured the full"
doc = " prompt→`end_turn` wall span at the connection."
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_replaces_tool_span_fallback_clock

attrs: doc = " authoritative: a matched journal line only corroborates, never"
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_never_overrides_store_native_root_timing

attrs: doc = " A degenerate journal line (zero span — no duration to offer, and"
doc = " unable to bracket a real tool span) never erases an existing"
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::degenerate_journal_line_keeps_tool_span_clock

attrs: doc = " Codex-review scenario: the documented missing-suffix residual pairs a"
doc = " STALE line (recorded for an older identical prompt) with the store's"
doc = " newest turn. When that turn carries a tool-span clock, the stale line"
doc = " — which ended before this turn's tools even started — must not"
doc = " replace it: the containment guard rejects any line that doesn't"
doc = " bracket the existing span. (Clockless turns have no clock to lose;"
doc = " for them the residual stands, pinned by"
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::stale_journal_line_never_overrides_tool_span_clock

attrs: doc = " Codex-review scenario: the journal's same-hash run is LONGER than the"
doc = " store's (an identical prompt whose turn the store didn't keep). Counts"
doc = " are equal overall, so only the run-length equality guard stands"
doc = " between the walk and handing the wrong span to the older identical"
doc = " prompt — it must stop and assign nothing."
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_longer_duplicate_run_assigns_nothing

attrs: doc = " Codex re-review scenario: a stalled (timeout-abandoned) append for"
doc = " turn A lands AFTER turn B's line, so the journal order is [B, A] while"
doc = " the store order is [A, B]. The two same-hash runs have EQUAL length,"
doc = " so the run guard alone would pair them swapped — the reader's order"
doc = " gate must reject the whole journal so nothing is assigned. No turn"
doc = " may wear the other's span."
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_reordered_equal_hash_run_never_swaps_spans

attrs: doc = " Codex R3 scenario — stale pseudo-tail: with prefix TRUNCATION (the"
doc = " rejected design) the surviving prefix's last entry could pair with a"
doc = " LATER same-hash turn across the gap. Store [A\"x\", B\"重试\", C\"重试\","
doc = " D\"z\", E\"重试\"], file landed [A, C, B, D, E] (B stalled): truncation"
doc = " would keep [A, C] and E would wear C's span. Whole-journal rejection"
doc = " must leave every turn clockless instead."
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_disorder_leaves_no_stale_pseudo_tail

attrs: doc = " Codex R5 scenario — interior journal gap: store [x, y, x, z] but the"
doc = " journal only has lines for the FIRST x (ord 1) and z (ord 4) — y was"
doc = " skipped (non-`end_turn`) and the third turn's line was dropped at the"
doc = " queue. Without the ordinal trim, the reverse walk pairs z correctly"
doc = " and then slides the FIRST x's span onto the THIRD turn (hashes match,"
doc = " contiguous runs are both length 1, counts pass). The trailing"
doc = " ordinal-contiguity trim must trust only [z]: z gets its span, the"
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_gap_never_slides_onto_older_same_hash_entry

attrs: doc = " ACCEPTED RESIDUAL (Codex R7) — this test PINS a known limitation, it"
doc = " does not bless it as desirable. When the session's newest turns ALL"
doc = " lost their journal lines (canceled/empty turns are deliberately"
doc = " unjournaled; queue-full drops), an older line remains the journal"
doc = " tail, and if the store's newest turn hash-collides with it while the"
doc = " same-hash run lengths align (here: [x, y, x] with only the FIRST x"
doc = " journaled — the y between breaks the store-side run), the old span is"
doc = " attributed to the newer turn. Closing this needs a store-side"
doc = " persistence/tail anchor Cursor does not expose. If this test starts"
doc = " failing because the misattribution no longer happens, the residual"
doc = " was closed — update the docs in `turn_timings` and flip these"
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::accepted_residual_missing_tail_lines_can_misattribute_span

attrs: doc = " Codex R6 scenario — cross-connection ordinal coincidence: the old"
doc = " connection journaled its first \"x\" as ord 1; a RESUMED connection's"
doc = " first turn (ord 1) was canceled-unjournaled and its second turn \"z\""
doc = " landed as ord 2. `1 → 2` is numerically consecutive but spans two"
doc = " connections — trusting it would slide the old x's span onto the"
doc = " store's third turn. The trim must require equal `conn`: only [z] is"
doc = " trusted; z gets its span, everything older stays clockless."
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_connection_boundary_breaks_ordinal_contiguity

attrs: doc = " Codex R4-2 scenario — non-contiguous phantom: the store kept only"
doc = " `A:\"x\"`, but a (hand-built / legacy) journal carries three monotonic"
doc = " lines `[x, y, x]` — e.g. two later turns canceled before Cursor"
doc = " persisted them. Tail pairing would hand the LAST \"x\" line's span to"
doc = " store-A (both contiguous runs have length 1, so the run guard is"
doc = " blind). The count guard (journal longer than the store's user turns)"
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_with_more_entries_than_store_turns_assigns_nothing

attrs: doc = " The guard must NOT over-block the legitimate case: equal-length"
doc = " duplicate runs (both prompts persisted) pair 1:1 and both turns get"
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_equal_duplicate_runs_pair_one_to_one

attrs: doc = " A journal whose tail does NOT hash-match the last user turn must"
doc = " assign nothing — the walk stops instead of scanning, which could"
doc = " misattribute a span to an earlier identical prompt."
tests.name: parsers::cursor::tests::journal_tail_mismatch_assigns_nothing

attrs: doc = " Each log turn keeps its OWN opening message id — a turn must not inherit"
doc = " the previous one's, which would fork at the wrong place silently."
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::each_turn_carries_its_own_opening_message_id

attrs: doc = " A turn whose first rendered block came from a tool result (a log read"
doc = " from a truncated prefix) still adopts the id of the next assistant"
doc = " message in the same turn."
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::a_turn_opened_by_a_tool_result_still_adopts_a_later_message_id

attrs: doc = " No usable id in the log leaves the field honestly empty — an empty"
doc = " string would be an id the adapter cannot match while claiming it can,"
doc = " and `acp::fork` forks by content fingerprint in that case instead."
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::a_message_without_an_id_leaves_the_fork_point_unnamed

attrs: doc = " A write open migrates the log and publishes the successor WITHOUT"
doc = " deleting the source, so both names sit in one directory and the older"
doc = " one is frozen at the migration point. Reading it would show a truncated"
doc = " history as if it were current — silently."
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::a_retained_predecessor_never_wins_over_the_published_successor

attrs: doc = " The rule is \"highest canonical generation\", not \"3\"."
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::a_future_generation_outranks_the_current_one

attrs: doc = " The live-append race is handled INSIDE the selected generation: the"
doc = " decoded prefix of a half-written tail is the answer, never the stale"
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::a_torn_tail_yields_the_selected_generations_prefix_not_the_predecessor

attrs: doc = " An empty newest generation is an empty session, NOT a licence to show"
doc = " the predecessor. Upstream is explicit that retained predecessors provide"
doc = " no fallback, and presenting pre-migration history as current is worse"
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::an_empty_newest_generation_does_not_fall_back_to_the_predecessor

attrs: doc = " Same rule for a newest generation that reads fine but does not DECODE —"
doc = " a separate branch from the empty file above, and the one an"
doc = " implementation that only guards `fs::read` errors would get wrong."
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::an_undecodable_newest_generation_does_not_fall_back_to_the_predecessor

attrs: doc = " And for one that cannot be read at all. Unix-only: Windows has no"
doc = " equivalent of clearing the read bit through `fs::set_permissions`."
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::an_unreadable_newest_generation_does_not_fall_back_to_the_predecessor

attrs: doc = " A root holding both encodings is malformed by upstream's own rule (a"
doc = " root belongs to one encoding). Generations are therefore compared WITHIN"
doc = " an encoding, and the compressed set wins — `deepseek-acp` never"
doc = " configures `compression`, so every generation it writes is compressed."
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::a_mixed_encoding_root_reads_the_compressed_set

attrs: doc = " `readdir` can fail AFTER yielding entries — a stale NFS handle, a FUSE"
doc = " mount erroring mid-stream. Keeping what arrived would crown the retained"
doc = " predecessor exactly when the successor is the entry that never came, so"
doc = " a partial listing has to yield nothing instead — even though the"
doc = " predecessor is right there and perfectly readable. No temporary"
doc = " directory can be made to fail this way, hence the injected listing."
tests.name: parsers::deepseek::tests::a_broken_listing_does_not_fall_back_to_a_readable_predecessor

attrs: doc = " The shape every ACP-driven session actually has: the messages live ONLY"
doc = " inside a `$set.messages` array. This used to parse as zero messages."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::jsonl_rebuilds_history_from_set_messages

attrs: doc = " `$set.messages` REPLACES the history wholesale (upstream clears the map"
