doc = " first), and bare records appended afterwards extend it."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::jsonl_set_messages_replaces_then_appends

attrs: doc = " `$rewindTo` drops the target and everything after it."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::jsonl_rewind_truncates_from_target

attrs: doc = " A rewind onto an id that is no longer present clears the WHOLE history"
doc = " upstream, rather than leaving it untouched."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::jsonl_rewind_to_unknown_id_clears_everything

attrs: doc = " A repeated id REPLACES the record in place: the position is the first"
doc = " one seen, and fields the newer record omits do NOT survive."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::jsonl_repeated_id_replaces_whole_record_in_place

attrs: doc = " One unparseable line must not take the whole transcript down with it."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::jsonl_skips_malformed_lines

attrs: doc = " A `.jsonl` file that is really one pretty-printed JSON object falls back"
doc = " to the legacy single-record reader."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::jsonl_falls_back_to_legacy_single_object

attrs: doc = " A brand-new session whose history never changed carries metadata only —"
doc = " `updateMessagesFromHistory` writes nothing when nothing moved. It must"
doc = " still list, just with no messages."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::jsonl_metadata_only_session_still_lists

attrs: doc = " `$set.summary` outranks both `update_topic` and the first user message."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::jsonl_prefers_metadata_summary_for_title

attrs: doc = " Subagent transcripts live one directory deeper and have no `session-`"
doc = " prefix. They must be discovered, attributed to the right project, and"
doc = " marked as children so they never import as root conversations."
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::discovers_subagent_transcripts_as_children

attrs: doc = " `$set.directories` backs up folder resolution when the alias is unknown"
tests.name: parsers::gemini::tests::falls_back_to_metadata_directories_for_folder_path

attrs: doc = " Grok 4.6 injects monitor completion as `<monitor-event>` *before*"
doc = " `task_completed` and the later `<system-reminder> Monitor \"id\" ended`."
doc = " Session 4972 used this shape; treating it as a wake trigger is what"
doc = " keeps the follow-up assistant from merging into the first bubble."
tests.name: parsers::grok::tests::monitor_event_terminal_is_a_verified_wake_trigger

attrs: doc = " A `get_command_or_subagent_output` poll carries its whole result in"
doc = " `rawOutput` (no `content[]`, no `output_for_prompt`), which used to be"
doc = " dropped — leaving the card empty. It must reach the frontend verbatim so"
doc = " the background-task card can render command/status/exit code/output."
tests.name: parsers::grok::tests::background_task_poll_surfaces_task_output_envelope

attrs: doc = " Grok injects reminders as `user_message_chunk`s flagged"
doc = " `_meta.hideFromScrollback`. Rendering them as user bubbles split one reply"
doc = " into two turns with a raw `<system-reminder>` wedged between."
tests.name: parsers::grok::tests::hidden_user_chunk_does_not_split_the_reply

attrs: doc = " Session 4972 order: hidden `<monitor-event> DONE` arrives *before*"
doc = " `task_completed will_wake=true`, then the wake reply. Clearing the"
doc = " parked trigger on that completion would leave the wake unlabeled, and"
doc = " the UI would fold it into the first assistant bubble."
tests.name: parsers::grok::tests::monitor_event_before_task_completed_marks_following_assistant

attrs: doc = " A plain (non-image) file attachment. This parser folded resources"
doc = " itself and had no `resource_link` case at all, so an attached file came"
doc = " back from history as an empty block — the same gap `acp_native` had."
doc = " Both now go through the one projection a viewer saw live."
tests.name: parsers::grok::tests::plain_file_attachments_survive_a_reload_as_their_markers

attrs: doc = " Grok's own catalog outranks the id-shaped guess. The fixture's session"
doc = " model (summary `current_model_id` = `grok-4.5`) would infer 500K from its"
doc = " name, so a distinct cached window proves the ring read `models_cache.json`"
tests.name: parsers::grok::tests::context_window_prefers_groks_models_cache

attrs: doc = " A BYO endpoint (`[model.<id>]` in `config.toml`) never appears in the"
doc = " fetched catalog, so its declared window is the second source."
tests.name: parsers::grok::tests::context_window_falls_back_to_byo_config_toml

attrs: doc = " No catalog on disk (the common case for a machine that only ever ran"
doc = " grok through codeg) → the name heuristic still supplies a window."
tests.name: parsers::grok::tests::context_window_falls_back_to_the_name_heuristic

attrs: doc = " The placeholder test has to match the whole shape, not just the prefix:"
doc = " \"New session - \" is a legal thing for a person to call a session, and"
doc = " renaming one to that must not send it back to the fallback."
tests.name: parsers::opencode::tests::only_opencodes_own_generated_name_counts_as_untitled

attrs: doc = " OpenCode names a session before anyone has spoken and is supposed to"
doc = " replace that name on the first turn — but the call is forked and its"
doc = " errors swallowed, so an unreachable small model leaves every session"
doc = " called \"New session - <timestamp>\" forever. Stand in for it the same way"
doc = " OpenCode's own TUI does: with the opening user message."
tests.name: parsers::opencode::tests::a_placeholder_title_gives_way_to_what_the_user_actually_said

attrs: doc = " The fallback runs the same folding and capping every other agent's"
doc = " derived title does, so a session opened with a file mention is named"
doc = " after the label rather than a truncated `file://` URL."
tests.name: parsers::opencode::tests::a_derived_title_is_folded_and_capped_like_every_other_agents

attrs: doc = " 128000`, and the entry REPLACES any built-in of the same id. So a listed"
doc = " model that declares nothing is not unknown — it is 128K, including for"
doc = " an id codeg's own name table would answer differently. This is the shape"
doc = " codeg's Pi settings panel writes (`apply_pi_custom_model` records `id` +"
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::a_listed_model_without_a_window_takes_pi_s_own_default

attrs: doc = " One provider listing an id twice: pi's `applyModelsJson` upserts in file"
doc = " order, so the second entry overwrites the first and 100K is what pi"
doc = " runs with. Reading the first instead would report 9× the room."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::a_repeated_model_id_resolves_to_its_last_declaration

attrs: doc = " `modelOverrides` is the topmost layer in pi's composer, and it patches:"
doc = " a window there wins, its absence leaves the layer below in charge."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::a_model_override_wins_over_the_models_entry

attrs: doc = " The lookup only pays off if `get_conversation` actually consults it —"
doc = " and only if the declaration OUTRANKS the name table, which is the whole"
doc = " point (a proxy in front of a known model id serves a window the table"
doc = " cannot know). `sample_records` runs `claude-sonnet-4-6`, which the table"
doc = " answers with 200K, so the two readings are distinguishable."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::a_declared_window_outranks_the_name_table_through_get_conversation

attrs: doc = " Regression: a `bash` result is an MCP block array, and serializing it"
doc = " painted the terminal card with the JSON source string"
doc = " (`[{\"text\":\"$ next build\\n…\",\"type\":\"text\"}]`) instead of the output."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::tool_result_content_shapes

attrs: doc = " REGRESSION: pi's thinking block spells its payload `thinking`, not `text`"
doc = " (`docs/session-format.md`; 21/21 blocks in real local transcripts carry"
doc = " nothing, so every reasoning block pi had ever written was dropped on the"
doc = " floor — silently, because an unmatched block is simply skipped."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::thinking_block_reads_pi_field_name

attrs: doc = " The `text` fallback exists only so a future upstream rename degrades"
doc = " instead of regressing to the same silent drop."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::thinking_block_falls_back_to_text_field

attrs: doc = " REGRESSION: a pi session file is a TREE. After the user rewinds and asks"
doc = " something else (`/tree`, or re-prompting from an earlier entry), the"
doc = " abandoned reply is STILL in the file — pi branches in place. pi itself"
doc = " renders only the path from the last entry back to the root"
doc = " (`_buildIndex` + `buildSessionPath`), so reading the file linearly spliced"
doc = " a reply the user had thrown away into the middle of the conversation."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::abandoned_branch_is_not_rendered

attrs: doc = " A v1 (pre-tree) session has no `id`/`parentId` at all. There is no leaf to"

doc = " be able to empty a conversation it cannot analyze."

attrs: doc = " REGRESSION: re-editing the FIRST prompt forks at the virtual root. pi's"
doc = " `/tree` branches from `targetEntry.parentId`, which for the first user"
doc = " message is `null`, so it calls `resetLeaf()` and appends the replacement"
doc = " with `parentId: null` — two explicit roots, no shared parent entry. Fork"
doc = " detection that only counted resolvable parents saw no fork here and kept"
doc = " the abandoned first exchange in the transcript."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::root_reedit_fork_drops_the_abandoned_first_branch

attrs: doc = " A file with a BROKEN chain but no fork keeps everything. Pruning exists to"
doc = " drop an abandoned branch; with no parent holding two children there is no"
doc = " branch, so an unreachable entry is a defect in the file — and silently"
doc = " deleting a user's messages over a defect is far worse than showing a"
doc = " record pi would have skipped."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::broken_chain_without_a_fork_keeps_every_record

attrs: doc = " A `parentId` chain that loops must terminate rather than hang."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::cyclic_parent_chain_terminates

attrs: doc = " pi's `getSessionName()` scans backwards, so a `/name` rename is the title."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::last_session_info_wins

attrs: doc = " `getSessionName()` scans `getEntries()` — every PHYSICAL entry — backwards"
doc = " and returns at the first `session_info` it reaches. So a `/name` issued on"
doc = " a branch the user later abandoned still names the session (the name is"
doc = " session-wide, not branch-scoped), and a latest entry with an empty name"
doc = " CLEARS the name rather than letting an older one resurface."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::session_name_follows_pi_over_all_physical_entries

attrs: doc = " pi's `edit` writes a one-line receipt into `content` and the real unified"
doc = " diff into `details.patch`. Surfacing the receipt made an edit whose LIVE"
doc = " card renders a full diff collapse to a sentence once reopened."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::edit_result_surfaces_the_unified_patch

attrs: doc = " A `details.patch` that is not a unified diff must NOT displace pi's own"
doc = " text — the swap is only worth doing when the renderer can parse it."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::non_diff_details_patch_leaves_the_text_alone

attrs: doc = " and a user can attach one the same way. Both used to be dropped, leaving"
doc = " only pi's \"Read image file […]\" placeholder."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::images_survive_in_prompts_and_tool_results

attrs: doc = " REGRESSION: `exitCode` is `number | undefined` — an interrupted run never"
doc = " gets one — so defaulting a missing code to `0` painted a Ctrl-C'd command"
doc = " as a success. The truncation notice keeps a prefix from reading as the"
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::cancelled_and_truncated_bash_executions_are_marked

attrs: doc = " A clean run stays clean — no notices, no error."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::successful_bash_execution_is_untouched

attrs: doc = " `stopReason: \"error\"` is the only trace a failed provider call leaves; its"
doc = " content is usually empty, so the turn used to render blank or vanish."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::errored_assistant_turn_surfaces_the_error

attrs: doc = " A compaction renders through the same provider-neutral pair every other"
doc = " agent's compaction uses (`_meta.contextCompaction` + a settled result)."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::compaction_becomes_the_shared_divider_pair

attrs: doc = " `/tree`'s branch recap and a displayed extension message are conversation,"
doc = " not bookkeeping — both become System turns."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::branch_summary_and_custom_message_become_system_turns

attrs: doc = " back to `<agentDir>/sessions`, so a user who sets it kept a pi that"
doc = " resumed fine and a codeg history list that was permanently empty."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::settings_json_session_dir_is_honored

attrs: doc = " REGRESSION: a RELATIVE `sessionDir` must fall through to the default."
doc = " pi's `normalizePath` leaves a relative value relative, and the pi process"
doc = " runs with the ACP session's WORKSPACE as its cwd (pi-acp's"
doc = " `PiRpcProcess.spawn` passes `cwd: params.cwd`) — so pi's own documented"
doc = " `<workspace>/.pi/sessions`, which this parser cannot name. Resolving it"
doc = " against the agent dir pointed at a directory nobody writes to AND shadowed"
doc = " the default, costing the user the history pi had already written to"
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::relative_settings_session_dir_falls_back_to_the_default

attrs: doc = " A DRIVE-relative `sessionDir` falls through for the same reason a plain"
doc = " relative one does: `\\srv\\x` (and `/srv/x`) carries a root but no drive"
doc = " prefix, so Windows resolves it against whatever drive the pi process's cwd"
doc = " sits on — and that cwd is the per-session workspace pi-acp passes. Widening"
doc = " the gate from `is_absolute` to `has_root` would name a directory codeg"
doc = " cannot know AND shadow the history in `<agent_dir>\\sessions`."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::drive_relative_settings_session_dir_falls_back_to_the_default

attrs: doc = " pi expands a tilde only for a bare `~` and a `~/` prefix"
doc = " (`normalizePath`); `~other/path` is an ordinary relative path to pi, not"
doc = " the home of a user called `other`. Applied to both env overrides, which pi"
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::tilde_expansion_matches_pi_normalize_path

attrs: doc = " A settings file that is missing, unreadable as JSON, or carries no usable"
doc = " `sessionDir` must fall through to the default rather than to nothing."
tests.name: parsers::pi::tests::unusable_settings_json_falls_back_to_default

attrs: doc = " A title is capped by its parser BEFORE it reaches the decorator, and the"
doc = " cap has no idea where the frame starts. A short first prompt puts the cut"
doc = " inside the frame, leaving an opening separator and half a descriptor with"
doc = " no closing one — which the whole-frame strip pass will not touch."
tests.name: parsers::route_sanitizer_tests::a_title_truncated_mid_frame_leaks_no_route_metadata

attrs: doc = " The shape `append_agent_routes` ACTUALLY produces: the frame is its own"
doc = " prompt block, so every parser that keeps one block per recorded text item"
doc = " back two. Emptying the second in place used to leave a zero-height text"
doc = " part that the transcript's `space-y-4` stack still gave a full gap — the"
doc = " blank band under an `@`-mention bubble reopened from history."
tests.name: parsers::route_sanitizer_tests::a_frame_in_its_own_block_leaves_no_empty_block_behind

attrs: doc = " An agent that joins the prompt's text blocks with a BLANK line leaves the"
doc = " strip one newline to spare (it absorbs a single adjacent one), and"
doc = " `whitespace-pre-wrap` paints the survivor as an empty line under the"
doc = " message — same symptom, different transcript shape."
tests.name: parsers::route_sanitizer_tests::a_blank_line_before_the_frame_is_not_left_behind

attrs: doc = " Antigravity does not persist the prompt verbatim: its ACP server joins"
doc = " the text blocks with a space and replaces each separator with one, so the"
doc = " trajectory holds ONE block of prose with the frame trailing it and no"
doc = " separator anywhere. The whole frame used to render inside the user's"
doc = " bubble when such a session was reopened — and, sliced by the title cap,"
doc = " inside the sidebar title as well."
tests.name: parsers::route_sanitizer_tests::a_frame_an_agent_stored_without_separators_leaves_neither_prose_nor_title

attrs: doc = " The 100-char cap can land INSIDE the descriptor prefix rather than"
doc = " before it, for any first prompt whose prose length falls in a 37-wide"
doc = " band. A separator can never be halved that way, so this shape only"
doc = " exists for the agents that rewrite the separators away."
tests.name: parsers::route_sanitizer_tests::a_title_capped_halfway_through_the_marker_still_leaks_nothing

attrs: doc = " The cut is deliberately asymmetric, so pin both halves."
tests.name: parsers::route_sanitizer_tests::only_a_title_is_cut_at_a_dangling_separator

attrs: doc = " The shape `fs::canonicalize` hands back on Windows, and the one that"
doc = " broke image attachments in issue #392."
tests.name: paths::tests::simplifies_a_verbatim_drive_path

attrs: doc = " Everything without a rewritable prefix must come back byte-identical —"
doc = " this is what keeps the Linux/macOS/Docker upload response unchanged."
tests.name: paths::tests::leaves_every_other_shape_untouched

attrs: doc = " A spawn refused with `ETXTBSY` is retried until the writer lets go — the"
doc = " racing fork→exec window is self-closing, so the caller must see the"
doc = " eventual success, not the transient failure."
tests.name: process::tests::exec_busy_spawn_is_retried_until_the_file_is_free

attrs: doc = " Any other spawn failure returns on the first attempt: retrying a missing"
doc = " program would only delay the caller's own fallback (the terminal"
tests.name: process::tests::non_busy_spawn_failure_is_not_retried

attrs: doc = " A file held open by a long-lived writer gives up once the budget is"
doc = " spent and reports the original `ETXTBSY` — never swallowed, never"
tests.name: process::tests::persistently_busy_spawn_gives_up_with_the_original_error

attrs: doc = " `ETXTBSY` arriving as a bare errno, with no `ErrorKind` mapping, is still"
doc = " recognized — and a neighboring errno is not."
tests.name: process::tests::raw_etxtbsy_errno_is_recognized_as_exec_busy

attrs: doc = " The whole local-server path over a REAL pty: a real shell prints a real"
doc = " banner, the watch reads it out of the output stream, connects to the"
doc = " socket, and the frontend's event arrives naming the window that owns"
doc = " The pieces have unit tests of their own; what only an end-to-end run"
doc = " can show is that the watch is wired into the reader at all, and that a"
doc = " banner survives a real PTY (its line endings, its echo, its shell)."
tests.name: terminal::manager::tests::a_server_announced_in_a_terminal_reaches_the_frontend

attrs: doc = " `cmd` is matched by name on every platform so the ACP wrapper's cmd arm"
doc = " stays reachable from unix test runs."
tests.name: terminal::shell_flavor::tests::cmd_is_recognized_by_name_on_every_platform

attrs: doc = " The stderr shapes below are what git and the forges actually print. A"
doc = " push-back refused for being out of date used to come back advising the"
doc = " reader to turn on maintainer edits — a setting that, in the report that"
doc = " prompted this, was already on. So the two must never be confused."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_stale_push_back_is_not_read_as_a_permission_problem

attrs: doc = " Anything unrecognised must stay `Unknown`, because `Unknown` is what"
doc = " prints no advice — the whole point of the split."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::an_unrecognised_push_failure_gets_no_advice

attrs: doc = " A status code has to be matched in the phrasing that carries it. Branch"
doc = " and repository names are part of every push error, and plenty of them"
doc = " are named after an issue number."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_number_in_a_branch_name_is_not_a_status_code

attrs: doc = " The derived directory name is joined ONTO the configured root, so it"
doc = " has to stay relative even for the paths that have no final component"
doc = " to borrow: a filesystem root, and anything ending in `..`. An absolute"
doc = " name would replace the configured root instead of landing under it —"
doc = " silently putting the worktree somewhere the user never chose."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_project_without_a_name_still_lands_under_the_configured_root

attrs: doc = " Where a fresh task worktree lands. The default layout is load-bearing:"
doc = " every worktree already on disk was minted next to its project folder,"
doc = " so an unset (or blanked) setting has to keep producing exactly that"
doc = " path — the recreate-from-branch fallback looks for it by name."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_blank_worktree_root_keeps_worktrees_next_to_the_project

attrs: doc = " A configured directory holds the worktree DIRECTORY, not the checkout"
doc = " itself — two tasks of the same folder have to be able to share it."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_configured_root_holds_one_directory_per_task

attrs: doc = " The two shorthands a typed path is expected to honour: `~` is the home"
doc = " directory, and a relative path hangs off the project folder. An unknown"
doc = " home leaves `~` alone rather than guessing a different directory."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_typed_root_expands_home_and_resolves_relatives

attrs: doc = " Native Windows paths, where the naming and the join have to agree: a"
doc = " project folder whose \"name\" came back as the whole path (`C:\\src\\repo`)"
doc = " makes `<root>/<name>` an absolute join that REPLACES the configured"
doc = " root, so every setting would silently resolve back to the sibling"
doc = " layout. Nothing here is exotic — it is what the OS folder picker hands"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_windows_project_path_still_honours_the_configured_root

attrs: doc = " #649: the pump reads nothing but the conversation link to decide"
doc = " whether a launch continues or starts over, so a row that still points"
doc = " at an earlier run is dispatched as `Retry` no matter how it got back to"
doc = " the queue. `requeue_canceled` clears the link precisely so a task the"
doc = " user put back on the board comes through here as `Fresh`."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::launch_mode_follows_the_conversation_link

attrs: doc = " The sweep's row-level gate: exactly the tasks whose merge button the"
doc = " board would show — and whose light is green — land unattended."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::auto_merge_candidate_mirrors_the_board

attrs: doc = " The refusal wordings that mean \"lost a race\" are skipped silently by"
doc = " the sweep; the strings live in `merge_task`, and this pin keeps the"
doc = " match and the wording from drifting apart."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::benign_merge_races_are_recognized

attrs: doc = " The merge queue is first-asked-first-served, with the task id breaking a"
doc = " tie — the same rule `mergeQueueRanks` draws on the cards, so the \"第 2"
doc = " 位\" a user reads is the order they actually land in."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::the_merge_queue_drains_oldest_request_first

attrs: doc = " Each scenario reframes the SAME user text — that is the whole point of"
doc = " having scenarios, and `revise` must stay byte-identical to the wording"
doc = " the action had before they existed."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::follow_up_scenarios_reframe_the_same_feedback

attrs: doc = " The standing guard licenses committing, and it is the LAST block the"
doc = " agent reads — so a question turn has to replace it, not merely say"
doc = " \"don't edit\" a few blocks earlier."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_question_turn_withdraws_the_licence_to_commit

attrs: doc = " A report-deliverable task (forge plan-first / review-only)"
doc = " swaps the commit licence on its ORIGINAL order — otherwise the guard's"
doc = " \"commit as you like\", being the last block read, would quietly undo the"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_report_deliverable_order_swaps_the_commit_licence

attrs: doc = " A retry stands in for the turn it interrupted, and a retry/requeue note"
doc = " refines that turn without changing its KIND — so the guard's licence"
doc = " follows the unsettled follow-up underneath the note, not the note."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_retry_licence_follows_the_interrupted_turn_not_the_note

attrs: doc = " The one scenario that stands alone without user text."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_self_check_composes_without_any_user_text

attrs: doc = " A retry replays what the interrupted generation still owed — and an"
doc = " unanswered question must not come back as a work order."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_retry_replays_an_unanswered_question_as_a_question

attrs: doc = " The lookup is a barrier, not a filter: skipping past the newest"
doc = " instruction would resurrect an older one the agent already carried out."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_newer_instruction_hides_an_older_one

attrs: doc = " A completed turn consumes the instruction it carried, so it stops being"
doc = " re-injected into every generation for the rest of the task's life."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::settling_into_review_consumes_the_instruction

attrs: doc = " A task canceled before it ever had a session comes back through `Fresh`,"
doc = " so the note the user attached has to reach that arm too."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_restart_note_reaches_a_fresh_launch

attrs: doc = " A requeue drops the session link, so the run the user put back on the"
doc = " board comes through `Fresh` — in the SAME worktree, carrying whatever"
doc = " the stopped generation left there. The prompt has to say so: read as a"
doc = " first run it would have the agent redo work that is already committed on"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_requeued_run_says_its_worktree_is_not_empty

attrs: doc = " #649's requeue lands on `Fresh`, and a task can be sitting on a"
doc = " follow-up when the user stops it: review → \"rework this\" → cancel →"
doc = " requeue. The feedback is the whole point of that generation, so the"
doc = " arm that replaces it must replay it — dropping it sends the agent back"
doc = " to the original order in a worktree where that order is already done."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_requeued_run_replays_the_follow_up_it_interrupted

attrs: doc = " And the licence follows that same turn. A question the user asked before"
doc = " stopping the run is still a question after the requeue: the guard's"
doc = " \"commit as you like\" is the last thing the agent reads, so it has to be"
doc = " withdrawn here just as the retry arm withdraws it."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_requeued_question_keeps_its_read_only_licence

attrs: doc = " …and the note the user types INTO the requeue box must not bury it. The"
doc = " scan stops at the newest instruction, so a note takes the `outstanding`"
doc = " slot and only the returned turn's *intent* survives — fine for a resumed"
doc = " session, which still has the words, and useless for the session a"
doc = " requeue now starts, which would get a read-only licence for a question"
doc = " it was never shown, or \"take this note into account\" with no account."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_requeue_note_does_not_bury_the_turn_it_refines

attrs: doc = " The mirror image, and the reason the extra replay is gated on `resumed`:"
doc = " a session that really did resume already holds the returned turn, and"
doc = " replaying it a second time would re-ask a question the transcript above"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_resumed_retry_replays_only_the_newest_instruction

attrs: doc = " A screenshot pasted into the follow-up box has to reach the agent as an"
doc = " image block, right behind the sentence that framed it — dropping it"
doc = " would leave the framing pointing at nothing."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_follow_up_carries_its_attachments_after_the_framing

attrs: doc = " The same attachments have to survive the replay path: a run interrupted"
doc = " before it answered owes the user the screenshot as well as the sentence."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::an_outstanding_instruction_replays_its_attachments

attrs: doc = " A task's image blocks are stored, so the encoding the composer chose can"
doc = " be stale by the time the run happens (a slow probe then, a different"
doc = " agent now). Dispatch re-encodes for whoever actually answered."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::images_are_reencoded_for_the_agent_that_answered

attrs: doc = " An event written before follow-ups could carry attachments has no"
doc = " `blocks` field at all — that has to read as \"nothing was attached\"."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_legacy_instruction_without_blocks_still_replays

attrs: doc = " Two ways a busy task could hide its own instruction: `list_events`"
doc = " returns the OLDEST rows within its limit, and an agent's progress"
doc = " milestones are unbounded in number, so scanning raw events would bury"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_chatty_run_cannot_bury_the_latest_instruction

attrs: doc = " A follow-up recorded by `claim_for_run_with_action` must be readable the"
doc = " moment the claim commits — a pump can launch the generation right after."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_claim_carries_its_instruction_atomically

attrs: doc = " What the user typed in the merge dialog has to reach the agent — and has"
doc = " to land BEFORE the closing rules, which are what keep \"also do X\" from"
doc = " being read as licence to push or to delete the worktree."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::merge_prompt_carries_the_users_instructions_ahead_of_the_rules

attrs: doc = " …and an empty box adds nothing: no dangling header, no stray blank"
doc = " section between the numbered steps and the rules."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::merge_prompt_says_nothing_when_there_are_no_instructions

attrs: doc = " The worktree is off disk; everything below is what the clients see."
doc = " Without the `folder://changed` delete the removed worktree keeps"
doc = " rendering in every sidebar until the next full `fetchFolders`."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::worktree_removal_announces_the_dropped_folder

attrs: doc = " A retried cleanup finds the row already soft-deleted. It must still"
doc = " announce the drop — a client that missed the first broadcast is the"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::worktree_removal_re_announces_an_already_deleted_folder

attrs: doc = " The other half of the CAS: the status alone would let a stale"
doc = " connection's cancel land on the RUN AFTER it, which is `running` again"
doc = " and so passes the status gate. Only `run_seq` tells the two apart."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_previous_generation_cancelled_event_spares_the_current_run

attrs: doc = " The mirror image of the case above, and the half sparing the set opens:"
doc = " a retired run's DELEGATION children are namespaced by connection id, so"
doc = " keeping the task's set keeps THEIR keys too — with nothing left that"
doc = " could ever answer them, because the same retirement just unmapped the"
doc = " chain (`track_request` and `forget_delegation_child` both resolve a"
doc = " detached child to nothing). One orphan pins the set non-empty until a"
doc = " wholesale clear comes along — a later retirement that IS the last one"
doc = " out, or a cancel — and until then every generation's first request"
doc = " misses the `len() == 1` edge: the board says `running` for a run parked"
doc = " on the user, which is bug #447 all over again. Unlike the transient"
doc = " over-clear, answering the request is not what gets you out of it."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::retiring_a_run_takes_its_orphaned_delegation_requests_with_it

attrs: doc = " The happy path, end to end: the branch is pushed, a pull request is"
doc = " opened against the recorded base, and the task settles into `done` with"
doc = " the evidence of HOW it finished — plus the link, on the row the issue"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::delivery_opens_a_pull_request_and_settles_the_task

attrs: doc = " The delivery's own version of the offer both other acceptances make:"
doc = " take the checkout along. Safe here in a way a bare `branch -D` is not —"
doc = " by the time this runs the commits it destroys locally are on the forge."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_delivery_takes_the_worktree_along_when_asked

attrs: doc = " The worktree turned dirty between `deliver_pr`'s pre-flight clean check"
doc = " and the removal. `worktree remove --force` would drop those files"
doc = " without a word and they are on no forge, so the checkout is KEPT and"
doc = " flagged for a retry from the card — while the delivery itself, which is"
doc = " what the button promised, still reports success."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_worktree_that_turned_dirty_is_kept_rather_than_forced_away

attrs: doc = " The blind spot `git status` cannot cover: a COMMIT made in the same"
doc = " window leaves the worktree spotless while putting the branch ahead of"
doc = " everything the delivery published. `worktree remove --force` plus"
doc = " `branch -D` would take that commit with them, and it is on no forge —"
doc = " so the tip is checked against the OID that actually went out, and a"
doc = " branch that outran it keeps both its checkout and its commit."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_branch_that_outran_the_delivery_keeps_its_unpublished_commit

attrs: doc = " A pull request that already matches all four criteria is ADOPTED. This"
doc = " is what makes a retry after a settle-time failure safe: the second"
doc = " attempt must not open a second pull request for the same commit."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::an_existing_matching_pull_request_is_adopted_not_duplicated

attrs: doc = " A near-miss is never adopted: same commit, different base. Without the"
doc = " four-way match this would settle the task against the wrong pull"
doc = " request; with it, a new one is opened for the right base."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_pull_request_for_another_base_is_not_adopted

attrs: doc = " Every step after the review→merging CAS can fail, and every one of them"
doc = " has to leave the task in review with a readable reason — never stranded"
doc = " in `merging`, where only crash recovery could free it."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::any_failed_step_returns_the_task_to_review

attrs: doc = " A closed-without-merge match is a human decision. The engine neither"
doc = " reopens it nor opens a duplicate — it hands the task back with the"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_closed_pull_request_stops_the_delivery

attrs: doc = " Preconditions are checked BEFORE the CAS, so a refusal leaves the task"
doc = " untouched — same status, same run generation, and nothing pushed."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::refusals_happen_before_anything_moves

attrs: doc = " The gate lives in the engine, not the UI: this command is reachable by"
doc = " id from an old frontend or a direct web API call."
doc = " Two ways to be undeliverable, and neither may push anything: a task with"
doc = " no forge source has no repository to deliver to at all, and a"
doc = " pull-request task whose branch information is missing (a row written"
doc = " before that was recorded) must be re-triggered rather than pushed at a"
doc = " branch name we would have to guess."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_task_without_deliverable_provenance_is_refused

attrs: doc = " Crash recovery: the process died between the push and the settle. The"
doc = " forge is the only truth, and a full four-way match settles the task"
doc = " exactly as the live path would have."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::recovery_settles_a_delivery_whose_pull_request_matches

attrs: doc = " Everything short of a full match goes back to a human. Adopting a"
doc = " near-miss would settle the task against a pull request that merely"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::recovery_bounces_anything_it_cannot_prove

attrs: doc = " A delivery running in THIS process is not orphaned. Recovery has no"
doc = " live connection to check (a delivery has no agent session), so the"
doc = " in-flight set is the only thing standing between a slow push and the"
doc = " reconcile tick tearing it down."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::recovery_leaves_a_delivery_this_process_owns_alone

attrs: doc = " The pull request would be diffed against the base branch AS THE REMOTE"
doc = " HAS IT. A local base that is ahead means the review showed the task's"
doc = " own commit while the pull request would carry the unpushed ones too —"
doc = " refuse rather than publish work nobody looked at."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_local_base_ahead_of_the_remote_is_refused

attrs: doc = " A merge that cannot take in-flight ownership must not dispatch either."
doc = " The claim and the review→merging CAS are independent, so a claim-loser"
doc = " that carried on could win the CAS and then be left unowned when the"
doc = " claim-holder released the registry entry on its own way out."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_merge_that_cannot_claim_ownership_does_not_dispatch

attrs: doc = " Two clients clicking deliver at once. Only one may run the push, and —"
doc = " the part that bit us — the LOSER must not release the winner's"
doc = " ownership, or the reconcile sweep would bounce a live delivery."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_second_delivery_neither_runs_nor_steals_the_claim

attrs: doc = " A recovery pass that spent time at the forge must not undo a delivery"
doc = " that started while it was deciding — the bounce is bound to the"
doc = " generation the pass actually read."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::stale_recovery_cannot_bounce_a_newer_generation

attrs: doc = " One branch may have several open pull requests as long as each targets"
doc = " its own base — but only ONE per head/base pair. So a pull request for"
doc = " another base is no obstacle (create), while one for THIS base headed by"
doc = " a different commit is (bounce, rather than earn a 422 from GitHub)."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_stale_head_on_this_base_bounces_instead_of_duplicating

attrs: doc = " A delivery occupies the folder's `merging` slot, so a sibling task's"
doc = " unattended merge is refused while it runs. That refusal must stay a"
doc = " BENIGN race: `set_review_error` would latch auto-merge off for that card"
doc = " permanently, over a condition that clears itself in seconds."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_delivery_in_flight_does_not_latch_off_a_sibling_auto_merge

attrs: doc = " A task that came from a proposed change gets its comment on the CHANGE,"
doc = " not on an issue with the same number. GitHub serves both from one"
doc = " endpoint and would not notice; GitLab has two collections, where the"
doc = " wrong one lands on an unrelated issue or 404s."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_pull_request_tasks_comment_targets_the_pull_request

attrs: doc = " The comment is a fact sheet: the link and the counters. Nothing the"
doc = " agent wrote may reach a thread other people are reading."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_delivered_task_comments_the_link_and_the_numbers

attrs: doc = " A task whose trigger dialog left the box unchecked publishes nothing —"
doc = " this is the one thing a task does in a place other people watch."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_task_that_declined_the_comment_writes_nothing

attrs: doc = " A row minted before the choice lived on the task carries no answer at"
doc = " all. \"No recorded yes\" is a no: an upgrade must not start commenting on"
doc = " threads for tasks whose author was never asked."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_task_without_a_recorded_answer_writes_nothing

attrs: doc = " Best-effort means best-effort: a comment that cannot be posted is a"
doc = " timeline entry, not a status change. The task is finished either way."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_failed_write_back_leaves_the_finished_task_alone

attrs: doc = " The OTHER settlement path: a task that landed on the base branch"
doc = " locally. Its comment names the commit, not a pull request — and the"
doc = " write-back is spawned from inside the folder's git lock, which it must"
doc = " neither take nor be blocked by."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_locally_merged_task_comments_the_commit

attrs: doc = " The dead generation's index entry has no other way out — `reconcile_once`"
doc = " only scans `running` / `awaiting_input`, and the TurnComplete that would"
doc = " have retired it is the very thing that went missing. Recovery inherits"
doc = " that teardown, and must do it before it acts: this same pass honors the"
doc = " \"delete the worktree\" the user ticked, and worktree removal reads that"
doc = " same map as \"an agent is still working in there\"."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::recovery_retires_the_dead_merge_generations_connection

attrs: doc = " The other outcome, same teardown: a recovery that cannot prove the merge"
doc = " landed bounces the row to `review` — where a surviving entry would keep"
doc = " attributing the dead connection's late events to a task that has moved"
doc = " on, and would block the worktree cleanup offered right there on the card."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_bounced_recovery_retires_the_dead_connection_too

attrs: doc = " Retiring one generation must not disarm another. The outstanding-request"
doc = " set is keyed by task, so a stale pass that reaches a task someone else"
doc = " has already relaunched would otherwise drop the live generation's"
doc = " pending permissions — and the next resolution would empty a set that is"
doc = " already empty and put the card back to `running` while the agent is"
doc = " still parked on the request nobody answered."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::retiring_a_connection_spares_the_requests_of_one_still_on_the_task

attrs: doc = " `index` is a correlation table, not a liveness one. Whatever leaves an"
doc = " entry behind, the user's \"remove worktree\" must not be refused on behalf"
doc = " of a connection that is gone — the refusal sets a `failed` flag whose"
doc = " retry can never clear, because nothing would ever arrive to remove the"
doc = " entry. The manager is the truth, and what it says is gone is retired."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::worktree_removal_is_not_refused_by_a_dead_connection

attrs: doc = " Git for Windows can finish the destructive part of `worktree remove`"
doc = " (registration and checkout contents) but fail to remove the now-empty"
doc = " directory. That first pass leaves the task flagged for cleanup; its retry"
doc = " must recognize the harmless shell, finish the branch/DB cleanup, and not"
doc = " report files that do not exist."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::worktree_cleanup_retry_converges_an_empty_detached_shell

attrs: doc = " A missing `.git` file alone is not proof that the directory is a harmless"
doc = " post-removal shell. Files may have appeared after the partial teardown,"
doc = " and none of them is recoverable through git, so the retry must preserve"
doc = " both the sentinel and the branch."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::worktree_cleanup_retry_preserves_a_file_in_a_detached_shell

attrs: doc = " THE probe behind issue #642's dead-end retry, exercised where the bug"
doc = " actually happens. `has_changes` runs `git status` from the path itself,"
doc = " so a shell in the default layout — beside the project, no repository"
doc = " above it — makes git error, and reading that error as \"dirty\" is what"
doc = " made the retry offer the same refusal forever. An empty shell has, by"
doc = " definition, nothing a `--force` removal could take."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::an_empty_shell_beside_a_project_reads_as_clean

attrs: doc = " The other half of the same answer: outside a repository git errors on a"
doc = " shell whatever is in it, so emptiness is the ONLY thing separating a"
doc = " harmless leftover from files nothing can give back."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_file_in_a_shell_beside_a_project_still_reads_as_dirty

attrs: doc = " A worktree root configured INSIDE the project (a relative"
doc = " `worktree_root`, which the setting takes at face value) puts the shell"
doc = " under the project's own `.git`. `git status` then answers happily — about"
doc = " the PROJECT — so a project with a stray file of its own would answer"
doc = " \"dirty\" for a shell holding nothing, and #642's retry would still never"
doc = " converge. Without a `.git` marker the path is not a checkout git speaks"
doc = " for, and its answer must not be read as this path's."
doc = " The project's dirt is an edit to a TRACKED file, not a stray untracked"
doc = " one: `has_changes` spawns git through `crate::process`, which inherits"
doc = " the real environment, so an untracked fixture is only as visible as the"
doc = " developer's global `core.excludesFile` lets it be — and a fixture git"
doc = " silently ignores would make this test pass against the very bug it"
doc = " exists to pin. No ignore rule can hide a modified tracked file."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::an_empty_shell_inside_a_dirty_project_reads_as_clean

attrs: doc = " And the marker check must not short-circuit the case it is guarding: a"
doc = " checkout that still HAS its `.git` is exactly what `git status` is for,"
doc = " uncommitted work included. Tracked and modified for the reason above —"
doc = " an untracked fixture would read as clean under a global ignore rule that"
doc = " happens to match it, and fail this assertion on that developer's machine"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::an_intact_worktree_is_still_measured_by_git

attrs: doc = " The removal underneath is `worktree remove --force`, and a stop pressed"
doc = " while the agent is editing is exactly when a checkout is dirty. Nothing"
doc = " the user clicked named those files — the cancel dialog's checkbox offers"
doc = " \"its worktree and work branch\" — so this has to refuse, the same line"
doc = " `complete_task` draws and the branch dropdown re-asks about."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::worktree_removal_refuses_to_take_uncommitted_work

attrs: doc = " The probe fails CLOSED. `git status` can stop answering for reasons that"
doc = " have nothing to do with the checkout being gone — a corrupt index, a"
doc = " permission error — and the operation waiting on that answer is"
doc = " `worktree remove --force`. Reading \"could not ask\" as \"clean\" would"
doc = " trade a recoverable stall for unrecoverable files."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_worktree_git_cannot_read_is_not_assumed_clean

attrs: doc = " The removal has to serialize against a LAUNCH, and the folder git lock"
doc = " cannot do that: `launch` holds the TASK lock across its whole setup —"
doc = " `ensure_worktree` included — and takes no folder lock at all."
doc = " The sequence that gets there is ordinary board use: a cancel that was"
doc = " asked to take the worktree along leaves the row `canceled`, the user"
doc = " requeues it (a pure DB write that waits on no lock), and the pump"
doc = " launches it — all while the removal sits between its status read and its"
doc = " `git worktree remove`. Nothing about the requeue is wrong; the fresh run"
doc = " would mint its own checkout. Deleting the directory out from under"
doc = " Holding the task lock here stands in for that launch: without the lock"
doc = " on the removal's side, the worktree is gone before the guard is dropped."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::worktree_removal_waits_for_the_task_lock

attrs: doc = " An acceptance that removes the worktree has to say so on the TASK"
doc = " channel, not just the folder one. Both acceptance paths broadcast the"
doc = " row BEFORE the cleanup runs (`settle_merge_generation` and this one), so"
doc = " a removal that stays silent leaves every open board holding the snapshot"
doc = " taken while the worktree still existed: the card flips to `done` but its"
doc = " \"worktree removed\" badge — keyed on `worktree_folder_id` going null —"
doc = " never appears until someone refetches the whole table."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::removing_the_worktree_announces_the_task_after_the_folder

attrs: doc = " A task nobody triggered from a forge has no thread to comment on — the"
doc = " write-back must never invent one from the folder's remote."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_task_without_a_forge_source_is_never_commented

attrs: doc = " The engine has to be listening to the event bus BEFORE it starts its"
doc = " boot work, not after: the bus drops what it broadcasts while nobody is"
doc = " subscribed, so a task the user starts during boot would emit its"
doc = " `TurnComplete` into nothing and sit `running` forever — the reconcile"
doc = " sweep deliberately leaves rows whose connection is still live to"
doc = " Pinned without timing games. A `merging` row parks the boot pass on the"
doc = " folder's git lock, which this test holds, so the engine is provably"
doc = " still inside boot work when the event goes out; and the queued row"
doc = " flipping to `failed` is the boot pass announcing it got that far."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::boot_work_does_not_swallow_the_events_published_under_it

attrs: doc = " Nothing makes an agent commit before its task lands in review — the"
doc = " merge generation's prompt starts by committing whatever is left over —"
doc = " so a task whose new files are still untracked has done work all the"
doc = " same. Reading it as \"changed nothing\" would put \"complete\" on the card"
doc = " and let the user close a task whose work never lands."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::work_the_agent_never_committed_still_counts

attrs: doc = " Base content the branch ABSORBED is not this task's work. An agent that"
doc = " merges the base branch in — or rebases onto it — brings every commit the"
doc = " base gained along, and measuring from the commit the task branched off"
doc = " would count all of it: a task that added one line would report the whole"
doc = " week's work, and the counters decide which acceptance the board offers."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::base_content_the_branch_absorbed_is_not_the_tasks_work

attrs: doc = " The task says which branch it is for, and that is where it starts and"
doc = " what it lands back onto — whatever the project folder happens to be"
doc = " checked out on when the task is claimed."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_task_starts_on_the_base_branch_it_was_created_for

attrs: doc = " No choice recorded — every task created before this existed, and every"
doc = " task of a user who does not care — keeps branching from the project"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_task_without_a_chosen_branch_still_follows_the_checkout

attrs: doc = " A branch that is gone by the time the task is claimed must not quietly"
doc = " fall back to the checkout: the whole point of the choice is that the"
doc = " work lands somewhere specific, and starting from `main` instead would"
doc = " be a wrong answer delivered silently."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_chosen_branch_that_disappeared_refuses_instead_of_falling_back

attrs: doc = " A pull-request task starts ON the pull request, and its review diff is"
doc = " measured from the MERGE BASE — so the pull request's own changes are"
doc = " part of what gets reviewed, and the base branch's unrelated progress is"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_pull_request_task_checks_out_the_pull_request_head

attrs: doc = " The counters on the row are the TASK's own work, which on a"
doc = " pull-request task is NOT the review diff: the worktree starts on the"
doc = " pull request, so the whole contribution is already there before the"
doc = " agent does anything. A review-only run — findings reported, nothing"
doc = " committed — has to settle at zero, or the board hides \"complete\" behind"
doc = " a delivery that would push an empty change."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_pull_request_task_counts_only_what_the_agent_added

attrs: doc = " The same rule on the path that made it matter: a pull-request task whose"
doc = " agent wrote a file and never added it. The counters have to say the task"
doc = " did something, the drawer has to list the same file the counters count,"
doc = " and completing has to refuse — closing it here would leave work that"
doc = " nothing is going to land (delivery cannot push an uncommitted tree"
doc = " either; it says so and asks for another round). The ignore rules are"
doc = " pinned where they are applied, in"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::an_untracked_file_keeps_a_pull_request_task_out_of_complete

attrs: doc = " The counters are written once, when the run settles, and every board"
doc = " decision reads them afterwards — so a row can outlive what it describes"
doc = " (a worktree committed to since, or a pull-request task settled by a"
doc = " build that credited it with the pull request's own files). The boot pass"
doc = " re-measures whatever is still sitting in review."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::the_boot_pass_re_measures_a_review_row

attrs: doc = " The same setup against GitLab. Everything downstream — the merge-base"
doc = " baseline, the pinned OID, the review diff — is shared code; what is NOT"
doc = " shared is the ref the head is published under, and fetching GitHub's"
doc = " spelling from a GitLab server finds nothing at all."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_merge_request_task_checks_out_the_gitlab_head_ref

attrs: doc = " A pull request force-pushed since the task was created no longer has"
doc = " the commit the user triggered on. Checking out the NEW head would run"
doc = " the task against code nobody chose, so setup fails and says so."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_force_pushed_pull_request_refuses_instead_of_switching_commits

attrs: doc = " The window between \"we checked\" and \"we pushed\" is real, and what the"
doc = " pull request looks like AFTER the push is what the card will claim. A"
doc = " review that was closed, or retargeted at another base, is not a"
doc = " delivery — the task says so instead of recording `done`."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_push_back_does_not_settle_against_a_review_that_moved

attrs: doc = " Merged in that same window is the opposite answer — but ONLY when what"
doc = " merged is what we pushed. The losing order is real: someone merges the"
doc = " old head, we push on top, and the reread says \"merged\" about a merge"
doc = " our commits are not in."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_push_back_settles_on_a_merge_only_when_it_contains_our_commit

attrs: doc = " The delivery of a pull-request task is a push back onto that pull"
doc = " request's OWN branch. Nothing is created — the review the user is"
doc = " already looking at is where the work belongs."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_pull_request_task_is_pushed_back_to_its_own_branch

attrs: doc = " A pull request from a FORK pushes back to the fork — that is where its"
doc = " branch lives, and where its author and reviewers are looking. The"
doc = " repository in the push is the fork's; every API call stays on the"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_fork_pull_request_task_pushes_back_to_the_fork

attrs: doc = " A push back with nothing new is REFUSED, and the acceptance that fits"
doc = " takes over. The task's branch is the pull request's own head — a review"
doc = " turn that committed nothing — so a delivery would push nothing, leave"
doc = " the pull request exactly as it was, and still record the task as"
doc = " delivered to it. The board offers \"complete\" for this row (nothing of"
doc = " its own to land); the backend has to agree, or the two disagree about"
doc = " The review-only task on a fork this account cannot write to is still"
doc = " accepted — completing needs no write access at all, and the fake here"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_push_back_with_nothing_new_is_refused_for_completing

attrs: doc = " The OTHER way a delivery finds nothing to push: its push already landed"
doc = " and something interrupted the settle. The retry must recognize the pull"
doc = " request as carrying this task's commit and finish — without pushing"
doc = " again, which is what lets it complete on a fork this account cannot"
doc = " write to (the fake here fails any push). Distinguished from the refused"
doc = " case above by the task actually having work: it was triggered on the"
doc = " pull request's earlier head and committed on top of it."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_delivery_whose_push_already_landed_settles_without_pushing_again

attrs: doc = " A row recorded before the head repository was part of the meta (builds"
doc = " that refused forks at trigger, so same-repo by construction) pushes"
doc = " where it always did: the source repository."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_push_back_without_a_recorded_head_repo_pushes_to_the_source_repo

attrs: doc = " Everything that would make the push land somewhere it does not belong"
doc = " is refused BEFORE the push, with the task untouched in review."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_push_back_refuses_before_it_pushes_anywhere_wrong

attrs: doc = " Landing a pull request's work on the local base would take its changes"
doc = " in behind the author's back and leave the review open. The refusal is"
doc = " in the engine, where an old frontend or a direct API call still hits it."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_pull_request_task_is_never_merged_locally

attrs: doc = " The merge dispatch runs its launch off-thread so the click is not held"
doc = " for the run (a resumed session may compact first — an unbounded turn)."
doc = " What must NOT change with it: a launch that never gets an agent up still"
doc = " reports its reason to the caller, and leaves the row settled and unowned"
doc = " by the time it does. Anything less and the dialog would close on a merge"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_merge_whose_launch_never_goes_live_still_reports_and_settles

attrs: doc = " Fire-once, from either side. The launch reports itself live; the task"
doc = " driving it reports every way of failing before that point. A second"
doc = " report — a launch that fails AFTER going live — must not overwrite the"
doc = " first, or a dispatch the user was told succeeded would come back as an"
doc = " error into a dialog that has already closed."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::the_dispatch_signal_reports_exactly_once

attrs: doc = " Recovery of an interrupted push-back settles on ONE piece of evidence:"
doc = " the pull request's head IS the commit this delivery was pushing."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::recovery_settles_a_push_back_only_on_the_commit_it_pushed

attrs: doc = " Merge states written before deliveries existed carry no `op`. They are"
doc = " all lands, and reading one as a delivery would send crash recovery to"
doc = " the forge for a task that never had one."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::merge_state_without_an_op_decodes_as_a_land

attrs: doc = " The feature's whole point: a nearly full session is compacted, and the"
doc = " round's own prompt only goes out after that turn has landed."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_full_context_is_compacted_before_the_round_prompt

attrs: doc = " A compaction the agent REFUSED is a failure, not an \"ok\" with a"
doc = " footnote. `rejected` reaches the `TurnComplete` arm at all only because"
doc = " a prompt rejection stopped tearing the connection down (issue #797); it"
doc = " used to arrive as the terminal `Error` the waiter settles as `failed`,"
doc = " and the catch-all below it would otherwise have promoted a compaction"
doc = " that never ran to a successful one."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_rejected_compaction_prompt_is_recorded_as_a_failure

attrs: doc = " Below the threshold nothing is sent and nothing is written — the"
doc = " ordinary case has to stay free of both an extra turn and timeline noise."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_session_below_the_threshold_is_left_alone

attrs: doc = " The off switch. A full context with the setting at 0 is exactly today's"
doc = " behaviour — no reading, no turn, no event."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_zero_threshold_disables_the_check

attrs: doc = " The explicit setting is what gets sent, verbatim — it exists precisely"
doc = " for the agents codeg has no default for."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::the_configured_command_is_sent_verbatim

attrs: doc = " A session that reports no occupancy can't be measured against a"
doc = " threshold. It must not be compacted on a guess — and the skip is"
doc = " recorded, because with the setting switched on \"nothing happened\" needs"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::an_unmeasurable_session_is_not_compacted_but_is_recorded

attrs: doc = " A cancel that lands while the compaction turn is in flight ends the"
doc = " wait through the same `TurnComplete{cancelled}` the manager emits — the"
doc = " launch must not sit on it, and the round is recorded as canceled rather"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_canceled_compaction_turn_releases_the_launch

attrs: doc = " The race the `compaction_turns` marker exists for. The bus is a"
doc = " broadcast: the launch's waiter reacts to the compaction's `TurnComplete`"
doc = " at once, but the engine's own receiver awaits DB work per event and can"
doc = " dequeue that same envelope only after the launch has indexed the"
doc = " connection and sent the round's real prompt. Handled naively, the"
doc = " compaction's completion would settle the round it preceded — and"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_late_compaction_completion_does_not_settle_the_round

attrs: doc = " The fence covers everything up to its watermark — the wait can end"
doc = " without ever reading the completion, and must still be able to fence one"
doc = " it never saw — but nothing above it. A higher seq can only be the round's"
doc = " own turn, so it passes AND retires the fence."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::the_compaction_fence_stops_at_the_rounds_own_turn

attrs: doc = " Ending the wait on liveness rather than on the event itself is exactly"
doc = " when the completion is most likely to still be sitting in the engine's"
doc = " receiver: `apply_event` clears `turn_in_flight` BEFORE the envelope is"
doc = " broadcast. The probe has to fence it on the way out, or the fix for the"
doc = " settle race has a hole the size of the tick."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::ending_the_wait_on_liveness_still_fences_the_completion

attrs: doc = " The fence must not outlive the launch that set it. A generation torn"
doc = " down before it ever went live (lost CAS, failed prompt, cancel) is"
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_torn_down_launch_takes_its_fence_with_it

attrs: doc = " `apply_event` clears `turn_in_flight` on `TurnComplete` but not on a"
doc = " terminal error or a disconnect — so a receiver that lagged one of those"
doc = " away would block on `recv()` for a connection that is never going to"
doc = " speak again, holding the task lock and taking any later cancel with it."
doc = " The liveness tick is what ends those waits."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_wait_with_no_events_still_ends_on_liveness

attrs: doc = " The kill slot is generation-scoped like every other one on this engine:"
doc = " a cancel of an older run must not abort the compaction of a newer one."
tests.name: work_task::engine::tests::a_stale_cancel_does_not_abort_a_newer_compaction

attrs: doc = " Why removing a task worktree has to consult BOTH probes: each is blind"
doc = " to exactly what the other sees. `remove_worktree_and_branch` runs"
doc = " `worktree remove --force` + `branch -D`, so anything either probe would"
doc = " have found is destroyed silently if only one of them is asked."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::status_and_base_diff_have_opposite_blind_spots

attrs: doc = " The measure every acceptance decision runs on has to see work the agent"
doc = " never committed — a task is not required to commit before it lands in"
doc = " review, and the merge generation's own prompt starts by committing"
doc = " whatever is left over. Uncommitted edits to tracked files were always"
doc = " visible; a brand-new file nobody added is the case a plain diff misses,"
doc = " and reporting that task as \"changed nothing\" is what puts the wrong"
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::the_acceptance_measure_sees_work_that_was_never_committed

attrs: doc = " A file the ignore rules exclude but that is TRACKED anyway (`git add"
doc = " -f`, then committed) is the task's work like any other. Only the index"
doc = " knows it: an index rebuilt from the anchor would not carry it, and"
doc = " `add -A -N` will not put it back — the ignore rules see to that — so it"
doc = " would drop out of the measure entirely, and the plain diff that DOES"
doc = " see it would be the more accurate one. Completing the task would then"
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::a_tracked_file_the_ignore_rules_exclude_stays_in_the_measure

attrs: doc = " A SPARSE checkout has tracked files with no file on disk, and they must"
doc = " not read as deletions: that would report a task that changed nothing as"
doc = " having removed everything outside the cone. What keeps them out is the"
doc = " scratch index being a COPY of the worktree's own (skip-worktree flags"
doc = " and all) rather than a tree read back from the anchor."
doc = " `read-tree -mu`, which is how sparse checkouts worked long before the"
doc = " `git sparse-checkout` command existed — the test should not depend on"
doc = " the git version the developer happens to run."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::a_sparse_checkout_reports_no_phantom_deletions

attrs: doc = " The branch guard behind converging a missing worktree: unlanded commits"
doc = " keep the branch, and both landed shapes (merge ancestry, squash tree"
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::unlanded_branch_work_is_recognized_in_the_root_repo

attrs: doc = " A same-name TAG must never answer for the branch: unqualified"
doc = " resolution prefers tags, and both halves of the missing-worktree story"
doc = " would go wrong on it — the deletion guard would read the tag's landed"
doc = " commit and clear real work for `branch -D`, and the recovery add would"
doc = " produce a detached checkout of the tag."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::a_same_name_tag_cannot_shadow_the_branch

attrs: doc = " Probe failures keep the branch: an unreadable repo must not read as"
doc = " \"nothing to lose\" on the path that ends in `branch -D`."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::a_broken_probe_keeps_the_branch

attrs: doc = " Task worktrees can be pointed at a directory of the user's choosing"
doc = " (the folder's `worktree_root` setting), and the folder's FIRST task"
doc = " meets that directory before it exists. Nothing in the engine creates"
doc = " it: `git worktree add` is expected to make the leading directories"
doc = " along with the checkout, so this pins that expectation on the exact"
doc = " call the fresh mint makes."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::a_worktree_root_that_does_not_exist_yet_is_created_by_the_add

attrs: doc = " Both answers of the compare-and-delete, on one repository."
doc = " A caller that passes `expected_tip` has PROVED where the work went —"
doc = " a delivery knows the exact OID it pushed — and the branch is expendable"
doc = " for exactly as long as it still points there. Checking that separately"
doc = " and then running `branch -D` leaves a window; this is the pair fused"
doc = " into one git operation, so a branch that moved keeps its commit and"
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::a_branch_is_deleted_only_while_it_still_holds_the_expected_tip

attrs: doc = " The engine normally catches contents before calling this layer, but a"
doc = " file can appear after git has removed the checkout marker and before the"
doc = " task retries. Git is not the risk here — it validates the `.git` marker"
doc = " and refuses the removal outright, contents untouched. The risk is the"
doc = " marker-less path this function grew FOR empty shells, which is the only"
doc = " code that will delete such a directory at all: it must stay"
doc = " non-recursive, so that a file makes it fail closed and keep the branch."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::registered_worktree_without_git_marker_never_takes_a_sentinel

attrs: doc = " The predicate the refusal is built on, asked of whichever platform is"
doc = " running rather than of the one that happened to write the test."
doc = " `C:repo` is the whole reason it exists, and it is the case that cannot"
doc = " be stated platform-blind: Windows reads a drive prefix there and has to"
doc = " refuse it, while a platform without path prefixes reads the same bytes"
doc = " as an ordinary filename and must not. Everything else names a single"
doc = " directory on BOTH — a rooted drive, a UNC share, a verbatim path, and"
doc = " every Unix shape a folder row actually holds — so a refusal there would"
doc = " break cleanup for real users."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::only_a_drive_relative_path_is_refused

attrs: doc = " Git looks a `<worktree>` argument up by unique path SUFFIX before it"
doc = " resolves it as a path, so a RELATIVE name is not scoped to the"
doc = " repository it is handed to — it reaches a registered checkout anywhere"
doc = " on disk, and `--force` deletes that one, uncommitted files included."
doc = " Folder paths are stored exactly as they were given, so the argument is"
doc = " only as absolute as whoever created the folder made it. This is the one"
doc = " call in this file that can destroy a checkout, so it resolves the path"
doc = " itself rather than trusting git to scope it."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::a_relative_path_cannot_reach_a_worktree_somewhere_else

attrs: doc = " The other side of that choice: a worktree git still speaks for is git's"
doc = " to refuse, and its refusal must not be overwritten by ours. The"
doc = " `remove_dir` recovery still runs here and still fails — a live checkout"
doc = " is not empty — so this pins that failing SECOND does not make it the"
doc = " story. A lock is the cleanest way to make git decline a healthy"
doc = " checkout, and it is exactly the case where git's own text carries"
doc = " something no filesystem error could (\"use 'remove -f -f' to override\")."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::a_locked_worktree_keeps_gits_own_refusal

attrs: doc = " A retry after the checkout was removed must get the SAME branch back,"
doc = " prior commits included — not a fresh tree on a fresh base."
tests.name: work_task::git::tests::a_vanished_checkout_is_recreated_from_its_branch
